chapters.title: Chapter 151 | Renovations
paragraphs: After the massage was over, Dexter carried Mira to the bathroom, washed the massage oil from her skin, dried her, dressed her in a fresh set of clothes, and wheeled her back to the living room.
What was strange was that Mira refused to speak to him throughout and he had no idea what he had done wrong.
And the whole time. She refused to look at him. Also, her face was still flushed in a deep shade of red. From her neck and even the tip of her ears.
Dexter stood behind her wheelchair, utterly bewildered.
’Did I press too hard? Did I hurt her? Is she having an allergic reaction to the oil?’
He leaned down slightly, trying to catch her gaze. "Mira, are you—"
"Don’t."
Dexter had no choice but to straighten back up.
He stared at the back of her head. The flush on her neck hadn’t faded at all. If anything, it seemed to have deepened since he’d moved her out of the bedroom.
’She must be running a fever.’
’I should probably make something to help with the fever.’
Dexter turned and walked quickly to the kitchen, his mind already racing through recipes.

As a Great Grandmaster Foodsmith, he possessed an encyclopedic knowledge of medicinal ingredients and their effects on the human body. He knew exactly which herbs reduced inflammation, which roots lowered body temperature, and which combinations could reduce fever.
He reached into his spatial storage and began pulling out ingredients.
Dried spirit ginger root, firethorn peppercorns, a thin slice of Millennium Blood Ginseng and a cut of Fiend-Class beast meat.
The meat was rich in dense, restorative properties and possessed a deep, savory flavor that would serve as the perfect backbone for a hearty pepper soup.
He set the Type-II Spirit Cooking Pot on the stove and ignited his Abyssal Flame and within minutes, the kitchen was filled with the sharp, mouth-watering aroma of peppercorns and seared meat.
Twenty minutes later, the soup was done.
He ladled it into a deep ceramic bowl. The broth was a rich, dark amber, flecked with floating peppercorn oil and thin shreds of tender meat. Steam rose into the air as the scent rose with it.
[Name: Pepper Soup]
[Grade: Grade 3]
Not as powerful as the Celestial Origin Star Rice from this morning, but still a genuine Grade Three Arcane Meal
Dexter carried the bowl to the living room.
"Mira," he said gently, kneeling beside her and holding the bowl at her eye level. "I made you pepper soup. I think you might be running a fever, so I added some medicinal herbs. It should help."
Mira finally turned her head.
Her crimson eyes fell on the steaming bowl then her gaze shifted from the soup to Dexter’s face, then back to the soup, then back to his face.
Then she saw he was actually sincere and wasn’t teasing. Which meant he had no idea what he did with the gloves.
Mira blinked her eyes and she almost smiled.
Then, one of her Spectral Arms materialized beside her shoulder.
The translucent mana limb reached forward, wrapped its glowing fingers carefully around the bowl, and lifted it from Dexter’s hands with surprising steadiness.
Dexter was quite impressed by her control. It seemed like she had been training in a secret and is very proficient in it.
The arm carried the bowl to her lips and she tilted her head slightly, taking in a slow sip.
Her eyes widened slightly at the incredible taste. She closed them and then drank in silence, easing the strange, tight feeling that had been coiling inside her body since the massage.
’She looks quite cute when she’s silent...’
’Things might be more peaceful if Mira was the one who couldn’t speak.’
But he shook his head at the random thought.
’But on a serious note, it’s high time I gave them the pill that heals 20 percent of their illnesses.’
Dexter watched her for a moment, satisfied, then stood and walked back toward the kitchen.
He had barely taken three steps when he saw Lyra looking at him with a pitiful expression.
She had just finished her snacks and had been cultivating on the sofa when Dexter walked by with the soup, distracting her.
She looked exactly like a puppy that had been locked outside while its owner ate dinner.
"Alright, alright. I also made some for you."
Dexter shook his eyes as he chuckled then walked back to the kitchen and ladled a second portion into a fresh bowl, the. held it out to her.
Lyra’s pout vanished instantly as her dark eyes lit up like two black holes. She took the bowl and cradled it against her chest like a precious treasure.
’Thanks, Dexter!’
She immediately brought the bowl directly to her lips and took a sip.
A small, barely audible content sound escaped her throat.
Dexter smiled and ladled a third portion.
He carried it down the hallway to the bedroom. Selene was sitting cross-legged on the bed, deep in cultivation.
Her silver-white hair floated weightlessly around her shoulders, stirred by the invisible currents of mana flowing into her body.
Dexter sat on the edge of the bed beside her. "Selene."
Her cultivation paused. Her head turned toward him.
"I made pepper soup. Drink it while it’s still hot — it’s better that way."
He placed the warm bowl carefully into her hands, guiding her fingers to the sides so she could feel the heat and grip it securely.
Selene tilted her head slightly. A small, quiet smile touched her pale lips. "Thank you."
She raised the bowl to her mouth and drank.
Dexter left her to it and returned to his renovation work.
The interior of the house was finished, only the exterior remained. He decided to tackle the roof first.
But there was just one problem, the ladder he bought wasn’t tall enough.
He could actually, jump up. With his current Superhuman-level strength, four meters was nothing.
But the house was old. If he landed too hard, he risked cracking the tiles or create even bigger hole which would create an even larger, more expensive problem than the leak he was trying to fix.
’I hope Tessa’s dad has one.’

chapters.title: Chapter 152 | Suprise
paragraphs: The interior of the house was finished, only the exterior remained. He decided to tackle the roof first.
But there was just one problem, the ladder he bought wasn’t tall enough.
He could actually, jump up. With his current Superhuman-level strength, four meters was nothing.
But the house was old. If he landed too hard, he risked cracking the tiles or create even bigger hole which would create an even larger, more expensive problem than the leak he was trying to fix.
’I hope Tessa’s dad has one.’
Dexter wiped his hands on his jeans, walked out the front gate, and turned left toward Tessa’s house.
He reached the wooden fence and knocked three times, and waited.
A moment later, the door opened.
Tessa’s father stood in the doorway.
"Good afternoon sir. I was wondering, do you happen to have a ladder I could borrow? Mine isn’t tall enough to reach the roof."
The man blinked, then nodded. "Sure. Wait here a moment."
He disappeared back inside the house. While Dexter waited, he glanced up at the second-floor window.
Tessa was there.
She was leaning against the window with her chin propped on both hands, her messy red hair falling around her face like a curtain as she waved enthusiastically at him.
Dexter shook his head and waved back.
A minute later, Tessa’s father reappeared through the front door, carrying a heavy wooden extension ladder.
"There you go. Bring it back whenever you’re done."
"Thank you, sir. I appreciate it." Dexter reached for the ladder, then paused.
"Actually, there’s something else I wanted to discuss with you." He paused.
"Tessa mentioned the idea of forming a business partnership — that I would provide Enchanted Meals, and you would sell them at your bakery."
"I wanted to make sure that was also your idea, And she’s not just jesting. Moreover I needed to hear it from you personally."
Tessa’s father was quiet for a while, then he slowly nodded.
"She told me about it. And I think it’s a good idea."

He unfolded his arms and leaned against the doorframe. "You’re a Foodsmith. That’s not something you see every day in this neighborhood. Having Arcane Meals available at our bakery would boost our sales considerably."
Dexter smiled.
’Seems like the little girl is reliable after all.’
"Thank you, sir."
The man waved a hand dismissively. "Just make good food. That’s all I ask."
Dexter nodded, hoisted the ladder onto his own shoulder and carried it back to his house.
He set the ladder against the rear wall, climbed up and reached the leak.

He carefully removed the damaged tile, cleaned the area, applied a layer of sealant, and fitted a replacement tile into place, pressing it down firmly, then he inspected the surrounding tiles for any additional cracks.
There were two more minor cracks and he worked on them both.

He spent another fifteen minutes on the roof, checking the flashing around the chimney pipe and clearing debris from the gutters before climbing back down satisfied that the roof would hold through the next storm.
He moved the ladder to the front of the house and began painting the porch.
The old wooden railing had been peeling. He sanded it down, applied a fresh coat of brown paint, and moved on to the porch columns.
He was halfway through the second column when he heard footsteps behind him.
He turned around.
Lyra and Selene were standing at the edge of the porch.
Selene was holding a cold bottle of soda in her hand as she looked in his general direction.
Lyra stood beside her, holding a clean white towel.
Dexter stared at the two girls in front of him, then blinked in surprise.
He looked at Selene. "Do you need me to open it for you?"
Selene shook her head slowly.
Dexter’s brow furrowed. ’Then why is she holding it?’
Then Selene spoke in an almost shy voice.
"For you."
Dexter froze.
He stared at the cold can of soda in her hands. Then at her face. Then back at the bottle.
"For... me?"
Selene nodded. Her fingers tightened slightly around the can nervously and there was a faint hint of color on her pale cheeks.
Dexter stood there and stared at the blind girl holding the drink, he was stunned.
Behind Selene, Lyra held out the folded towel with both hands, her dark eyes watching him through her glasses earnestly.
Dexter looked at the towel. Then at the soda. Then at Selene’s face.
Something warm bloomed in Dexter’s chest, spreading slowly through his ribs like warm tea on a cold morning.
He set the paint roller down, wiped his hands on his jeans, and reached out to take the soda from Selene’s hands and at that moment, their fingers and Dexter felt her could skin. seems

Selene didn’t flinch this time nor did she pull away allowing the warmth of his finger to cub the frost in her. Her fingers lingered against his for just a fraction of a second before she reluctantly pulled away.
"Thank you," Dexter said quietly. "Both of you. Thank you.
He took the towel from Lyra with his other hand and she looked up at him, a small smile on her face.
The two nodded their head and walked back inside.
Dexter stood alone on the porch, unmoving.
Then he exhaled slowly, walked to the porch steps, and sat down. He wiped the sweat off his face with the towel and draped it over one knee, cracked open the soda bottle, and brought it to his lips.
’Pfft.’
The can hissed as cold, fizzy liquid rushed down his throat. He closed his eyes and let out a low, satisfied sound.
"Ah... that’s the spot."
He took another long sip and stared out at the neighborhood.
The sun was beginning to set.
The sky had turned a deep, molten orange as the ray of light spilled across the rooftops and fences of the street.
"Woof! Woof! Meow!"
He could hear several animal noises somewhere in the street.
Dexter leaned back slightly.
’This is nice.’
It would have been a perfect life.
Sitting on a porch, cold drink in hand. Sunset painting the sky. Three women waiting for him inside his own house.
It looked like the kind of life any man would kill to have, just like a dream.
From being a servant to getting to this level... it was quite the accomplishment.
He finished the drink, set the empty bottle down on the porch, and stood up.
There was still work to do.
He started with the lawn. The small patch of grass in front of the porch had grown wild and uneven, with weeds. He pulled them by hand, cleared the dead patches, and raked the soil flat.
Then the fence.
He sanded the corroded spots applied primer, and painted over the entire fence white, making it looked really really nice.
Then the porch columns next, the railing, the front steps and other things.
It was well past seven when he finally set down his tools.
He went to the street to admire his handy work and he couldn’t help but smile.
’Now it looks perfect!’

chapters.title: Chapter 153 | Rewards!!!
paragraphs: Admiring his work for a few more minutes, Dexter smiled in satisfaction, walked inside and headed straight for the kitchen.

Dinner had already been prepared earlier that afternoon while he was making the pepper soup for Lyra and Selene, he had simultaneously assembled a separate meal of braised vegetables and steamed rice with a side of pan-seared chicken.
The food had been kept warm in the Type-II Spirit Cooking Pot, which maintained temperature perfectly without overcooking.
He ladled the food into four bowls, set them on the table, and called the girls.
It was silent but the sound of the TV from the living room could be heard all the way to the dining table.
The braised vegetables were perfectly seasoned, the chicken seared with a crisp, golden skin that gave way to tender, juicy meat.
After dinner, he washed the dishes, dried his hands, and walked into the living room.
Mira was sitting in her wheelchair by the window which was now her usual spot.
Her complexion had improved somewhat since the afternoon. But there was still lingering pink along her cheekbones and the tips of her ears.
Dexter stopped behind her wheelchair and reached for the brakes.
"Come on," he said. "Time for your evening massage."
"Not today."
Dexter paused, his hands hovering over the brake levers.
He looked at her and saw her eyes were fixed firmly on the window.
Although he wouldn’t claim to know Mira deeply but he had learned to read her over the past few weeks.
He could tell when her refusals were performative, when she pushed back simply because of her pride and when she was truly serious.
This time, she was serious.
He removed his hands from the wheelchair.
"Alright," he said slowly. Then, after a second, his brow furrowed with concern. "Is it the fever? Are you feeling worse? I can make more soup if you—"
Mira’s head snapped toward him and her crimson eyes unexpectedly widened as her brows furrowed in confusion
’Fever? Soup?’
It took her a full two seconds to connect the dots.
’He truly has no idea... This idiot.’
Mira stared at him incredulously for a moment. Then she exhaled slowly and shook her head.
"No need. I’ll be alright by tomorrow."
She spoke calmly but the pink on her ears darkened even further.
Dexter studied her face carefully. Her complexion did look better than it had a few hours ago.
She was probably right, whatever had caused it seemed to be passing.
"Alright," he conceded. "But if you haven’t improved by tomorrow, I’ll call a doctor to come look at you."
Mira’s eyes narrowed. "There’s no need to go that far.
"It could be something serious, Mira. If—"
"Im fine is." She said in a sharp tone then turned her head as she said in a soft tone.. "I just need to be alone for a while."
Dexter blinked as he frowned at her. ’This is new...’
He could tell she was angry and yet she was trying to be. He shook his head and scoffed. "You’re really bipolar you know that."
Mira rolled her eyes and refused to answer his obvious attempt at ragebaiting.
Seeing her not taking the bait, Dexter shrugged and left for his room.
Cultivating on his bed, Dexter gave up trying to decode the labyrinth of Mira’s emotions, and closed his eyes.
He had barely entered a meditative state when—
Ding!
Dexter’s eyes snapped open.
Golden text materialized in the air before him.
[10,000x Investment System Activated]
[Calculating cumulative investments...]
[Multiplier: 100x]
[Investment 1: Purchased snacks and junk food for Lyra Vance.]

[Return: 100 Grade-2 Assorted Snacks — Varieties include mana soaked chips, chocolate wafers, honey-roasted mana nuts, dried celestial fruit strips, and assorted confectioneries. All items possess mild restorative properties and are safe for daily consumption.]
[Investment 2: Purchased massage oil and massaging equipment for Mira Calloway.]

[Return: Grade-4 Spiritual Massage Oil — A refined medicinal oil that penetrates deep into muscle tissue, repairs micro-tears in connective tissue, and soothes nerve endings. Regular application accelerates long-term nerve regeneration by 15%.]
[Return: Type-3 Shockwave Gloves — Can release shockwave attacks from the palms]
[Investment 3: Performed 36 Styles Massage Technique on Mira Calloway, stimulating dormant nerve pathways and channeling mana into damaged tissue.]
[Return: Technique Evolution — 36 Styles Massage Technique (Tier 2) → 108 Heavenly Massage Sutra Technique (Tier 5)]
[108 Heavenly Massage Sutra (Tier 5)]

Description: A legendary body-refining massage art passed down from ancient medical cultivators. The sutra contains 108 distinct techniques, each targeting a different aspect of the physical body — muscle, bone, nerve, meridian, organ, blood vessel, and even the soul-anchoring points along the spine.
Effects when performed on others:
- Accelerates healing of damaged tissue by 400%
- Stimulates dormant nerve pathways
- Improves blood circulation dramatically
- Releases accumulated tension in deep muscle tissue
- Strengthens the connection between mind and body
- Can gradually repair minor meridian damage with repeated sessions
- Induces a state of deep physical and mental relaxation.
[Investment 4: Taught Mira Calloway new physical awareness through therapeutic bodywork.]
[Return: Grade-3 Contraceptive Capsule ×5]
[Grade-3 Contraceptive Capsule]
Appearance: A small, translucent capsule containing two pills — one red, one blue.
Effects:

- Red Pill: Consuming the red pill renders the user completely infertile for one full year. No pregnancy can occur regardless of circumstances. The effect is immediate and cannot be overridden by other medications or abilities.
- Blue Pill: Consuming the blue pill immediately cancels the red pill’s effect, restoring full fertility within 24 hours.
Note: Both pills are painless, have zero side effects, and do not interfere with mana circulation or cultivation.
[Investment 5: Purchased paint and renovation materials for the household.]

[Return: Type-3 Invisible Paint — A specialized paint infused with light-bending mana particles. When applied to any surface — including skin, clothing, weapons, or structures — it renders the coated object completely invisible to the naked eye and most mana-detection methods for up to 8 hours. Washes off completely with warm water.]

sentences.text: Admiring his work for a few more minutes, Dexter smiled in satisfaction, walked inside and headed straight for the kitchen.

Dinner had already been prepared earlier that afternoon while he was making the pepper soup for Lyra and Selene, he had simultaneously assembled a separate meal of braised vegetables and steamed rice with a side of pan-seared chicken.
The food had been kept warm in the Type-II Spirit Cooking Pot, which maintained temperature perfectly without overcooking.
He ladled the food into four bowls, set them on the table, and called the girls.
It was silent but the sound of the TV from the living room could be heard all the way to the dining table.
The braised vegetables were perfectly seasoned, the chicken seared with a crisp, golden skin that gave way to tender, juicy meat.
After dinner, he washed the dishes, dried his hands, and walked into the living room.
Mira was sitting in her wheelchair by the window which was now her usual spot.
Her complexion had improved somewhat since the afternoon.
But there was still lingering pink along her cheekbones and the tips of her ears.
Dexter stopped behind her wheelchair and reached for the brakes.
"Come on," he said.
"Time for your evening massage."
"Not today."
Dexter paused, his hands hovering over the brake levers.
He looked at her and saw her eyes were fixed firmly on the window.
Although he wouldn’t claim to know Mira deeply but he had learned to read her over the past few weeks.
He could tell when her refusals were performative, when she pushed back simply because of her pride and when she was truly serious.
This time, she was serious.
He removed his hands from the wheelchair.
"Alright," he said slowly.
Then, after a second, his brow furrowed with concern.
"Is it the fever?
Are you feeling worse?
I can make more soup if you—"
Mira’s head snapped toward him and her crimson eyes unexpectedly widened as her brows furrowed in confusion
’Fever?
Soup?’
It took her a full two seconds to connect the dots.
’He truly has no idea...
This idiot.’
Mira stared at him incredulously for a moment.
Then she exhaled slowly and shook her head.
"No need.
I’ll be alright by tomorrow."
She spoke calmly but the pink on her ears darkened even further.
Dexter studied her face carefully.
Her complexion did look better than it had a few hours ago.
She was probably right, whatever had caused it seemed to be passing.
"Alright," he conceded.
"But if you haven’t improved by tomorrow, I’ll call a doctor to come look at you."
Mira’s eyes narrowed.
"There’s no need to go that far.
"It could be something serious, Mira.
If—"
"Im fine is." She said in a sharp tone then turned her head as she said in a soft tone..
"I just need to be alone for a while."
Dexter blinked as he frowned at her. ’This is new...’
He could tell she was angry and yet she was trying to be.
He shook his head and scoffed.
"You’re really bipolar you know that."
Mira rolled her eyes and refused to answer his obvious attempt at ragebaiting.
Seeing her not taking the bait, Dexter shrugged and left for his room.
Cultivating on his bed, Dexter gave up trying to decode the labyrinth of Mira’s emotions, and closed his eyes.
He had barely entered a meditative state when—
Ding!
Dexter’s eyes snapped open.
Golden text materialized in the air before him.

[Calculating cumulative investments...]

All items possess mild restorative properties and are safe for daily consumption.]

Regular application accelerates long-term nerve regeneration by 15%.]
[Return: Type-3 Shockwave Gloves — Can release shockwave attacks from the palms]

chapters.title: Chapter 154 | Legal Owner Of House
paragraphs: [Investment 7: Bought Grade-3 Fiend-Class meat for all three wives.]
[Return: 20 kg of Transcendent-Class Beast Meat (Tier 1)]
[Transcendent-Class Beast Meat (Tier 1)]

Description: Meat harvested from a Tier-1 Transcendent Realm beast. This meat is saturated with incredibly dense, pure life energy. Consumption grants significant permanent boosts to physical attributes, accelerates cultivation, and dramatically strengthens the body’s foundation. The flavor is rich, complex, and deeply savory — considered a delicacy even among Transcendent Realm cultivators.
Note: This meat is approximately 50 times more potent than Fiend-Class beast meat.
[Investment 8: Provided ongoing daily nourishment and care.]
[Return: 3 Years of Compressed Cultivation]
[Return: 500 kg of Celestial Spirit Beans]
[Celestial Spirit Beans]

Description: A rare, cultivation-grade legume grown in high-density mana fields. Each bean contains concentrated energy and essential nutrients. It also cleans impurities in the body and is rumored that once eaten for a long time, one would gain the legendary Holy Son/ Daughter Physique, pure of even a single grain of dirt.
[Investment 9: Endured physical pain absorbed from wives via Ring of Shared Burdens.]
[Return: Adrenaline Surge Pill ×3]
[Adrenaline Surge Pill]
Grade: 3

Effect: Upon consumption, the pill instantly heals all current injuries and eliminates all physical pain for 6 hours. During this period, the user’s physical attributes surge to their absolute maximum potential, temporarily breaking through all physical limits.
Warning: Once the 6-hour duration expires, all previously healed injuries will return — worsened by 20%. The user will also experience severe exhaustion for 12 hours.
Note: The host now possesses a total of 3 Adrenaline Surge Pills.
Dexter started going through the notifications happily.
The first one made him smile, knowing he had more snacks to feed Lyra.
The second investment return was to be expected. He had taken his time to purchase things for Mira to increase the massage effectiveness.
The shockwave glove was also a nice addition. It gauges him more long range ability to battle enemies.
As he saw the third investment reward, Dexter smiled even more. The technique has finally advanced all the way to Tier 5. He had been waiting for this for a while.
Now that Mira was staring to heal and could now move her fingers. With this sutra, it wouldn’t be long before she would be able to walk now. Dexter was quite excited.
He didn’t wait to see others reaction when Mira suddenly stands up, shocking the entire world with her strength.
’Would be even better if the system would reward me for making her walk.’
’Now that it works on meridians, I can finally use it on the others... I don’t think Selene would allow that though.’ He pursed his lips and then checked the dead id the notification.
Then his eyes landed on the 4th investment return and his expression slowly transformed from confusion to disbelief to bewilderment.
"Taught Mira Calloway new physical awareness through therapeutic bodywork"?
He had massaged her entire body just like he has always done.
It was purely a medical procedure designed to stimulate nerve regeneration and prevent muscle atrophy.
’How come I taught her new physical awareness? And why the hell is the system giving me contraceptives?’
His face warmed.
’What exactly does the system think I was doing?’
He flipped his hands and stared at the capsule packet that had materialized in his palm. They contained a red pill and a blue pill nestled side by side like two tiny jewels.

They could actually prevent pregnancy for a full year without a single repercussions. It round sell quite well among youngsters. But Dexter shook his head and shoved them into his spatial storage without looking at them again.
’I’m not going to think about this.’
He forced his mind away from the topic with considerable effort and looked at the next notification.
Dexter raised an eyebrow.
Invisible paint. He could paint himself invisible. Or paint a wall invisible. Or paint a weapon invisible.
’Interesting. I have no idea what I’ll use this for, but interesting.’
Then his eyes drifted to the next reward and Dexter’s eyes widened.
He read the notification almost five times to confirm it.
’The deed to the house?’

His mind flashed back to the first day — standing outside the bungalow with the Ashford family butler, accepting an envelope containing a key and a set of documents. The butler had told him that the house was his. That the Ashford family had washed their hands of it. That he was the sole owner.
But the system was now telling him otherwise. He quickly searched underneath his bed and brought out a set of documents.
It looked real and his name was there but now, the system was generating a ’new’ deed for him, which means the original documents had been fake!

The Ashford family had never actually transferred ownership of the house to him and they had given him a key to a house they still legally owned, most likely as a means of retaining leverage. A way to evict him, or worse, reclaim the property whenever it suited them!
He truly hasn’t escaped the influence of the Ashford family even after all these time?!
Dexter’s face flushed red as crimson veins started to climb up neck, buldging out from underneath his skin like snakes.
Three rings appeared in his eyes as he clenched his fists tightly. He was truly angry this time.
"Aldric... Valentina... hmph!"
Dexter’s jaw tightened.
’Of course they did. Of course they lied.’

The realization shouldn’t have surprised him. The Ashford family had lied about everything, his mother, his status, the marriage contract, the dungeon expedition that had crippled his wives. One more lie on top of the pile was entirely in character.
But now, thanks to the system, the house was genuinely his. Legally and permanently his with no hidden strings and leverage nor any hidden clauses.
’Let them try to take it back now.’
He folded the deed carefully and placed it into his spatial storage alongside the other rewards.
Dexter then focused on the other rewards and he blinked his eyes in disbelief.

chapters.title: Chapter 155 | Middle Of The Night & Selene
paragraphs: ’Transcendent-Class meat...’

He had never even seen a Transcendent Realm beast, let alone held one’s meat in his hands. Transcendent Realm creatures were the kind of monsters that required multiple teams of Ultra-Rank heroes to bring down.
Not to mention that a single Tier-1 Transcendent beast could probably flatten this entire neighborhood if it wanted to.
And now he had twenty kilograms of its meat sitting in his spatial storage.
’If I cook with this...’

His Great Grandmaster Foodsmith mind was already racing. A single cut of Transcendent-Class meat, properly prepared, could elevate a meal to Grade Five or higher. The girls’ cultivation bases would skyrocket. Their damaged bodies would receive an unprecedented surge of restorative energy.
Dexter’s mouth watered and his eyes lit up. He couldn’t wait to cook with the meat quickly but then, he forced himself to calm down.

He would save this for the right moment. Cooking with Transcendent-Class meat required careful preparation and the right combination of supporting ingredients to create a very high grade meal. It might even have the chance to enter the 6 tier!

Then his eyes at the three years of cultivation and the Celestial Spirit beans. He was particularly pleased cites about the beans. And as for the three years cultivation, he was already used to getting such things so it was alredy normal to him.
’I hope I get more of the Celestial Beans.’
With it, the impurities in his body would be cleansed and while he knew nothing about the Holy Child Physique, it sounded powerful and attractive.
As for the Adrenaline Surge pill, he didn’t want to think about it.
"System. Apply the three years of compressed cultivation."
The effect was immediate.
A tidal wave of mana erupted from deep within his inner universe as it flooded into the massive Helix shape DNA.
His cultivation began to climb as he broke through all the way to the 9th level of the Superhuman realm.
"Boom!"

Dexter’s body shook as his muscles tightened and his bones crackled. His blood raced through his veins like liquid fire, carrying mana to every part of his body. The air mattress beneath him crinkled and deformed from the sheer pressure radiating from his skin.
9th Stage Superhuman Realm!
Just three more stages and he would stand at the absolute peak of the Superhuman Realm. Then breakthrough to the Ultra Realm, the realm of the powerful.
Where one can truly call themselves a powerhouse.
Dexter opened his eyes and three colored lights flickered in his pupils before fading to natural black as he let loose a soft smile.
However, Dexter didn’t pause to celebrate, he closed his eyes again and continued cultivating.
He cultivated through the night and only turned to sleep when it was 2.am.
He had been renovating the entire house throughout the day so he was quite tired and he slept quite quickly, just as quickly as his mom left.
An hour passed, maybe twi.
Then—
"Creak."
The whisper of his bedroom door opening sounded through the room.
Although he was asleep, his enhanced hearing picked it up!
His consciousness snapped back to full alertness and he was about to move.
’Who—’
Then the cold hit him like a ghost creeping around his room.
The temperature in the room dropped by several degrees in a split second. Dexter immediately recognized who it was.
There was only one person in this house who carried that kind of cold.
’Selene? Is she having another episode?’
He internally shook his head. ’I’d just given her the serum. Even if It doesn’t hold a full week, it should be enough for three days right?’
Although he was thinking this, he didn’t move and wanted to see what she wanted.
"Tap." "Tap." "Tap."
Hesitant footsteps sounded on the wooden floor as it got closer slowly as though trying their best not to make noise.
The footsteps moved from the door to the center of the room, then stopped as silence descended.

Selene was standing somewhere near the foot of his bed. Dexter could feel her presence through the cold mana emanating from her and her intoxicating smell just like when the first rain drop of water hit dry desert.
He could hear her breathing slowly.
20 seconds passed, then 30 seconds, as she remained there without moving.
Selene didn’t move and simply stood there, at the foot of his bed, in the dark.
It was then he came to a conclusion... ’She’s cold.’

Of course she was cold. The chronic illness that infected her body generated an endless supply of freezing energy that her body couldn’t regulate. During the day, the warmth of the sun and the activity of movement helped distract from it. But at night, the cold became unbearable.
Even if Dexter had taken away the pain, the discomfort was still there.
And Dexter’s body radiated heat. And not just ordinary human heat but heat derived from one of the nine heavenly flames.
She had come to his room exactly for the heat, but she couldn’t bring herself to do it.
"Tap."
She moved another step closer as her hand, stretched out toward him. Close enough that Dexter could feel the chill of her fingertips hovering just inches above his shoulder.
Then she pulled back.
A quiet, frustrated exhale escaped her lips, then—
"Tap!" "Tap!" "Tap!"
The footsteps retracted as it reached the door.
Dexter wanted to stand up and call her back but he stopped himself. What would he say? ’Stay? Let’s sleep together while I share my flame heat with you.’
"Click."
The door closed softly and silence returned as Selene returned to her room.
Dexter eyes snapped open as he sat upright slowly.
He stared at his closed bedroom door for a long time.
’It seemed she really wanted to stay.’
She had reached out to touch him. And then she had stopped herself.
’Why?’
Three weeks ago, she had flinched at the slightest brush of his fingers as though his hands were made of acid.

The fact that she now ’wanted’ to be near him and that she actively sought his warmth, was already a monumental shift in her behavior. But wanting something and allowing yourself to have it were two very different things.
She was caught between her body’s desperate need for warmth and her mind’s stubborn refusal to be vulnerable.
’It seems we need to talk.’

"Tap!" "Tap!" "Tap!"
The footsteps retracted as it reached the door.
Dexter wanted to stand up and call her back but he stopped himself.
What would he say? ’Stay?
Let’s sleep together while I share my flame heat with you.’
"Click."
The door closed softly and silence returned as Selene returned to her room.
Dexter eyes snapped open as he sat upright slowly.
He stared at his closed bedroom door for a long time.
’It seemed she really wanted to stay.’
She had reached out to touch him.
And then she had stopped herself.
’Why?’
Three weeks ago, she had flinched at the slightest brush of his fingers as though his hands were made of acid.
The fact that she now ’wanted’ to be near him and that she actively sought his warmth, was already a monumental shift in her behavior.
But wanting something and allowing yourself to have it were two very different things.
She was caught between her body’s desperate need for warmth and her mind’s stubborn refusal to be vulnerable.
’It seems we need to talk.’

chapters.title: Chapter 156 | Strange Lady...
paragraphs: Morning came quietly.
Dexter woke around 5:00 AM, as he always did.
The sky outside was still dark and the neighborhood was also silent with occasional sounds of dogs barking.
He showered, dressed in a clean grey wig-beater and a dark joggers, then began his morning routine.
Breakfast was simple today — Celestial Spirit Bean porridge with honey, soft scrambled eggs, and warm Star-Shaped Leaf tea.
He kept the portions moderate. The girls’ bodies were still processing yesterday’s concentrated wave of nourishment, and overloading them again so soon would be counterproductive.
He woke the girls one by one.
Lyra first with a typed message on his phone, [Wake up. Breakfast is ready.] held in front of her face until her eyes opened. She nodded, stretched, and shuffled to the bathroom.
Selene was alredy awake but she didn’t look at him directly. However, she didn’t avoid him either.
After making breakfast, he pushed her wheelchair to the bathroom, helped her through her morning routine.
"Unclasping a bra with two fingers. You’re quite the expert now aren’t you."
Mira smiled wickedly as she watched him take care of her.
Dexter responded half-heartedly.
"Yeah. My fingers are quite magical, aren’t they?"
Mira was stunned at Dexter’s quick retort which made her remember about yesterday’s incident.
"You—"
"You what? Didn’t you start it?"
Dexter chuckled as he wagged his fingers in front of her face and laughed as Mira glared at him with a Mixture of anger and embarrassment.
Without waiting for her to speak anymore, he took care of her. He also noticed the flush from yesterday had faded entirely but it came back when he made fun of her.
Breakfast was eaten in silence. The Celestial Spirit Bean porridge was well-received and even Mira finished her entire bowl without complaint, though she would rather die than admit she enjoyed it.
After breakfast, Dexter left the girls to their own devices and stepped outside to the front porch.
The street was quiet, most residents already gone to work or school.

Dexter knelt on the porch with a bag of seeds and several empty clay pots. He filled each pot with dark, rich soil from the backyard, patted it flat, and carefully pressed small holes into the earth with his thumb. Into each hole, he dropped a single seeds and soon his hands were soon caked with soil.
Also, his grey wife beater were also a stained with dirt. He didn’t mind though and he found it deeply satisfying planting seeds.
"Vrooom!"
He was halfway through the fifth pot when a car pulled up to the curb.
Dexter glanced up briefly.
It was a luxury BMW.
The engine purred loudly like a beast.
Dexter’s eyes lingered on it for a moment, then he returned to his planting.
’Must be visiting one of the neighbors. Probably Grandma Lucy’s relatives.’
’Though why they’d park in front of my house instead of hers is beyond me.’
He shrugged mentally and went back to pressing seeds into soil.
Thirty seconds passed.
Then—
"Knock. Knock."
Dexter frowned and he looked up, staring at the gate for a moment, then brushed his palms against his joggers and stood up.
He walked to the gate, unlatched the lock, and pulled it open.
A woman stood on the other side.
The woman standing on the other side of the gate had orange hair that caught the morning sunlight and threw it back in warm, reddish-gold threads.
It fell past her shoulders in carefully styled waves, it was obvious she had spent hours achieving the appearance of effortless beauty.
A pair of red-framed sunglasses on her face, partially covering her orange eyes.
She was dressed in a tailored cream blouse, high-waisted charcoal trousers, and pointed heels with a leather handbag on her shoulder, and thin gold earrings glinted beneath her hair.
Everything about her screamed money, wealth and taste.
"Can I help you?"
The woman’s amber gaze traveled from his face down to his chest, then to his dirty hands, then back up to his face.
Her lips thinned un disdain as ash spoke arrogantly.
"Who are you?"
Dexter’s eyes blinked, slightly stunned.
"You came to my house and you’re asking me who I am?"
"Wrong address, lady."
He immediately pulled the gate shut, then turn back to continue his work.
He hadn’t taken two steps before—
"Knock. Knock."
Dexter stopped. Closed his eyes. Counted to three. Then turned around, walked back, and pulled the gate open again.
"What do you want?"
The woman’s expression hardened and her amber eyes flashing with irritation and arrogance.
"You dare slam the door against my face?"
She glared at Dexter but inhaled deeply and calmed down and said sharply. "I’m sure I have the right address. No. 18, Willow Creek Lane, Fenmore street. "
"Yes, this is the house," Dexter interrupted flatly.
"Then this is the right address. I’m looking for my sister." The woman’s chin lifted as she looked down on Dexter indifferently.
"I assume you’re the gardener?"
Dexter’s expression didnr change but his eyes sharpened.
Gardener.
He looked at the woman again. Then he noticed the hair again, it wasn’t crimson but it was familiar and also, the facial structure was similar too. The same proud, deliberate way of holding her head.
’Sister.’
This woman was looking for Mira. Which meant she was a Calloway.
But Dexter didn’t say any of that.
"I’m no gardener," he said, his voice flat and stripped of warmth. "State your business here."
The woman frowned. Her lips parted as if to deliver another sharp retort — then stopped as her amber eyes narrowed, studying his face.
Then her eyes flashed.
A slow, knowing smirk curled across her lips.
"You’re not the gardener, which means you’re Dexter," she said. "The bastard son of the Ashford family."
She said it as though she was sating singling filthy.
"The ’conniving’ bastard son of the Ashford family," she mocked as her face hardened.
Instantly, her aura exploded.
"Weng!"
As though a mountain had landed on him, awall of compressed, dense and heavy pressure slammed into Dexter.
The pressure radiated outward from her body in visible waves, distorting the air around her and the grass on the side of the walkway flattened as though pressed by an invisible hand.
Ultra Realm!

chapters.title: Chapter 157 | It’s Just The Wind...
paragraphs: Ultra Realm.
The lady’s amber eyes locked onto Dexter with a sneer.
She expected to see fear on his face, waiting for his knees to buckle and for him to crash into the ground underneath the weight of her aura.
But...
Dexter stood perfectly still as though a slightly powerful wind just by passed him, ruffling his hair and fluttering his dirty wife-beater but, that was all.
His expression was totally flat and unimpressed. He was even slightly annoyed.
The lady’s expression changed slightly as her smirk faltered for a split second.
’Wasn’t this guy said to be useless? How was he able to overcome realm suppression?’
Dexter frowned and said flatly, his patience wearing thin.
"If you’re done with the theatrics, you can come in. I assume you want to see your sister."
The woman stared at Dexter with a slight frown but she ultimately nodded her head as her subsided.m back inside of her.
"Yes. I’m looking for my sister, Mira. I assume she’s here."
Dexter pursed his lips. "Alright. Come in."
He stepped aside.
The woman removed her red sunglasses, and tucked them into her handbag.
As she stepped through the gate and into the front yard, her nose wrinkled in irritation as she walked the ground as though it would stain her expensive heel.
Her eyes swept the yard with pure disgust.
Even though it had all been fully renovated, she still behaved as though she was stepping in a crack house.
Dexter rolled his eyes.
He had spent almost two days transforming this property into something clean and presentable. The fence was freshly painted, the lawn was trimmed and the porch was spotless.
Even the walls were clean and whole. It looked really neat.
But this lady behaved as though it was beneath her.
’Dramatic for nothing.’
He led her up the porch steps and to the front door. He pulled it open, turned to face her, gave her fake smile.
"Come in.
Under normal circumstances, Dexter would have been genuinely welcoming. Discovering that a guest was his sister-in-law and Mira’s own blood. He would hosted her better.
But he didn’t for two reasons.
The first was her behavior.
And the second, was Mira.
If this woman was truly close to Mira, she would have been there three weeks ago, a the marriage and stand beside Mira on that evening.
Bur she wasn’t. And it wasn’t as though she couldn’t have known. The marriage had been public. The Ashford family’s humiliation of their bastard son had been all over the news.
Even the monster outbreak made news. Not to mention the assassination attempt on the highway.
If this woman had cared, she would have come days ago or even weeks ago.
Instead, she was showing up now.
Which meant one of two things. Either something had changed that had suddenly made Mira worth visiting, or this visit had nothing to do with sisterly affection at all.
’Mira isn’t going to be happy to see her.’
The lady was about to step inside when Dexter spoke in a sharp tone.
"Take off your shoes."
The woman froze mid-step and her eyes widened as she turned to stare at him in disbelief.
"What?"
Dexter indifferently repeated himself.
"You either take off your shoes and come in, or you keep them on and stay outside. Your choice."
The woman’s jaw tightened and he eyes seem to erupt in flames as she glared at Dexter as though she wanted to burn him right there.
Dexter blinked hind eye and continued to stare at her with a flat gaze.
He had been on the receiving end of Mira’s glares every single day, this woman’s glare was barely anything.
The two of them stood there on the porch, glaring at each other.
Eventually, the woman exhaled sharply.
"Fine."
She reached down, unbuckled her heels and placed them neatly to the side of the door.
Dexter nodded. "Good, you can now come in."
The woman walked into the house barefoot, and it looked like she was walking through hell.
Dexter chuckled internally. ’That’s what you get.’
Of course he did it intentionally after all, he also wears his boots around the house.
The lady’s gaze swept through the place and her her lips curled in disdain.
While the house looked a bit small, it was clean and every square inch of it had been repaired, painted, and polished by his own hands.
If she couldn’t see that, it was her problem, not his.
The woman’s eyes continued their survey as it moved from the kitchen all the way to the living room then she froze as her gaze landed on a specific spot in the living room.
The space directly in front of the large window. And in that place was Mira
She sat in her wheelchair with her eyes closed and her hands in her laps.
To a stranger, she looked like she was resting but the lady in the doorway narrowed her gaze.
Anna was actually being absorbed by Mira.
The Star Nodes of the Grand Cosmos Scripture were passive. Even when Mira wasn’t actively cultivating, they still drew mana like a gravitational pull.
"Mira," she breathed.
Mira heard it and the mana flow ceased as though it was an illusion.
Mira opened her eyes and turned her head to the direction.
Crimson eyes instantly collided with amber ember eyes as the two sisters stared at each other across small living room.
Mira’s expression was flat as she gazed at her sister while her sister’s brows were furrowed.
’I must have been imagining it.’
She had actually sensed mana flowing toward her sister whose meridians had been shattered beyond repair three years ago and had become a cripple physically and internally.
’It’s probably just the wind.’
That was because the alternative was impossible.

Healing shattered meridians wasn’t a matter of medicine or rest or time. It required a sustained, astronomical investment of heavenly treasures like Grade 6 or higher pills, rare herbs and even transcendent healers.
The kind of resources that would drain even the wealthiest families in Stargate City.
She eas there when her family elders calculated the exact cost of restoring Mira’s meridians and it resulted in them losing 60 to 70 percent of their asset.
The Calloway family which was ranked fifth most influential family in Stargate City would have been reduced to commoners within a year.
And in a city like Stargate City, a wealthy family without wealth would be wiped out in days as old grudges would be settled.
All to heal just a single person.

chapters.title: Chapter 158 | The Nine Families
paragraphs: Therefore, even if the Calloway family sacrificed everything and successfully rebuilt Mira’s meridian, there was no guarantee she would walk again.
Of course the Calloway family refused.

From a purely strategic standpoint, sacrificing an entire family’s future for one member was a losing proposition. The Calloway family had other prodigies they could use the resources they had to nurture.
So they had let her remain until they had found another use for her.
Marriage.
Stargate City was governed by nine influential families. Nine pillars of wealth, power, and. strength.
At the top was the unquestioned, unrivaled, unapproachable Ashford family. The apex.
Their wealth was so vast that the second and third family combined wasn’t even half their net worth. Their political connections extended into every level of government, military, and commerce.

The name Ashford was a brand. They were so dominant that, over the decades, anyone in the city who happened to share the surname "Ashford" through coincidence had changed their name. Whether voluntary or involuntarily, it was unknown.
Below the Ashford family was the Sterling family They controlled the city’s monster corpses. In any other city, they would have been the premier family. In Stargate City, they were second.
The third family was the Montclair dynasty, from old money and old blood.

Their influence was from generational political power. They possess members seated on nearly every major civic committee, regulatory board, and judicial panel in the city. Their wealth was comparable to the Sterlings, though slightly less, and their strength was supplemented by an extensive network of alliances with smaller families and guilds.
The fourth family was the Hawthorne family.

The fifth family, was the Calloway family. They had produced more B-Rank and A-Rank heroes per generation than any family outside the top three. Their daughters, in particular, were known for exceptional mana affinities and rare talents. Mira had been their crown jewel with an S-Rank affinity with an A-Rank Crimson Flame-Heart talent, the youngest B-Rank hero in the city’s history. Her potential had been limitless until the dungeon.
The sixth family was the Frost family.
The seventh family was the Vance family.
The eighth and ninth families were the Carver and Delacroix families respectively

The competition between families are wild and the hierarchy was rigid. Moving up even a single position required decades of sustained effort, strategic marriages, and careful accumulation of wealth and military power.
Or, the easiest way, through marriage alliance with a massively wealthy and influential family. The three families room this shortcut.
Each had negotiated independently ans each had been promised the same prize: marriage of their daughter to the firstborn son and heir of the Ashford family.

The contract had been ironclad as per the insistence of the three lesser families to prevent the Ashfords from wriggling out of the arrangement and making it so that dissolution was nearly impossible.
They had thought they were being clever and had cornered the Ashfords, but knowing that the Ashfords had been smarter.
The firstborn was Dexter.
By the time the three families discovered the truth, the contract was already signed and they couldn’t back out.

The Ashford family had scammed all three families in one stroke. They had rid themselves of their embarrassing bastard son, fulfilled the marriage contract to the letter, and — most brilliantly — avoided giving the three lesser families access to the real Ashford heir and the genuine political leverage that would have come with him.

But the three families had still benefited from the arrangement. A marriage tie to the Ashford name, even through a bastard, was still a marriage tie. The Calloway family had risen from 5th to 4th. The Frost family from 6th to 5th. The Vance family from 7th to 6th. Each had climbed a single rank.

Had they married the true heir the political and social capital would have been enormously greater. It would have been a two-rank jump instead of one, along with access to Ashford resources, Ashford support, and Ashford political backing.
Instead, they got Dexter, a bastard who couldn’t even cultivate.
At least — that was what they had believed.
Although it took time to explain, roughly three seconds had passed.
Rosalind’s fake smile widened as she approached Mira’s wheelchair.
"Sister."
She said in an almost sweet tone.
Mira’s crimson eyes glanced indifferently at her elder sister as she spoke in a cold tone.
"Rosalind. What are you doing here?"
’Rosalind... sounds villainous.’
Dexter hadn’t bothered to ask when she arrived at his gate, nor that he cared to anyways.
Rosalind face made a mock frown, prey pretending to be hurt.
"Mira, I’m your elder sister. Of course I have to check on your wellbeing. You’ve been married for almost a month now. I was worried andneeded to see how your husband is treating you."
She turned toward Dexter as her eyes swept over his dirty wife beater.
Her smirk deepened.
"So this is your husband," she said, addressing Mira but speaking loud enough for Dexter to hear every syllable. "I thought they said he was useless."
She paused as she sensed his energy wave but there was nothing.
"He really is as useless as they said." she sneered and said in a loud tone.
She turned back to Mira.

"During the assassination attempt, I’m pretty sure he was busy hiding in a corner while the real hero did the work." She let out a soft, musical laugh. "Thankfully, you’re alright. That’s what matters."
Mira rolled her eyes.
She glanced at Dexter and a faint trace of amusement could be seen in her eyes but she turned back to Rosalind.
"What do you want?"

"I came here for you," she said, her voice stiffening. "And you’re not being very appreciative. I traveled all this way to check on my own sister, and this is the reception I receive?" She placed a hand on her hip. "But I won’t take it to heart. I know you’ve been through a lot."

sentences.text: Therefore, even if the Calloway family sacrificed everything and successfully rebuilt Mira’s meridian, there was no guarantee she would walk again.
Of course the Calloway family refused.
From a purely strategic standpoint, sacrificing an entire family’s future for one member was a losing proposition.
The Calloway family had other prodigies they could use the resources they had to nurture.
So they had let her remain until they had found another use for her.
Marriage.
Stargate City was governed by nine influential families.
Nine pillars of wealth, power, and. strength.
At the top was the unquestioned, unrivaled, unapproachable Ashford family.
The apex.
Their wealth was so vast that the second and third family combined wasn’t even half their net worth.
Their political connections extended into every level of government, military, and commerce.
The name Ashford was a brand.
They were so dominant that, over the decades, anyone in the city who happened to share the surname "Ashford" through coincidence had changed their name.
Whether voluntary or involuntarily, it was unknown.
Below the Ashford family was the Sterling family They controlled the city’s monster corpses.
In any other city, they would have been the premier family.
In Stargate City, they were second.
The third family was the Montclair dynasty, from old money and old blood.
Their influence was from generational political power.
They possess members seated on nearly every major civic committee, regulatory board, and judicial panel in the city.
Their wealth was comparable to the Sterlings, though slightly less, and their strength was supplemented by an extensive network of alliances with smaller families and guilds.
The fourth family was the Hawthorne family.
The fifth family, was the Calloway family.
They had produced more B-Rank and A-Rank heroes per generation than any family outside the top three.
Their daughters, in particular, were known for exceptional mana affinities and rare talents.
Mira had been their crown jewel with an S-Rank affinity with an A-Rank Crimson Flame-Heart talent, the youngest B-Rank hero in the city’s history.
Her potential had been limitless until the dungeon.
The sixth family was the Frost family.
The seventh family was the Vance family.
The eighth and ninth families were the Carver and Delacroix families respectively
The competition between families are wild and the hierarchy was rigid.
Moving up even a single position required decades of sustained effort, strategic marriages, and careful accumulation of wealth and military power.
Or, the easiest way, through marriage alliance with a massively wealthy and influential family.
The three families room this shortcut.
Each had negotiated independently ans each had been promised the same prize: marriage of their daughter to the firstborn son and heir of the Ashford family.

The contract had been ironclad as per the insistence of the three lesser families to prevent the Ashfords from wriggling out of the arrangement and making it so that dissolution was nearly impossible.
They had thought they were being clever and had cornered the Ashfords, but knowing that the Ashfords had been smarter.
The firstborn was Dexter.
By the time the three families discovered the truth, the contract was already signed and they couldn’t back out.
The Ashford family had scammed all three families in one stroke.

They had rid themselves of their embarrassing bastard son, fulfilled the marriage contract to the letter, and — most brilliantly — avoided giving the three lesser families access to the real Ashford heir and the genuine political leverage that would have come with him.
But the three families had still benefited from the arrangement.
A marriage tie to the Ashford name, even through a bastard, was still a marriage tie.
The Calloway family had risen from 5th to 4th.
The Frost family from 6th to 5th.
The Vance family from 7th to 6th.
Each had climbed a single rank.
Had they married the true heir the political and social capital would have been enormously greater.
It would have been a two-rank jump instead of one, along with access to Ashford resources, Ashford support, and Ashford political backing.
Instead, they got Dexter, a bastard who couldn’t even cultivate.
At least — that was what they had believed.
Although it took time to explain, roughly three seconds had passed.
Rosalind’s fake smile widened as she approached Mira’s wheelchair.
"Sister."
She said in an almost sweet tone.
Mira’s crimson eyes glanced indifferently at her elder sister as she spoke in a cold tone.
"Rosalind.
What are you doing here?"
’Rosalind... sounds villainous.’
Dexter hadn’t bothered to ask when she arrived at his gate, nor that he cared to anyways.
Rosalind face made a mock frown, prey pretending to be hurt.
"Mira, I’m your elder sister.
Of course I have to check on your wellbeing.
You’ve been married for almost a month now.
I was worried andneeded to see how your husband is treating you."
She turned toward Dexter as her eyes swept over his dirty wife beater.
Her smirk deepened.
"So this is your husband," she said, addressing Mira but speaking loud enough for Dexter to hear every syllable.
"I thought they said he was useless."
She paused as she sensed his energy wave but there was nothing.
"He really is as useless as they said." she sneered and said in a loud tone.
She turned back to Mira.
"During the assassination attempt, I’m pretty sure he was busy hiding in a corner while the real hero did the work." She let out a soft, musical laugh.
"Thankfully, you’re alright.
That’s what matters."
Mira rolled her eyes.
She glanced at Dexter and a faint trace of amusement could be seen in her eyes but she turned back to Rosalind.
"What do you want?"
Rosalind’s fake pout faltered for a fraction of a second before she recomposed herself.
"I came here for you," she said, her voice stiffening.
"And you’re not being very appreciative.
I traveled all this way to check on my own sister, and this is the reception I receive?" She placed a hand on her hip.
"But I won’t take it to heart.
I know you’ve been through a lot."

chapters.title: Chapter 159 | Get Out!
paragraphs: Rosalind fake pouted in a false hurt tone.
"I came here for you, and you’re not being very appreciative. It kind of hurts but I won’t take it to mind. I know you’ve been through a lot."

She then moved toward the sofa. As she turned to sit, her nose wrinkled. She looked at the cushion which dexter had cleaned and vacuumed clean, recently vacuumed as though she was about to sit in a public toilet as she gently sat at the edge of the sofa.
It was as though the sofa might contaminate her if she allowed herself to fully relax against it.
Dexter’s eye twitched.
’She’s beginning to get in my nerves.’
Dexter’s patience was wearing thin but he chose to wait and continued watching.
Rosalind crossed one leg over the other as she started speaking.
"Alright," she said, her tone shifting from performative sisterly concern to business. "I won’t argue with you anymore, Mira. I came here for a reason."
She paused, letting the silence build.
"We found the Phoenix Flare Flower."
The name landed in the room like a thunderclap.
Mira’s eyes widened slightly as she stared hard at her sister.
Seeing this reaction, Rosalind smiled smugly and continued, clearly savoring the moment.

"Crowell lead a dungeon raid a few days ago to an S-Rank dungeon, I was also part of the team. " she said. "We cleared the dungeon and killed the Phoenix. One of the rewards was actually a Phoenix Flare Flower."
’Crowell.’
Crowell Montclair. Of the Montclair family. The third most influential family in Stargate City.
Mira’s former fiancé.
The man she had been engaged to before her meridians were shattered, and before she became a cripple and packaged off to marry a bastard she had never met.
Rosalind’s smile widened.

"As you know, the Phoenix Flare Flower is a Tier-5 Heavenly Treasure," she continued, her voice taking on the smooth, persuasive cadence of a saleswoman delivering her pitch. "As I’m sure you know, it possesses a restorative ability called Phoenix Rebirth."
She uncrossed and re-crossed her legs as her confidence grew even stronger.

"Phoenix Rebirth is known for one thing, creating a secondary meridian and repairing damaged ones, granting one the legendary Phoenix meridians which is wider, stronger, and more efficient than the others."
"If you use it, you will gain another set of meridians and repair your former damaged ones. And once your meridians are restored...there might be a chance you could walk again."
Rosalind smiled, crossed her arms and waited for Mira to react.

She wanted the proud, broken sister little sister of hers to be excited, beg, ask about Crowell, plead with her to arrange a meeting. To promise anything in exchange for the flower that could make her use mana again.
And even insult and forsake her useless husband.
Rosalind had rehearsed this moment and she couldn’t help but smile with expectant gaze.
What she got instead was —
Mira’s utter indifference!
Mira’s eyes had widened slightly because she had suppressed a yawn then they narrowed and went completely, indifferent.
"No need."
The two words from Mira’s lips felt like jolt in Rosalind’s brain.
Rosalind blinked.
"I’m sorry?"
"I said I don’t need it," Mira repeated, her voice unchanged. "Now, if that’s all you came here for—"
She turned her head away from Rosalind.
"Get out."
Dexter slapped his mouth to suppress his laughter. So it wasn’t just him Mira was annoying to.
Rosalind stared with a stunned look on her face as though she was dreaming. She frowned uncrossed her legs as she opened her mouth.
"I don’t think you heard me right. Crowell MontClaire , your real fiancé entered an S-rank dungeon for you and found a Phoenix Flare Flower capable of restoring shattered meridians."
She spoke slowly, enunciating each word as though Mira had lost the ability to comprehend language along with her ability to walk.
"If you use it, your shattered meridians will heal, completely. Do you understand what I’m saying, Mira? You would be able to cultivate again."
Mira turned her head back toward Rosalind impatience.
"And I don’t think ’you’ are hearing me right," she said, her voice was so flat at that moment. "I said I do not need it."
She held Rosalind’s gaze for one cold, unblinking second.
"Now, if that is all you came here for, get out."
Rosalind’s mouth opened and closed like a fish gasping for water as the narrative in her head collapsed.
The sister she had come to rescue was refusing to be rescued and was even looking at her with the same contempt she always had for her.
Rosalind stood up from the sofa. Her hands were clenched at her sides, her knuckles white.
"I don’t think you understand what you’re refusing," she said, in a sharp tone. "Father wants you to speak with Crowell. He wants you to ask Crowell to provide the Phoenix Flare Flower to you."
’There it is.’
Mira’s lips curved upwards in a cold smile.
"So Crowell hasn’t actually given the flower yet. And you want me to meet a condition in exchange for a Tier-5 treasure."
She tilted her head, her crimson eyes sharp as she glanced at her sister. She wanted to say something more but she eventually shook her head.
"Forget it. Just leave."
Rosalind’s face flushed with anger and embarrassment.
"You dare defy father? Father will not hear of this!" she snapped as she spoke in a cold tone. "Father has ’ordered’ you to—"
A figure stepped between the two sisters.
Dexter.
He positioned himself directly between Rosalind and Mira’s wheelchair in a relaxed and casual posture but his eyes were cold.
He looked directly at Rosalind, and when he spoke, his voice was anything but gentle.
"Whether it’s your father, or your entire Calloway family..."
He paused.
"...that has nothing to do with this house."
Rosalind stared at him, her amber eyes wide with a mixture of shock and outrage.
Dexter held her gaze without blinking.
"You’ve said what you came to say."
He raised his right hand and pointed toward the front door.
"So now, please leave."

chapters.title: Chapter 160 | Impossible!
paragraphs: Rosalind’s amber eyes flashed with cold fury. She looked at Dexter, from his foot all the way to his head and her lip curled with undisguised contempt.
"When did a bastard servant earn the right to speak to me like that?"
"Know your place."
She stepped forward and her Ultra-Rank aura exploded.
"Now... Fuck. Off."
Dexter blinked in surprise at this girl’s audacity, telling him to fuck off in his own house.
’Bitch, you asked for it.’
His eyes glowed violet and crimson as killing intent flashed in his gaze.
He raised his finger, reaching for the connection he shared with the Protection Talisman.
The talisman repelled all everyone and anything below the Transcendent Realm.
Rosalind who had just entered Ultra-Rank would be sent flying like an ant in a hurricane.
He was a split second from activating the talisman when—
"WHOOOOOM!!"
A roaring wall of flame exploded from behind him.
Dexter’s eyes went wide as a massive roaring heat hit him he took a step back, turning around and was stunned by what he saw.
Mira was actually on fire!
The woman sitting in the wheelchair moments ago was now enveloped in magnificent crimson flames.
Her blood-red hair floated in the air as though dancing with the fire itself and her crimson eyes burned like twin suns.
The blazing flames wrapped around her slender body like an hurricane and she was in the eye of it. She dint look like a goddess of flames, but a goddess of death and slaughter!
Dexter stared blankly.
This...
This was the first time he had ever seen Mira use her talent and it was breathtakingly beautiful and absolutely terrifying. It’s no wonder she was called the Crimson Valkyrie!
Then the flames surged as gathered behind Mira’s wheelchair as they twisted and solidified.
A two meters tall phantom image of a Crimson Valkyrie immediately materialized behind her.
She stood tall and proud, with a flaming sword in her hand.
Dexter stared in slight surprise.
He had read about the Crimson Valkyrie’s signature technique called the Crimson Flame Demoness technique.
It was said that in her prime, Crimson Valkyrie uses this to attack multiple enemies at the same time.
And at her peaks, she could merge with the Crimson Flame Demoness, raising her strength by almost 200%.
With this technique, she had killed above her level and cleared multiple S-rank dungeons.
It was probably what had saved her during the SSS-rank dungeon before she managed to escape.
Mira’s blazing crimson eyes instantly locked onto her sister as he voice lacked any warmth at all.
"When..."
"...did it become your turn to speak to my husband like that?"
Her right wrist actually moved at that moment as she suddenly flicked her index finger.
"BOOM!!"
The Flame Goddess moved.
The enormous sword descended in a vertical arc as it moved so fast the air shrieked!
Rosalind’s face changed as the color drained from her cheeks.
"Impossible!"
Her Ultra-Rank aura exploded outward as a scarlet barrier materialized before her.
"BANG!!"
Shockwave exploded as the flaming sword slammed into the barrier.
The scarlet barrier blazed brightly for half a second.
Then—
"Crack!"
The barrier shattered as the flaming sword slammed directly into Rosalind’s arms which she quickly crossed before her.
"BOOM!!!"
She was blasted backward like a cannonball as her body smashed through the living-room window.
"Crash!"
Glass exploded everywhere as her entire body flew completely out of the house before crashing onto the street outside.
Dexter cheered internally and couldn’t help but grin.
’Home run!’
Dexter’s smile suddenly stiffened and his eyelid twitched.
’Wait. I just renovated this house and now there’s a hole in my living room.’
Dexter glanced at Mira, then at the hole, then back at Mira and he smiled bitterly.
"You should have let me chase her out myself."
Mira blinked and the blazing fire in her eyes flickered as the Flame Goddess dissolved along with the crimson flames.
She looked down with a slightly embarrassed and apologetic expression like a kid who had done something wrong.
Mira remained silent.
Several seconds later, she quietly mumbled, "...I didn’t like the way she spoke to you."
Dexter froze and for a brief moment, his heart skipped a beat. He was actually speechless at that moment.
Pride and warmth bloomed in his chest, making him smile. But it froze at Mira’s next words.
"Only I get to bully you, no one else."
Dexter clicked his tongue and rolled his eyes.
"...Alright, but next time, let me handle it first."
Mira gave a small nod and turned away.
Dexter fake glared at her then leapt out of the house through the broken window.
He landed lightly on the front porch and walked toward the gate.
Outside...
Rosalind slowly climbed to her feet in the middle of the street. She was barefooted as her heels was still on Dexter’s front porch.
Her pretty clothes were covered in dust and burn holes. Her hair had become disheveled and blood at the corner of her lips as she panted.
Her chest was in pain but it wasn’t as painful as the humiliation in her chest.
Various expression flashed across her face.
Shock, confusion, disbelief, anger and also fear!
"Impossible..."
She mumbled over and over and over again as though she couldn’t believe what had happened just now.
Because, Mira should not have been able to do that!
Mira’s meridians were shattered, her mana dissipated and not only that, she was paralyzed from the neck down and in every way a, cripple.
And yet she had just launched an Ultra-Rank hero backward with a single strike from the technique she was famous for!
’How’s that possible? What changed?’
Something that Rosalind didn’t understand.
At that moment, Dexter jumped through the window and started walking calmly towards her.
’Right, the bastard husband will know what happened.’
Suddenly, a terrifying Ultra-Rank aura erupted from her body.
"BOOM!"
The pressure swept across the entire neighborhood.
Dogs that had been barking suddenly tucked their tails between their legs, birds scattered into the sky and even the insects fell silent as the peaceful street became deathly quiet.
