chapters.title: Chapter 161 | You’re Truly Beautiful When You Smile
paragraphs: Rosalind’s eyes locked onto Dexter with blinding, murderous rage.
She wasn’t able to finish the word.
A hand landed on her shoulder.
Instantly, the entire aura erupting out of her body dissipated like smoke, collapsing back into her body as though it had never existed.
The heavy pressure that had been pressing down on the entire neighborhood evaporated rapidly.
One second, an Ultra-Rank hero was radiating enough killing intent to silence the entire street, the next, she felt like an ordinary woman standing in the road in her bare feet.
Rosalind’s eyes went wide in confusion and shock as she turned around.
There, she saw an old woman standing behind her.
The old woman was short, slightly hunched, with her white hair pulled back in a bun, with deep wrinkles framing a pair of bright, mischievous eyes.
She wore a faded gardening apron over a simple cotton dress, and her hands were still dirty from working in her flowerbeds.
The old lady was smiling warmly as she held softly held Rosalind shoulder like a neighbor who had just stopped to chat with a fellow neighbor about the weather.
"Hey kid," the old woman said in a warm tone. "Who are you looking for?"
Rosalind stared at the lady and her mind went blank. That single tap on her shoulder had retracted her entire aura against her own will!
’What the hell is this woman?’
Although this was her first thought, she didn’t dare to voice it out!
For someone to be able to casually withdraw an Ultra-Rank hero’s aura with a single touch meant only one thing.
This old woman was stronger than her.
Far, far stronger.
Her mouth opened and closed twice before she managed to produce sound.
"I... my... I came here to visit my sister."
She stuttered like a little girl caught doing ai something bad.
At that moment, Dexter just reached the gate.
He stopped and took in the scene.
There, he saw Grandma Lucy’s holding Rosalind’s shoulder and she seem to be cooperating?
Grandma Lucy ignored Rosalind completely and turned toward Dexter with a warm smile.
"Little chef. I heard some commotion from your place. Is this girl bothering you?"
Dexter blinked.
He looked at Rosalind and he saw her face was pale and her eyes wide with terror.
Dexter raised an eyebrow and looked at Grandma Lucy. And his eyes narrowed slightly.
He had specifically came outside to vent and teach Rosalind a lesson about speaking with respect but it seems he was late.
Dexter let out a small smile and shook his head.
"Sorry for the disturbance, Grandma Lucy. It was just a slight argument between sisters, nothing serious. Moreover, this young lady was just leaving."
Rosalind shot Dexter a venomous glare but she didn’t dare say otherwise. So she forced a smile and managed to speak.
"Y-yes," she stuttered, nodding rapidly. "Yes, yes. I was just leaving.
"Alright kid. Take care of yourself then." Grandma Lucy smiled and patted Rosalind’s shoulder three times and then retracted her hand.
Each tap made Rosalind face pale even further as her body rumbled. Blood spilled from the corner of her lips.
Rosalind didn’t dare say anything but gritted her teeth and stared at Dexter with deep hatred.
But whatever words she wanted to deliver died on her lips under Grandma Lucy’s cheerful gaze.
She turned and walked toward her BMW with unsteady legs.
She didn’t have her handbag nor her shoes. She was walking barefoot on the street, stepping on the same dirt, and germs that she had been so careful to avoid inside his house.
Now she was stepping on all of it with full confidence because she had no choice.
And that made her even angrier.
She shot Dexter one final, ugly glare over her shoulder before yanking open the car door, sliding into the driver’s seat, and slamming it shut.
"Vroooom!"
The engine roared to life as the BMW pulled away from the curb, accelerating down the street, and disappeared around the corner.
Dexter watched her go then he turned to Grandma Lucy and rubbed the back of his neck.
"Sorry for the disturbance, Grandma Lucy."

Grandma Lucy smiled and nodded. "It’s alright, little chef. These things happen when you have family." She paused, her bright eyes twinkling. "Just remember your promise about giving me a taste of your cooking."
Dexter smiled warmly. "Don’t worry, Grandma Lucy. When I start cooking, you’ll be the first to taste the food. I promise."
"Good kid," she smiled and turned back to her course.
Dexter watched her go with narrowed eyes.
’She’s definitely not simple.’
He shook his head, and walked back inside through the front door.
The living room was a mess.
Glass shards covered the floor, dust coated every surface ans curtain hung by a single hook, swaying in the breeze that blew through the enormous hole where the window used to be.
Dexter looked at the destruction and pursed his lips.
’That’s going to cost money to fix.’

He sighed and began carefully picking up the larger pieces of broken glass, setting them aside in a pile. He would need to purchase new glass, new framing, new plaster, and possibly new insulation depending on how deep the structural damage went.
He was halfway through sweeping the smaller fragments into a dustpan when Mira spoke.
"Is she gone?"
Dexter nodded. "Yes. She left."
Mira’s brow furrowed. "She left just like that?"
Dexter shrugged. "Yeah. She left just like that."
"Rosalind now knows I can use mana."
Dexter stopped sweeping.
He turned back toward her. "Yeah."
Mira’s crimson eyes were fixed on her own hands. She suddenly spoke softly.
"Things might become very difficult for you over the next few weeks," she said.
Dexter’s brow furrowed as he thought about it.
Rosalind had seen Mira use mana which meant she thinks she had fully recovered her meridians, not knowing it was the Grand CosmosTechnique.
And Rosalind would definitely not keep that information to herself.

She would tell the Calloway family. Immediately and once the Calloway family learned that their broken, discarded daughter could cultivate again, they would want her back. Afterall, Mira was an S-Rank mana affinity holder with an A-Rank Crimson Flame-Heart talent. She was also supposed to be the future family head before disaster struck and now that she was half healed, therefore, they’re definitely not let her rot with a bastard husband.
But Dexter had read the marriage contract. Multiple times after realizing he had been scammed.
He had been looking for a loophole but he realized the contract was ironclad.
Moreover, it wasn’t a normal contract but a Death God Contract.

The three families had insisted on it. They had been so determined to prevent the Ashford family from finding a loophole that they had invoked the most binding form of magical contract in existence. A Death God Contract didn’t just bind the parties legally. It bound their souls.
If any party broke the terms of the contract, their body would remain intact. Their body would continue to exist. But their soul would be ripped from their flesh.
The contract itself enforced the penalty, and no power in the world could override it.

The Calloway family, the Vance family, the Frost family, and the Ashford family had all signed it. All four families were bound by it. And none of them, no matter how powerful, no matter how wealthy, no matter how desperate, would dare break it.
Breaking the contract was the same as seeking death.

So no. The Calloway family could not take Mira back. The same ironclad contract they had designed to trap the Ashford family was now the very thing preventing them from reclaiming what they had discarded.
Dexter turned to Mira and shook his head.
"Don’t worry about it," he said, his voice calm and steady. "Everything will be fine."
Mira glanced at him. Her crimson eyes searched his face for a long moment, looking for doubt, but she saw he was completely confident.
Suddenly, something warm bloomed in her chest as it spread slowly, filling her heart. Her gaze turned gentle and she suddenly smiled without knowing.
Dexter stared, completely dumbfounded. Mira was an extremely beautiful lady and now that she was smiling so warmly, her beauty multiplied by 1000 fold!
She was, in that single moment, breathtakingly beautiful.
The words left his mouth before his brain could stop them.
"You’re truly beautiful when you smile."
Mira froze, her eyes widened as the smile vanished.
Her face suddenly flushed red as she quickly whipped her head away.
"Pervert," she muttered.
He blinked.
"What did I do this time?"
Mira refused to answer.
But as she turned her face further toward the wall, hiding her expression behind the curtain of her hair, the corners of her lips curled upward once more.
[Mira Calloway Affection: ...]

chapters.title: Chapter 162 | Whenever You Wish
paragraphs: Dexter chuckled and turned around into to see Lyra and Selene standing in the hallway. It seemed they had witnessed everything.
Lyra eyes lit up in curiosity as her dark eyes moved between Dexter and Mira with barely concealed interest.
But Selene was another story, she seemed to be glaring at him even though she couldn’t see!
Dexter was confused at first but then it took 2 seconds for him to figure out why.
’They heard me call Mira beautiful.’
Dexter cleared his throat and smiled awkwardly.
"Uhm, you two are also very, very pretty."
Selene said nothing. She simply turned around and quietly walked back toward the backyard.
Lyra, however, lingered. She looked at Dexter with an expectant gaze.
Dexter scratched the back of his head.
’I really need to be more careful about what I say out loud.’
He flipped his hand. Three bags of chips materialized in his palm.

They were Grade-2 Sminley Chips. He had no idea why the system had chosen that particular name, but the packaging looked nice enough and the chips themselves were infused with mild restorative properties.
"I assume you want this?" Dexter said with a soft smile.
Lyra’s face lit up like a lantern.
She took the bags from his hand with both hands, cradling them against her chest like small treasures. Then she looked up at him, and a small smile touched her lips.
’Thank you, Dexter. You don’t look half-bad yourself.’
Dexter blinked and laughed.
Lyra’s smile widened by a fraction before she turned and hurried back to their room, already tearing open the first bag.
’One down, one to go.’
Dexter walked through the hallway toward the backyard.
Selene was sitting on the swinging chair at the backyard.
Her eyes were closed with her hands rested on her knees, palms upward as she cultivated.
Dexter stopped in front of her.
"We need to talk."
Selene didn’t respond, her face remained perfectly still, her cultivation unbroken.
Dexter pursed his lips and decided to get straight to the point. "I know you came to my room last night and I also know why.
A faint trace of embarrassment flickered across Selene’s pale face but it disappeared quickly.
"I don’t know what you’re talking about," she said quietly.
Dexter smiled helplessly. "You don’t have to pretend. I understand."
Selene opened her eyes. Her white gaze was aimed roughly in his direction but she said nothing.
"I’ve absorbed your pain," Dexter continued, keeping his voice gentle. "Because of that, I experienced the Eternal Winter Ice inside your body."
He paused.
"I know it isn’t exactly pain but more like an endless, freezing prickling discomfort."
Selene’s eyes trembled slightly.
"You know?" she whispered.
Dexter nodded. "I do."
He slowly raised his right hand.
With a soft whoosh, the abyssal emperor flame quietly appeared above his palm, spreading heat that radiated warmth in every direction.
The surrounding temperature rose immediately and the air around them grew several degrees warmer. The chill that clung to Selene’s skin began to recede,
Selene stared at the flame. Her pale lips parted slightly.
"An heavenly flame," she murmured. "So you really possess it."
Dexter closed his hand. The flame vanished.
Selene lowered her eyes but she still remained silent.
Dexter smiled gently.
"Sharing a bed would probably make both of us uncomfortable," he said. "So how about this instead?"
Selene looked up.

"Whenever the chill becomes unbearable, you can simply cultivate in my room. The Heavenly Flame naturally radiates warmth from my body, even when I’m sleeping. It should help suppress the Eternal Winter Ice without requiring any direct contact."
He paused.
"When you feel better, you can return to your own room, anytime you wish."
Silence filled the backyard.
The breeze stirred Selene’s silver hair. A bird chirped once from the neighbor’s tree, then fell silent.
Several long seconds passed.
"Thank you."
She mumbled quietly.
Dexter smiled. "It’s alright.
Then he looked at her for a moment and added, "I meant what I said, by the way."
Selene tilted her head. "About what?"
He held her gaze steadily. "The three of you are uniquely beautiful in your own way. And that is the truth."
A small smile graced Selene’s lips.
She didn’t turn away, letting Dexter bask in her beauty as she closed her eyes and continued her cultivation.
Dexter went back inside and headed for the storage room.

Among the renovation materials he had purchased, there were several planks of untreated pine. He selected three that were large enough to cover the hole in the living room wall, carried them to the living room, and began measuring them against the damaged section.
Mira watched him work from her wheelchair. She had moved slightly away from the window but remained in her usual spot near the wall.
Dexter cut the planks to size with a hand saw, fitted them into the gap, and nailed them securely into place.
It doesn’t look nice but it would keep the wind and the rain out until he could purchase proper materials.
He hammered the last nail into place and stepped back.
The living room was now noticeably darker.
The afternoon sunlight that had been streaming through the window was gone, replaced by the dim, flat light of the overhead lamp.
Mira’s favorite spot by the window was now just a spot by a wooden board.
The rest of the day went by smoothly.
Dexter cooked a light dinner. The girls ate.
Mira finished her entire bowl without complaint. Lyra ate three portions. Selene ate slowly but steadily.
After dinner, Dexter cleaned the kitchen, washed the dishes, and then turned to Mira.
"Time for your massage."
He expected another flat refusal, another sharp ’no’.
Instead, Mira simply replied, "Fine."
Dexter blinked.
’Fine? Just fine? No argument? No insult? No death glare?’
He shrugged and wheeled her to the bedroom, helped her onto the bed, and began the familiar routine.
Shirt off. Skirt off. Sports bra and cotton briefs remaining. Face down on the mattress.
He pulled on the special Glove, applied the massage oil to his hands, and then began.

chapters.title: Chapter 163 | Damn Vixen
paragraphs: Shirt off. Skirt off. Sports bra and cotton briefs remaining. Face down on the mattress.
He pulled on the Massage Glove, applied the upgraded Massage Oil to his hands, and began. He started with her shoulders, using the same technique as shown in the 108 Body Massage Sutra.
He set the glove to its lowest vibration and worked the muscles along her spine, channeling mana through his fingertips into the damaged nerve pathways.
Everything was fine.
Feeling a tough muscle in her spine, he increased the vibration as his hands slowly massaged her back, moving lower against her smooth shiny skin.
Eventually, he reached her and massaged her back dimples.
The glove hummed as he imbued his mana deep into her muscle tissue, stimulating and rejuvenating it, pressing and rolling at the same time.
Suddenly, Dexter felt Mira’s body tremble. He frowned slightly.
’Was I hallucinating?’
Mira was fully paralyzed, there was no way her body shook. He noticed the slight redness of her ears, blinked his eyes, and proceeded to ignore it.
He moved down her legs, her toes, then moved upwards her thighs as the glove continued its steady, deep vibration against her skin.
Mira’s face, which was turned to one side against the pillow, moved slightly as her breathing started to change.
Noticing this, Dexter frowned slightly. ’Is she in pain?’
But he shook his head, the pain was serenely transferred to him so she isn’t supposed to feel pain.

He moved to her upper thighs. The glove hummed against the thick muscle tissue there, vibrating deep into the connective fibers below as he moved upwards, reaching the peak of her thighs, close to the small gap between her thighs.
At that moment, Mira’s muscles involuntarily spasmed lightly against his skin as Mira’s ears went from red to crimson.
Dexter’s eyes widened slightly as realization crashed into his mind like an explosion.
’Vibrations, girls... I’m a fool.’
When it came to girls, vibration only meant one different things but against a specific part of their bodies, it meant another thing.
’And I’ve been doing it for the past two days!’
Dexter almost slapped himself. Which grown man wouldn’t have understood? And yet it flew over his head like his dad did when choosing a son.

Throughout his time dealing with Mira, he had always cleared his mind by meditating because no man in their right mind wouldn’t be aroused thinking of touching such a beauty everyday not to mention the fact that Dexter takes care of her everyday.
The technique has worked perfectly well until now. Seeing Mira’s muscles involuntarily tremble and her ears flushed red, he couldn’t help but swallow hard as his thoughts ran rapid and wild.
’Chaos in order, order in chaos. The primordial universe was birthed by...’

He immediately inhaled deeply and started to recite the mantra of Limitless Grand Cosmos Scripture because right now, his thoughts were beginning to have multiple scenes with various occupations involved.
’This is going to be hard.’

After several seconds, Dexter managed to tame his mind. He clenched his jaws and exhaled. Then after calming down considerably, he continued the massage but his movements had become noticeably stiffer.
Mira had noticed Dexter’s rigid movements. She suddenly shifted her neck to left side, facing Dexter.
Seeing his flushed face, she smirked, realizing he was finally putting two and two together. In an innocent and perfectly misleading tone, she asked, "Dexter, is something wrong?"
Dexter blinked and cleared his throat. "Nothing. Nothing is wrong. Stop speaking, let me focus on the massage."
Mira’s smirk widened. "Are you sure nothing is wrong? Your face is awfully red."
Dexter remained silent as he tried focusing on his massage.
Mira’s smile grew wider.
"If you’re sick, I can ask Lyra or Selene to buy medicine for you."
She paused dramatically before adding.
"Or if it’s a fever, I can perhaps make you some medicinal pepper soup. It might calm your internal organs and make you less hot."
She said it in a mocking tone, and Dexter’s gaze immediately flew towards her face and he saw a faint smirk at the corner of her lips and finally realized it.
She was teasing him.
He looked down at her, stunned.
"...You’re enjoying this, aren’t you?"
Mira blinked innocently.
"I have no idea what you’re talking about."
Dexter’s face flushed even more as he glared down at Mira, who was lying on the bed. "You are quite evil, you know that?"
Mira chuckled. "I am simply caring about your well-being. How’s that being evil? I must admit, seeing you embarrassed is a novelty."
Dexter forced his face to be expressionless as he feigned indifference.
"Please... I was only feeling a little embarrassed."
Mira chuckled softly. "Took you this long to notice."
Dexter almost face palmed himself before he stopped halfway. The glove was covered in massage oil.
Mira’s brows rose as she glanced at Dexter’s gloved hands near his face. "So, touching me isn’t enough?"
Dexter rolled his eyes. "Behave, otherwise I will leave without completing the massage?"
"Tch! No one likes a ’quick’ tempered husband."
Mira snorted jokingly, placing emphasis on ’quick’ as she turned her face to the other side.
However, her shoulders trembled ever so slightly as she laughed. Seeing her like that made Dexter shake his head helplessly.
’Damn vixen.’

He managed to keep his composure long enough to roughly finish the massage, hitting the required pressure points and meridian pathways as fast as the technique allowed without actually skipping anything important.
When the last stroke was done, he cleaned the oil off of Mira’s skin.
Usually he would have taken her to bathe, but at this moment, it was basically a bad idea.
After which, he dropped her on the bed and then called Selene and Lyra to the room to go sleep while he rushed into his room.
On the bed, Mira looked up at the ceiling, smiling in satisfaction.
The great, calm, mysterious Dexter Ashford, she had finally made him flustered.
’Finally, I was really worried he might not like women.’
She tilted her head back and blinked.
’Or maybe I should really be worried now...’
She chuckled.
For three years, she had been trapped in this broken body, unable to feel much.
But the massage had changed that.

chapters.title: Chapter 164 | Cultivating With Selene
paragraphs: Back in his bedroom, Dexter glanced at the ceiling and let out a sigh.
’Vixen.’
’I truly thought she had fever yesterday.’
He chuckled bitterly as he thought about the previous day.
Then he glanced at the gloves on his palm.
’Should I toss this away?’
It was quite a dilemma because with the glove, the effect of the massage technique increased a lot which speeds up Mira’s recovery.
But now that the glove Wa steering to have another effect, he wasn’t quite sure he should continue using it.
’Ah, this is causing me to have a headache. Will think about it another time.’
He threw the glove into his storage ring and sighed as he sat on his bed to cultivate. It took almost 30 minutes for him to finally clear all distracting thoughts and focus on meditating.
The clock ticked as an hours passed as he cultivated, then another hour passed.
At this moment, Dexter suddenly opened his eyes, glanced at the time on his phone.
’Selene isn’t here yet.’
He had been expecting Selene.
Ever since their conversation in the backyard that afternoon, he had been quietly certain that she would come as the arrangement was quite simple and straightforward.
But it was 1:00 AM, and Selene hadn’t come.
Dexter shook his head.
’She’s not comfortable with it yet.’
He wasn’t dejected but understood Selene’s concerns.
After-all, cultivating together in the same room was considered an intimate act, even if it wasn’t technically dual cultivation.

The mana that passed through one person’s body could mingle with the mana of another person in the same space. Their energy fields would overlap and if they were practicing the same cultivation technique, their breathing would synchronize as the shared mana would carry traces of each person’s unique cultivation signature.
For Selene, who absolutely loathes being touched and maintained strict personal boundaries, that kind of proximity was a significant step.
Dexter didn’t blame her. He simply resumed cultivating.
Roughly thirty minutes to an hour later—
"Creak..."
Dexter’s eyes opened slowly as his door slowly opened. There, a ghost-like beuty stood in the doorway.
The beauty’s head was bowed as her silver-white hair fell forward, covering her face.
At that moment, a chill speed through the air and fog seemed to float with her as she seemingly floated slowly towards him.
The ghost-like beauty was Selene.
Selene hesitantly walked into the room, but seeing Dexter warm smile, the hesitation faded slightly as she into the room.
Dexter stood up from the bed and gestured toward the mattress. "Here. You can take the bed."
"I will take air mattress."
Selene tilted her head, her hair tilting with her as she shook her head.
Dexter blinked. "You don’t want the bed?"
"We can both cultivate on the bed," she said quietly.
Dexter raised an eyebrow, slightly surprised.
But he nodded and sat on the far edge of the bed, leaving as much space as possible between himself and where Selene would sit.

Selene walked to the opposite edge, then sat down slowly, raised her legs, crossed them beneath her, and settled into a meditation posture with her spine was perfectly straight, her palms on her thighs, facing upward and then, she closed her eyes.
There was a faint flush on her pale cheeks and the tips of her ears were slightly pink.
Dexter held back his smile, refusing to say anything. He simply closed his eyes and activated his Heavenly flame. The Abyssal Emperor Flame roared to life.
The temperature in the room shifted dramatically.
Selene’s body constantly radiated cold as the Eternal Winter Ice leaked from her skin in invisible waves, dropping the temperature by several degrees.
But with the activation of the Heavenly Flame, everything changed instantly!
The frigid temperatures instantly rose.
Heat poured from Dexter’s body like a roaring flame.
But Dexter didn’t actually erupt with flames. He simply activated the warmth or heat of the heavenly flames. It rolled outward from his skin and filled the room like sunlight through a window.
The two energies met, one cold and one extremely hot.
Dexter’s heat was overwhelmingly stronger, afterall, it was an heavenly flame.
It radiated intense heat that Selene’s suppressed Eternal Winter Ice couldn’t hope to match.
At that moment, Selene let out a soft, comfortable sigh as the prickling sensation on her skin reduced by a lot and her muscles relaxed.
Dexter noticed it through his Enhanced Hearing and watched her heartbeat slow down incredibly. Her breathing had also deepened and the tension in her muscles had eased.
’Seems like it’s working.’
He nodded internally and then focused on his cultivation.
An hour passed.
Dexter occasionally opens his eyes every 30 minutes.
This time, he opened his eyes and noticed something.
Selene’s spine, which had been perfectly straight when she sat down, was beginning to lean slowly towards his direction.
From her breathing, she wasn’t sleeping but her body was tilting towards him unconsciously like a flower turning toward the sun.
Dexter wanted to increase the heat mire intensely, so she wouldn’t need to lean.
But if he did that, the temperature would cross the combustion threshold and everything, including the mattress, the sheets, the wooden bed frame would burst into flames.
But he also couldn’t tell her to come closer. She was already like a frightened rabbit.
So instead, he moved closer to her.
He shifted his position on the bed, sliding forward until his knees were almost touching hers.
Selene noticed.
Her eyes snapped open and widened as she felt the sudden surge of heat intensify.
The pricking sensation beneath her skin, the maddening itch of frozen nerve endings, seemed to melt as the deep ache in her bones faded.
It felt as though standing in front of a fireplace after a blizzard.
She looked up at him.
Dexter’s eyes were closed, absorbed in cultivation, he was pretending nothing had happened.
Selene stared at his peaceful expression for a long moment.
Then a small, quiet smile touched her lips.
She closed her eyes, straightened her back and continued cultivating.

chapters.title: Chapter 165 | It’s Not What You Think!
paragraphs: Roughly another hour passed.
Selene’s body was leaning forward again.
Dexter opened his eyes and looked at her. At this moment, her eyes were closed and her expression was incredibly peaceful.
Without a word, he shifted his position again. He didn’t move directly in front of her this time but actually moved directly beside her.
At this position, their shoulders were touching with no space in the middle as the heat from Dexter body directly made contact with Selene’s body.
Then he closed his eyes and resumed cultivating as though he had simply changed positions for comfort and nothing more.
Selene’s eyes opened as the heat penetrated through her skin through physical contact.
At that moment, the heat was so intense Selene almost let out a comfortable moan.
The hear from the heavenly flame pierced through her body and the Eternal Ice Winter retreated like a cowardly wolf
She immediately wanted to recoil and leave but it had been a while she felt this better.
Selene stared at Dexter’s face through her Echolocation. She could see the blurry outline of his expression and could tell he was calm and unbothered.
He was still pretending nothing was happening.
Her thoughts ran wild. She wanted to leave, but at the same time, her body wanted to stay!
It was a conundrum...
She eventually gave up as her body won the battle.
She slipped into cultivation and the atmosphere remained peaceful and warm.
It was the most comfortable Selene had been in three years.
She didn’t even know when she fell asleep.
"Ring! Ring! Ring!"
Dexter’s phone alarm shattered the silence like a hammer through glass.
His eyes snapped open.
The room was dim as the morning light filtered through the dusty window. The clock on his phone read 5:00 AM.
Dexter blinked and yawned slightly.
"Ugh.
He was aback by his morning breath.
His body was incredibly stiff. He had been sitting in the same cross-legged position for nearly four or three hours without moving.
He suddenly felt something in his shoulder. He looked to the left and saw Selene was asleep on his shoulder.
At some point during the night, her body had leaned towards him as her head layed on his shoulder with her silver-white hair spilling across his chest like moonlight on water.
As Dexter looked down at her, she looked very peaceful. More peaceful than he had ever seen her.
Dexter stared down at her for a long moment wondering how someone could be blessed with such beauty. It was as though she was molded and crafted specially by a creator.
He could see the hair on her eye was also silver in color and it looked really fascinating. If the creator used a day to craft others, they definitely used a Millennium to craft such beauty.
The dull pain snapped Dexter back to reality.
He had been sitting in this exact position for almost three hours, his legs were numb, his spine ached and his neck so stiff he could barely turn it.
But he hadn’t moved because she had been sleeping, and she looked comfortable, he didnt have the heart to disturb her.
It was at that moment Selene’s eyes opened and her brows furrowed for a moment before everything came to her and her eyes widened.
She felt the warmth beneath her cheek and felt rise and fall of his chest beneath her head.
Her Echolocation activated instantly, painting a picture of her surroundings and she realized she was holding Dexter’s left arm, while sleeping in his shoulder.
Her entire body stiffened instantly as she scrambled upright so fast she nearly flashed step!
"I-I!" she gasped. "S-sorry! D-didn’t—"
She shook her head as she backed off the bed, standing there for a split second, her face burning, her mouth opening and closing without producing any further words.
Then she turned and vanished ran out of the room.
"Bang!"
The door slammed shut behind her.
Dexter sat alone on the bed, staring at the closed door.
He let out a long, slow breath.
Then he smiled.
"Cute.
He stretched his arms above his head. His spine popped and his neck cracked twice. His legs tingled with the return of circulation, pins and needles shooting through his calves and feet.
He stood up, stretched again, and opened his bedroom door.
He stepped into the hallway.
And nearly collided with Lyra.
She was standing in the middle of the corridor, with her arms full.
Her left arm was cradling the Primordial Beast Egg against her chest and her right arm was hugging an open bag of Sminley Chips.
Also, her mouth was full of chips with crumbs the front of her shirt and the top of her massive breasts.
She had been heading toward the living room when Dexter emerged from his room.
She stopped.
Dexter stopped.
They stared at each other.
Then Lyra’s gaze shifted to Selene who had just entered their room and then back to Dexter and then behind Dexter, to his open bedroom door, then to the rumpled bed inside.
Her dark eyes blinked behind her glasses as a something suddenly clicked in her mind.
Dexter’s room. Dexter’s bed. Early morning. Selene coming out of Dexter’s room moments ago.
Lyra’s ears instantly turned bright red!
The chip she had been chewing fell out of her open mouth and landed on the floor.
She immediately turned and bolted into the room, the egg and the chip bag clutched tightly against her chest as the door slammed shut behind her.
Dexter stood in the hallway, as he blinked his eyes in confusion at first, then everything came to him as his eyes widened.
"Lyra, wait, that’s not what happened."
He wasn’t able to finish his words when the door clicked shut.
Dexter face palmed himself right there, his expression caught somewhere between exasperation and amusement.
Then he dropped his hand, rubbed his face, and sighed.
’I am never going to hear the end of this, am I?’

His legs tingled with the return of circulation, pins and needles shooting through his calves and feet.
He stood up, stretched again, and opened his bedroom door.
He stepped into the hallway.
And nearly collided with Lyra.
She was standing in the middle of the corridor, with her arms full.
Her left arm was cradling the Primordial Beast Egg against her chest and her right arm was hugging an open bag of Sminley Chips.
Also, her mouth was full of chips with crumbs the front of her shirt and the top of her massive breasts.
She had been heading toward the living room when Dexter emerged from his room.
She stopped.
Dexter stopped.
They stared at each other.
Then Lyra’s gaze shifted to Selene who had just entered their room and then back to Dexter and then behind Dexter, to his open bedroom door, then to the rumpled bed inside.
Her dark eyes blinked behind her glasses as a something suddenly clicked in her mind.
Dexter’s room.
Dexter’s bed.
Early morning.
Selene coming out of Dexter’s room moments ago.
Lyra’s ears instantly turned bright red!
The chip she had been chewing fell out of her open mouth and landed on the floor.
She immediately turned and bolted into the room, the egg and the chip bag clutched tightly against her chest as the door slammed shut behind her.
Dexter stood in the hallway, as he blinked his eyes in confusion at first, then everything came to him as his eyes widened.
"Lyra, wait, that’s not what happened."
He wasn’t able to finish his words when the door clicked shut.
Dexter face palmed himself right there, his expression caught somewhere between exasperation and amusement.
Then he dropped his hand, rubbed his face, and sighed.
’I am never going to hear the end of this, am I?’

chapters.title: Chapter 166 | You’re insufferable
paragraphs: Defeat is not the worst of failures. Not to have tried is the true failure" —George Edward Woodberry
’I’ll explain later.’
He shook his head and walked to the kitchen.
Today was an important day.
He had promised Tessa and her father that he would deliver twenty batches of Enchanted Meals to their bakery for sale.
But first, the girls came first.
He pulled out his ingredients and began planning the morning meal.
He had Diamond Rice, the Celestial Spirit Beans and had premium organic rice. He had the Transcendent-Class beast meat, and various Heavenly Treasures sitting in his spatial storage.
None of those would be used for the bakery orders. Those were exclusively for his wives.
The bakery meals would be made from ordinary ingredients.
For the girls’ breakfast, however, he had something special planned.
He reached into his spatial storage and pulled out a small, glowing pill.
The Phoenix Heart Elixir.
He still had three of them. These were Grade-4 Divine Medicines, capable of repairing damaged organs, restoring vitality, and greatly reducing permanent injuries.
The problem was delivery.

He couldn’t simply walk up to the girls and say, "Here, take this medicine." Even though they were beginning to trust him, they weren’t at the level where he could hand them unidentified pills and expect them to swallow without question.
’Lyra would probably take it without asking.’
Dexter chuckled as he thought of the cute girl.
But for Mira and Selene, he needed a subtler approach.
As a Great Grandmaster Foodsmith, he possessed the advanced ability to dissolve the concentrated medicinal properties of high-grade pills directly into an Arcane meal.
By doing this, the healing effect would be even increased than consuming the pill directly and all three girls would benefit simultaneously.
He dissolved one Phoenix Heart Elixir into a small vial of warm water, using his heavenly flame to break down the pill’s structure at the molecular level.
Then he began cooking.
He selected the Celestial Kirin Spirit Rice from his recipe collection.
Celestial Kirin Spirit Rice
Improves physical constitution. Removes cultivation impurities. Greatly enhances mana absorption. Increases breakthrough success rate.

He prepared the rice in the Type-II Spirit Cooking Pot, infusing it with carefully balanced herbs and a thin slice of Millennium Blood Ginseng. As the rice simmered, he drizzled the dissolved Phoenix Heart Elixir into the mixture, using his Great Grandmaster technique to weave the medicinal essence evenly throughout the grains.
[Ding! Congratulations! You have successfully created Celestial Kirin Spirit Rice (Grade 5)]
Effect: Permanently heals 25% of all internal injuries. Improves physical constitution. Removes cultivation impurities. Greatly enhances mana absorption. Increases breakthrough success rate.
Dexter nodded in satisfaction.
Twenty-five percent permanent healing was better than the pill alone. The food had amplified the medicine’s effectiveness from twenty percent to twenty-five.
He plated four bowls and carried them to the dining table.
Then he turned around, expecting to see Lyra hovering at the kitchen door, but she wasn’t there.
Dexter blinked and sighed.
’She’s definitely hiding. She probably thinks Selene and I did something last night.’
He rubbed the bridge of his nose and chuckled quietly.
’I really should explain before her imagination runs even wilder.’
But that would have to wait. Right now, he needed to get everyone fed.
He walked to the bathroom. Lyra and Selene had already finished washing up.
He found Mira sitting in her wheelchair, eyes closed, cultivating. He wheeled her to the bathroom, helped her through her morning routine.
He pulled a clean blouse out and began dressing her. He slid the fabric over her arms, positioned it across her shoulders, and reached behind her back to clasp her bra.
His fingers found the clasp.
And then his eyes flashed.
The Talent Upgrade Cards.
He had received three of them from the system. Three cards capable of raising any talent below C-Rank directly to C-Rank without side effects.
He had been waiting for the perfect opportunity to use them on the girls. But the right moment never seemed to arrive.
But right now, Mira was unguarded and was relaxed, fresh from the bath.
’I should probably do it now.’
Dexter flipped his right hand and a golden card materialized between his fingers.
It was small, roughly the size of a playing card, with a "C" engraved on it.
He pressed it against the bare skin of Mira’s back.
Instantly, the card dissolved.
It merged into her skin like a drop of water absorbing into sand, vanishing completely in less than a second.
A faint golden ripple spread outward from the point of contact, racing across her skin before fading.
"Hmm."
Mira groaned softly and her brows furrowed as she felt a slight prickle in her back.
"Why did you pinch me?" She tilted her head, glancing at Dexter with the corner of her eyes as she said in irritation.
Dexter finished clasping her bra and walked around to the front of her wheelchair and shrugged
"I didn’t pinch you. It’s probably a mosquito bite."
Mira’s crimson eyes locked onto his face as she gazed intently at him.
"Mosquito?"
Dexter nodded innocently. "Yeah. They are everywhere now. Even daring to feast on you. Tsk tsk tsk..."
Mira glared at him and said dangerously. "You’re becoming quite gutsy.
Dexter held up both hands in surrender. "Mosquito. I swear."
"There are no mosquitoes in this house."
Dexter blinked. "They probably came in through the broken window.
Mira’s eyes narrowed further.
But before she could deliver whatever punishment she was planning, Dexter heard a sound.
[Ding!]
Golden text materialized in his vision.
Talent Upgrade Successful!
Target: Mira Calloway
Talent: Spectral Arms
Rank: D → C
Talent has evolved successfully.
Dexter’s lips curved upward ever so slightly.
’Success.’
With this upgrade, her proficiency should increase vastly and maybe she could create more arms.
’Two left now.’
He would find the right moments for those too.
For now, he simply smiled at Mira, who was still glaring at him
"Breakfast is ready," he said cheerfully, changing the subject. "I made Celestial Kirin Spirit Rice. You will like it."
He grabbed the handles of her wheelchair and began pushing her toward the kitchen before she could reply.
"You are insufferable," she muttered.
Dexter simply chuckled, then parked her at the dining table and walked to the hallway.
"Lyra! Selene! Breakfast!"
A pause.
The door cracked open and a single dark eye appeared in the gap, scanning the hallway cautiously.
"Come eat," Dexter said keeping his inner voice and outer voice neutral and his expression innocent.
Lyra’s eyes narrowed.
Then the door opened fully as Lyra stepped out, holding the Primordial Beast Egg against her chest. Her face was carefully blank, but her ears were still pink.
She walked past Dexter without looking at him, to the dining table and sat down, staring at her bowl of Celestial Kirin Spirit Rice intently.

chapters.title: Chapter 167 | When Good Becomes Bad
paragraphs: Selene also stepped out. Her silver-white hair was neatly brushed and fell over her shoulders in a smooth cascade. Her pale skin was clean and fresh. Her white eyes were aimed at the floor.
She did not look at Dexter.
Not once.
Her ears, however, were a shade of pink that closely matched Lyra’s.
She walked past him quietly, pretending very hard that the last twelve hours had not happened.
Dexter watched her go.
’Well. This is going to be a fun breakfast.’
He walked to the dining table and sat down.
Four people. Four bowls of glowing, golden rice. Three women who were all, for various reasons, refusing to make eye contact with anyone else at the table.
The silence was thick enough to cut with a knife.
Dexter picked up his spoon.
"Eat up," he said. "It’s good."
No one responded.
At that moment, Mira’s seemed to have noticed something as the three of them sat down.
She looked up at Selene and then her gaze shifted to Lyra.
Lyra’s ears were red and she was actively trying g nit to look up.
Then Mira looked at Dexter.
Dexter was calmly and his expression was neutral.
Mira’s crimson eyes narrowed.
"What happened between the three of you?" Mira suddenly asked projecting the question to her surface thought.
The question landed on the table like a brick.
Lyra was startled and she immediately dove into her food like it was the most important thing in the world.
Selene didn’t say anything either. She glanced briefly at Mira, and Dexter could have sworn he saw the faintest trace of a smirk on Selene’s lips before it vanished.
But Mira had seen it too.

Mira’s brows furrowed even more as her crimson gaze sharpened, zeroing in on Selene. She had caught that smirk. She knew what it meant. Selene knew something she didn’t, and she was quietly amused about it.
’Did something really happen?’
Mira was beginning to feel slightly annoyed without knowing why as Selene’s behavior irritated her.
She turned her sharp gaze on Dexter.
"What happened?"
Dexter shrugged. "It was just a misunderstanding. That’s all."
Mira stared at him, waiting for elaboration but Dexter gave non and simply resumed eating.
Mira’s eye twitched.
She held her glare for a full five seconds, but Dexter didn’t crack.
Mira snorted.
"Hmph. Fine. Keep your secrets to yourself."
She conjured her Spectral Arms. The translucent orange limbs materialized behind her shoulders, reached for her spoon, and resumed feeding herself.
The rest of the meal passed and it was incredibly awkward.
They finished eating.
Dexter collected the bowls and carried them to the sink.
"Knock. Knock."
A sharp double-knock echoed from the front gate.
Dexter’s Enhanced Hearing activated automatically and he filtered the surrounding sounds and listened for a heart beat and he immediately knew who it was.
He dried his hands, walked to the front door, and opened the gate.
Tessa stood on the other side.
She was smiling softly like a kid who had just been given a lollipop.
She wore a simple blue dress with a white apron, and she was holding a large transparent bag filled with empty thermo food containers.
"Good morning!" she said brightly, her green eyes sparkling. Then she grinned very mischievously.
As she tilted her head letting her hair bounce to the side.
"Hope I didn’t disturb anything." Her voice was innocent but it was obvious she was thinking of another thing.
Dexter looked at the mischievous sparkle in her eyes before lightly flicking her forehead.
"Quit it, brat."
"Ow!"
She rubbed her forehead while pouting but her grin returned instantly.
Dexter gestured at the bag of containers. "I assume these are what you wanted me to use."
Tessa nodded rapidly, her curly hair bouncing with each movement. "Yep! Hen- Dad said to bring them over so you can fill them up. He’s already cleared a shelf in the display case for your meals."
Dexter took the bag from her. The containers were clean, sturdy, and came with temperature scaling effect.
"Alright," he said, glancing back at the house. "I should be done before nine or ten."
Tessa blinked. "That fast?"
"It’s just a Grade One meal. Won’t take long."
Tessa’s nodded.
"Alright," she said, rocking on her heels. "I’ll be looking forward to it."
But she didn’t leave.
Dexter waited. She continued standing there, her green eyes fixed on him.
He raised an eyebrow. "Do you need something else?"
Tessa clasped her hands behind her back and rocked forward onto her toes. "Can I watch you cook?"
Dexter was slightly taken aback by the request. Then he smiled, reached out, and gently pushed her forehead with his palm, tilting her back a step.
"No."
He closed the gate.
Tessa stood on the other side, pouting through the iron bars with the wounded expression of a puppy that had been denied a treat.
"Wicked."
Dexter waved a hand over his shoulder without turning around and walked back inside.
He found Mira in the living room.
She had wheeled herself to the window with her Spectral Arms.
Even though the window was now boarded up, she still sat there.
But she wasn’t cultivating.
She was staring at him as he came in.
Her expression was indifferent but sharp.
"I assume that was Tessa," she said.
Dexter paused. "Yeah. How did you know?"
Mira’s lips curled into a cold sneer. She didn’t answer.
He decided not to press the issue.
"Right," he said, walking past her toward the kitchen. "I’ll be busy cooking, so let me know if you need anything."
Mira said nothing. She simply turned her head back toward the window and closed her eyes.
As Dexter left, Mira opened her eyes as she muttered.
’Interesting.’
Dexter placed the containers on the kitchen counter and stood there for a moment, thinking.
The challenge ahead of him was not cooking. Cooking was easy, the challenge was the opposite of cooking.
He had to make his food worse.

As a Great Grandmaster Foodsmith, his natural cooking ability produced Grade Two meals at minimum, even when using ordinary ingredients. The mana infusion happened automatically. His techniques were so refined, that every dish he touched inevitably absorbed and channeled mana beyond the Grade One threshold.
To produce a Grade One meal, he would have to intentionally suppress his skill.
It was, in a strange way, harder than cooking at full power.

chapters.title: Chapter 168 | The Food Business
paragraphs: Dexter had no choice.
This neighborhood was nice but it people here weren’t that rich.
A Grade Two Enchanted Meal would sell for 12,000 to 50,000 dollars per portion. That was a month wages for many families here.
But a Grade One Enchanted Meal? could sell for 3,000 to 10,000 dollars. It was still expensive but some could decide to spend on an arcane meal for its effects.
Dexter rolled up his sleeves, tied his apron, and began pulling ingredients.
Ordinary rice, fresh vegetables, eggs, and the grade 1 arcane meat, soy sauce, ginger, garlic, sesame oil, nothing that would push the meal above Grade One.
He took a deep breath and began cooking but it was hard.
He had to suppress his Heavenly Gastronomy body, stop himself from using heavenly flame and even not even infusing mana into the meal.
He had to suppress all of it.
He cooked with basic techniques instead of using his various Foodsmith techniques.
The containers Tessa had provided were mass-produced thermal boxes. Just well-made disposable containers with basic insulation that could keep food fresh for one to two days.
By 8:54 AM, he was done.

Twenty containers of Grade One Enchanted Meals, neatly packed. Each portion contained a generous serving of vegetable fried rice with seared Berserk Beef, seasoned with ginger and garlic, garnished with green onions.
The aroma was rich and savory but not overwhelming.
Dexter inspected the first container and checked the system notification that appeared.
[Grade One Enchanted Meal — Comfort Chicken Rice]
[Effect: Mana Regeneration c 300%, Strength x 200%, Slight stamina boost. Improved digestion.
[Duration: 3 hours.]
’Perfect!’

He packed all twenty containers into his spatial storage. Then he paused, then ultimately decided to pack extra portions. Tessa had given him thirty containers in total, probably in case any containers turned out faulty.
Twenty for the bakery. Five for his plans.
He packed them separately and stored everything.
Then he turned around.
Two dark eyes stared at him from the kitchen doorway.
’Shit! You almost scared me!’
Lyra was standing there. Her AI glasses sat on her nose as the Primordial Beast Egg was cradled against her left hip.
She had been trying so hard to avoid Dexter all morning, but the aroma from the kitchen had been relentless.
Before she knew it, her feet had carried her to the kitchen without her permission.
She saw Dexter turn to met her and she immediately remembered the morning and her cheeks flushed crimson.
She wanted to leave but the smell was too good.
Dexter calmed his beating heart and smiled.
He pulled a container from his spatial storage and held it out to her.
"Here. I made this for you."
Lyra blinked, looked at him suspiciously but then she slowly went forward and reached for the container.
Her fingers closed around it as she took it but Dexter didn’t let go.
Lyra looked up at him with fluahed checks.
’W-hat?’
Dexter gently stared at her.
"Nothing happened between me and Selene."
Lyra’s eyes widened slightly.
"I only used my Heavenly Flame to help suppress Selene’s Eternal Winter Ice," Dexter continued.
He paused.
"Do you understand?"
Lyra held his gaze for a long moment, then she nodded.
’I believe you.’
Her sweet voice rang out in his mind.
Dexter aighed in relief and released his grip on the container.
"Good."
Lyra took it and immediately turned to leave the kitchen.
But before she crossed the door, she suddenly turned back.
"Even if you were."
Her face went even redder.
’I wouldn’t mind.’
’She is also your wife anyway.’
Then Lyra turned and fled the kitchen like a startled rabbit as the door slammed shut a second later.
Dexter stood alone in the kitchen, staring at the empty doorway.
’Even if I was what?’
’Doing what?’
’So she only looks innocent, uhn?’
He shook his head, rubbed his face with both hands, and firmly refused to think about it.
He changed into clean clothes into a simple black t-shirt and dark jeans, then walked to the living room.
Mira was in her wheelchair by the boarded-up window. Lyra was at the bedroom and Selene was in the backyard, cultivating.
"I’m heading out," Dexter announced loudly as it echoed through the entire house. "I’m delivering the meals to Mr. Henry’s bakery today."
Mira opened one eye. "Good luck."
Lyra’s voice echoed in his mind.
And he heard Selene muttered at the backyard.
"Thanks," Dexter said as he opened the door and walked out of the house.
Then he turned back and poked his head inside and spoke to Mira.
"Don’t open the door for anyone." he joked.
Mira’s crimson eyes snapped to him with the force of a laser beam.
"Get, out." she hissed.
Dexter grinned, closed the door, and locked it behind him.
He stood on the porch for a moment, looking down the street.
Grandma Lucy’s gate was open and he could see her silver hair bobbing above her garden fence as she tended her morning flowers.
Dexter walked over and knocked on her gate three times. But the gate opened before his third knock.
Grandma Lucy stood on the other side, beaming. Her bright eyes crinkled at the corners.
"Little chef! You’re here early!"
Dexter smiled and produced a container from his spatial storage. He held it out to her with both hands.
"Grandma Lucy. I promised you the first taste of my cooking. Here it is."
The old woman’s eyes went wide. She took the container with both hands, cradling it as though it were a newborn baby.
"Oh, you actually remembered!" She looked down at the container, then back up at Dexter. "Thank you, Dexter. You’re a truly good kid."
Dexter scratched the back of his head. "I try."
Grandma Lucy chuckled. "Do you want to come inside for a cup of tea?"
Dexter smiled politely. "I would love to, but I need to get these meals to Mr. Henry’s bakery as soon as possible. Rain check?"
"Of course, of course." Grandma Lucy nodded. "Next time then."
"Next time," Dexter agreed.
He waved goodbye and headed down the street toward the bakery.

chapters.title: Chapter 169 | The Scheme!
paragraphs: The walk took about five minutes.
When he arrived, he saw the shop was busy this morning.

Several customers stood in line at the counter. Some were regulars picking up their morning order. Others were browsing the pastry selection. A mother with two children was trying to decide between croissants and muffins while the children tugged at her sleeves and pointed at everything.
Behind the counter, Tessa was in her element.

She wore a clean white apron over her blue dress, her curly red hair tied back with a ribbon as she packed pastries into paper bags, making change, calling out order numbers, and chatting with customers all at the same time.
The moment Tessa saw Dexter walk through the door, her face lit up.
She turned to the older man beside her. "Take over the register for a second."
Then she ducked under the counter and hurried over to Dexter, her curly hair bouncing.
"Hey, Dexter!" She grinned. "You’re here earlier than I expected."
Dexter nodded. "Yeah. Cooking didn’t take as long as I thought."
He raised both hands. In each hand, he held a large bag containing ten sealed containers.
"I came to deliver the items," he said, glancing around the busy shop. "Though I have to be honest. I’m worried."
Tessa raised an eyebrow. "Worried about what?"
Dexter lowered his voice slightly. "No one in their right mind is going to spend 5,000 Dollars on a meal made by a stranger without a reputation. "
Tessa shook her head slowly.
"You truly do underestimate the people in this neighborhood."
She crossed her arms and leaned against one foot as she smirked.

"Some people here are not as simple as you think, Dexter. You’re always indoors. Apart from me and Grandma Lucy, you don’t know anyone. You should get to know them." She tilted her head, a small smile playing on her lips. "I think they’d like you."
Dexter raised an eye brow but shrugged.
"Maybe I should."
Tessa’s smile widened.
"Come on," she said, taking one of the bags from his hand. "Let’s get these in the display case. Hen- Dad cleared a shelf specifically for your meals."
She led him behind the counter, past the ovens, to a large glass display case near the front window.
A small handwritten sign sat on the empty shelf.
"Arcane Meals— Fresh Daily — Made by A Master Foodsmith."
"6000 dollars per Portion."
"6000?" he asked. "I was thinking 5000 first to gauge the reactions of customers."

Tessa shrugged. "Henry and I discussed it. If we stuck to 5000 which is the lowest, people won’t want to purchase something so low. But 6,000 will make them curious. And once word spreads about the effects and taste..." She grinned. "We’ll sell out by noon.
Dexter raised an eyebrow. "That confident?"
Tessa placed the first container on the shelf with a click.

"Let me put it this way," she said. "There’s a retired hero two streets over who can’t cultivate anymore because of a broken sternum. There’s a woman on Steering Street whose son has a competition in a week. And also a construction worker who comes home exhausted and barely have time to cultivate."
She placed the second container beside the first.
"None of them can afford Nexus cores, but a Grade One Enchanted Meal that costs 6000 dollars that increases their cultivation speed is within their means.
Dexter was surprised by Tessa’s intelligence and nodded his head.
Dexter rolled his eyes.
"You’re pretty smart for one so young." he said as he turned around to leave.
Tessa’s lips curled upward. "Oh, I’m young, am I? I look really young, don’t I?"
Dexter glanced at her from the corner of his eye. "Obviously."
Then he stopped and raised an eyebrow rose.
"Why aren’t you in school today?"
He paused for a beat then chuckled.
"Forget it. I know you’ll give another excuse again."
Tessa’s innocent smile widened until her dimples showed. "I actually have a really good excuse this time. Don’t you want to hear it?"
Dexter held up a hand. "Save it. I’m good."
Tessa chuckled behind him as he pushed open the bakery door and stepped out onto the sidewalk.
He waved once without turning around. "Bye, Tessa. Thanks."
"Bye, Dexter! Good luck!"

Dexter had intended to greet Mr. Henry before leaving, but the man hadn’t been in the shop. Only Tessa and a couple of part-time helpers were behind the counter. He figured Mr. Henry must have stepped out for something and decided not to linger.
But as it turned out, he didn’t have to wait long.
He was halfway when he saw a familiar broad-shouldered figure walking toward the bakery from the opposite direction. Mr. Henry was carrying holding a large bag in his grip.
The man’s face was expressionless as always.
Dexter stopped and waited.
When Mr. Henry’s eyes landed on him, recognition flickered in his eyes and he spoke.
"I assume you came to drop off the Arcane Meals."
Dexter nodded. "Yes, twenty portions. Tessa’s already got them in the display case."
Mr. Henry studied him for a moment then smiled.
"Alright. Let’s see how today goes."
Dexter smiled and produced a single container from his spatial storage. He held it out to Mr. Henry with both hands.
"This is for you."
Mr. Henry blinked as he looked at the container, then at Dexter.
"For me?"
Dexter nodded. "Yeah. This is my way of showing appreciation for letting me sell the food at your place."
Mr. Henry stared at him for a long moment. Then a low chuckle rumbled from his chest.
"You’re quite the schemer, aren’t you?"
Dexter smiled innocently. "I have no idea what you’re talking about."
Mr. Henry shook his head, still chuckling as he took the container with his free hand.
"Forget it."
"Thank you, sir," Dexter replied, stepping aside to let the man pass.
Mr. Henry walked past him and pushed open the bakery door. Before it closed behind him, Dexter caught one last glimpse of the man shaking his head with a quiet grin.
He understood exactly why Mr. Henry had called him a schemer. And the man wasn’t wrong.
The truth was that they had never discussed profit sharing. When Tessa had proposed the arrangement, she had talked about selling his meals in the bakery. She hadn’t mentioned a commission.

And in the absence of an explicit agreement, the default assumption in any business relationship was that the seller took a cut. Ten percent, twenty percent, thirty percent of whatever the market bore.

If the meals sold well, Mr. Henry would naturally expect a portion of the profits for providing the storefront, the customer base, and the display space. And he would have been entirely justified in asking for it.

But by giving Mr. Henry a free meal, thanking him for letting him sell his stuffs in his bakery for free, Dexter had created an unspoken agreement and accepting a gift created obligation. By accepting the container, Mr. Henry had implicitly accepted the terms that Dexter had set without ever stating them aloud.
No commission or profit sharing.
The bakery would sell his food for free. Dexter would keep every credit.
Dexter had spent 19 years in the Ashford estate. He had been cheated, shortchanged, manipulated, and exploited by servants, strangers and mostly relatives and had learnt a thing or two.

chapters.title: Chapter 170 | Shadow Sylve Syndicate
paragraphs: The hardware store was a fifteen-minute drive from the bakery.

Dexter parked the SUV in the small lot beside the building and walked inside. The store was a large, warehouse-style space with high ceilings, concrete floors, and rows of shelving stocked with everything from lumber to plumbing supplies.
He found the window section after a few minutes of searching.

The damage Rosalind had caused was significant. The entire window frame had been blown out along with a portion of the surrounding wall. He needed a new frame, new glass panels, insulation, exterior trim, drywall for the interior wall repair, and the appropriate fasteners and sealant.
He did the math as he walked through the aisles, loading items onto a flat cart.
New window frame, standard size.
Double-paned tempered glass panel, interior drywall sheet, insulation roll, exterior trim and caulking.
Fasteners, sealant, and miscellaneous hardware.
Total was approximately 2200 dollars.
He loaded everything onto the cart, paid at the register, and transferred the entire load into his spatial storage.
Dexter had just climbed back into the SUV and started the engine when his phone suddenly rang out.
He pulled the phone from his pocket and glanced at the screen.
[Unknown number]
’Is it Rachel?’
He frowned slightly.
He had saved Rachel’s number after her text so it definitely wasn’t her. Also, he hadn’t given his contact information to anyone else. Not even Tessa or Mr. Henry.
He stared at the ringing phone for a few seconds then shrugged and answered it.
"Hello?"
A somehow familiar voice came through the speaker.
"Hello. Is this Mr. Dexter?"
Deep West of Stargate City, existed a forest that most citizens knew only by name.
The Green Rim Forest. One of the many dangerous forests in all of Stargate city
From above, if one were to look over with a bird eye view, one would see an unbroken expanse of green.
Endless canopies of ancient trees that is dense and tall that their branches wove together, blocking all sunlight from reaching the forest ground.
But inside the forest was dangerous and dark.

The official explanation, maintained by the Hero Association, was that the Green Rim Forest was not fully explored and populated by monsters of various ranks, with rumors of Transcendent-tier beasts lurking in its deepest reaches.
Adventurers who ventured inside rarely returned.
The Hero Association had long since classified the forest as a Restricted Zone and thepublic accepted this without question.
After all, who would want to venture into a forest full of monsters?
Deep within the forest, in the expanse of green, if you looked with the eyes of a Legendary Hero, would actually see that at the center of the forest was actually a formation.
The moment one pierced through the illusion, there was a mini modern city, nestled in the heart of the forest and there were people in dark purple cloak walking about the street.
And at the center of this mini city was a massive skyscraper. It was impossibly tall, its peak vanishing into the low-hanging clouds.
This was the central stronghold of the Shadow Sylve Syndicate.
The most feared criminal organization in Stargate City. A collective of villains, assassins, information brokers, who operated outside of the law.
They did not seek power, or crave territory or political influence. They dealt in something far more valuable.
Death and money.
Money in exchange for the death of an individual, no matter who the person was.
The Hero Association had attempted to infiltrate Shadow Sylve seventeen times over the past decade.
None of the operatives sent in had ever returned.
At the very top of the skyscraper, on the highest floor, a man stood alone.
The office was sparse, with a single desk at the edge and a chair was pushed behind it.
The stood at the open balcony and there was no glass separating him from the outside world as the cold wind poured freely into the place.
His black coat fluttered behind him with his hands folded behind his back.
The man was middle-aged that looked between 45 to 50. He had dark hair and a single eye. A scar ran across his left eye.
"Tsss!"
A door behind him slid open and two shadowy figure dressed in dark violet cloak walked in
The hoods were drawn up, casting their faces in shadow. Only their jaws were visible as they stopped twenty meters behind the scarred man.
They immediately bowed their heads and remained still as silence filled the office.
The scarred man’s coat fluttered and the two cloaked figures stood motionless, heads bowed, waiting.
Ten minutes passed when the scarred man finally spoke.
"Did you get in contact with the leader?"
The two cloaked figures exchanged a glance beneath their hoods and the one on the left, slightly taller than the other, straightened and answered.
"No. We were unable to get in contact with the leader."
He immediately continued.
"We came across unexpected trouble."
The scarred man’s head tilted slightly.
"Unexpected trouble," he repeated.

"The entire house seemed to be protected by a high-level formation," the cloaked figure continued. "We attempted to approach from multiple angles. But every vector was blocked. The formation activated the moment we crossed the perimeter and repelled us before we could reach the structure. Breaking it also seemed impossible."
The scarred man was quiet for a moment.
"Oh?" The man said in a slightly surprised tone.
"A high-level formation. In a neighborhood like that?"
He turned his head slightly more. His single dark eye shifted toward the two cloaked figures, though his body remained facing the balcony.
"So you were unable to pierce through the formation?"
The second cloaked figure spoke. His voice was rougher than the first. Lower.

"The formation’s threshold appeared to be Transcendent Level. Anyone below that realm was automatically repelled. We tested it three times from different positions. Same result each time." He paused. "Unless you or one of the elders personally makes a move, we are unable to break through that formation."
The scarred man remains silent as his eye remained fixed on the two figures behind him.
Then he asked a different question.
"Were you able to see her?"

Is this Mr.
Dexter?"
Deep West of Stargate City, existed a forest that most citizens knew only by name.
The Green Rim Forest.
One of the many dangerous forests in all of Stargate city
From above, if one were to look over with a bird eye view, one would see an unbroken expanse of green.
Endless canopies of ancient trees that is dense and tall that their branches wove together, blocking all sunlight from reaching the forest ground.
But inside the forest was dangerous and dark.

The official explanation, maintained by the Hero Association, was that the Green Rim Forest was not fully explored and populated by monsters of various ranks, with rumors of Transcendent-tier beasts lurking in its deepest reaches.
Adventurers who ventured inside rarely returned.
The Hero Association had long since classified the forest as a Restricted Zone and thepublic accepted this without question.
After all, who would want to venture into a forest full of monsters?
Deep within the forest, in the expanse of green, if you looked with the eyes of a Legendary Hero, would actually see that at the center of the forest was actually a formation.
The moment one pierced through the illusion, there was a mini modern city, nestled in the heart of the forest and there were people in dark purple cloak walking about the street.
And at the center of this mini city was a massive skyscraper.
It was impossibly tall, its peak vanishing into the low-hanging clouds.
This was the central stronghold of the Shadow Sylve Syndicate.
The most feared criminal organization in Stargate City.
A collective of villains, assassins, information brokers, who operated outside of the law.
They did not seek power, or crave territory or political influence.
They dealt in something far more valuable.
Death and money.
Money in exchange for the death of an individual, no matter who the person was.
The Hero Association had attempted to infiltrate Shadow Sylve seventeen times over the past decade.
None of the operatives sent in had ever returned.
At the very top of the skyscraper, on the highest floor, a man stood alone.
The office was sparse, with a single desk at the edge and a chair was pushed behind it.
The stood at the open balcony and there was no glass separating him from the outside world as the cold wind poured freely into the place.
His black coat fluttered behind him with his hands folded behind his back.
The man was middle-aged that looked between 45 to 50.
He had dark hair and a single eye.
A scar ran across his left eye.
"Tsss!"
A door behind him slid open and two shadowy figure dressed in dark violet cloak walked in
The hoods were drawn up, casting their faces in shadow.
Only their jaws were visible as they stopped twenty meters behind the scarred man.
They immediately bowed their heads and remained still as silence filled the office.
The scarred man’s coat fluttered and the two cloaked figures stood motionless, heads bowed, waiting.
Ten minutes passed when the scarred man finally spoke.
"Did you get in contact with the leader?"
The two cloaked figures exchanged a glance beneath their hoods and the one on the left, slightly taller than the other, straightened and answered.
"No.
We were unable to get in contact with the leader."
He immediately continued.
"We came across unexpected trouble."
The scarred man’s head tilted slightly.
"Unexpected trouble," he repeated.
"The entire house seemed to be protected by a high-level formation," the cloaked figure continued.
"We attempted to approach from multiple angles.
But every vector was blocked.
The formation activated the moment we crossed the perimeter and repelled us before we could reach the structure.
Breaking it also seemed impossible."
The scarred man was quiet for a moment.
"Oh?" The man said in a slightly surprised tone.
"A high-level formation.
In a neighborhood like that?"
He turned his head slightly more.
His single dark eye shifted toward the two cloaked figures, though his body remained facing the balcony.
"So you were unable to pierce through the formation?"
The second cloaked figure spoke.
His voice was rougher than the first.
Lower.
"The formation’s threshold appeared to be Transcendent Level.
Anyone below that realm was automatically repelled.
We tested it three times from different positions.
Same result each time." He paused.
"Unless you or one of the elders personally makes a move, we are unable to break through that formation."
The scarred man remains silent as his eye remained fixed on the two figures behind him.
Then he asked a different question.
"Were you able to see her?"

chapters.title: Chapter 171 | Calloway Residence
paragraphs: The first cloaked figure nodded.
"Yes. But only a glimpse. She was inside the house, near a window. We observed her for approximately twelve seconds before she went out of view."
A pause.
"She appears to still be ill. The amnesia is still present. Otherwise, that bastard fellow would have been long dead."
The scarred man’s expression didn’t change. But something shifted in the air around him as a pressure emanated from him.
The scarred man exhaled.
"It’s already been long enough." He muttered to himself then, he moved his right hand from behind his back.

With a single, fluid motion, he flipped his palm upward. A translucent stone materialized above his hand. It was small, roughly the size of a marble, and perfectly spherical. Its surface was pale blue and faintly luminous, with thin veins of silver running through its interior like frozen lightning.
A Soul Stone.
A rare and extraordinarily expensive treasure designed to increase one’s soul strength.
The scarred man held the stone between his fingers then, without turning around, he flicked it backward.
The stone shot through the air through the air.
The first cloaked figure caught it without hesitation.

"It is not convenient for me to go there personally right now," the scarred man said. "The situation is delicate. Too many eyes and too many parties involved. If I make a move, it will be noticed. So you will do this instead."
He turned fully now, for the first time since the two figures had entered.
"Take the Soul Stone, watch the house and wait for an opportunity."
"She will not be holed up in that house forever. She will come out eventually. When she does, and when she is alone, you approach."
The two cloaked figures listened attentively.
"Place the Soul Stone on her forehead. It should be able to help her recover some of her memories. Once her memories begin to return, she will understand who she is and what needs to be done next."
He looked directly at the taller of the two figures.
"If she doesn’t remember and refuses..."
He said nothing more.
They nodded their heads in understanding.
The Calloway family residence was an empire unto itself.

The Calloway Estate occupied a massive tract of prime real estate in the eastern quarter of Stargate City, surrounded by walls of reinforced white stone that stretched nearly a kilometer in each direction. The perimeter was patrolled by hired heroes in Calloway livery.
Anti-intrusion formations were layered into the walls themselves, invisible to the naked eye but deadly to anyone foolish enough to test them.
Inside the walls, the estate was a self-contained world. Manicured gardens, training grounds, barracks for the family’s private military force and various other buildings.
And at the center of it all, rising above everything else like a crown, sat the Calloway Mansion.
The mansion was enormous. Three stories, with sweeping balconies, tall arched windows, and a grand entrance framed by pillars carved with the Calloway family crest.
This was the seat of the fifth most influential family in Stargate City.
And it was here, in the private study on the second floor, that the current head of the Calloway family sat at his desk and signed documents.

The study was large but understated. Dark wood shelves lined three walls, filled with leather-bound ledgers, cultivation manuals, and historical texts. A single window behind the desk offered a view of the central garden, where ancient maple trees cast long shadows across lawn.
The man behind the desk was handsome, sharp features, strong jaw and high cheekbones.
His hair was a deep, burnished red, darker than Rosalind’s copper-orange but lighter than Mira’s blood-crimson, tied back neatly in a low tail that hung past his collar.
A pair of thin gold-framed reading glasses sat on the bridge of his nose.
He looked to be in his mid-forties but he was, in fact, fifty-three.
The pen never paused as he signed various documents, his eyes scanned each page in the few seconds it took to sign, absorbing the contents with speed.
Suddenly, the door to the study opened but Victor Calloway didn’t look up and simply continued signing.
He signed three more documents, then he set his pen down, removed his glasses, and looked up.
There, Rosalind stood in front of his desk.
She stood with her hands folded before her but her eyes were blazing with fury so intense it seemed to heat the air between them. And at the corner of her mouth, was a trace of blood.
She hadn’t wiped it off and had left it there deliberately, so he would see it.
Victor looked at the blood.
Then at her eyes.
"What happened?"
Rosalind’s jaw clenched and she took a breath through her nose as she spoke like a brat reporting to their parent.
"Mira happened.
Victor’s brow furrowed.
"Explain."
Rosalind explained.

She told him everything. The visit to the bungalow. The bastard husband who had disrespected her at the gate. The sheer audacity of a man with no name, no status, and no power ordering her around as though she were a servant.
She told him about Mira’s refusal. The Phoenix Flare Flower offer. And Mira’s flat rejection of everything.
"She refused to beg," Rosalind said, her voice tight with disbelief. "She refused to even consider it. She said she didn’t need it. She told me to get out."
Victor’s expression didn’t change.
Rosalind continued.
"And then she attacked me."
The room went very still.
Victor’s pen, which he had been idling rolling between his fingers, stopped.
"She what?"
"She attacked me," Rosalind repeated. "Actually using Crimson Demoness techniques against her own sister. She’s grown even more disrespectful after living a while with that batard! Hmph!"
She touched the corner of her mouth where the blood had dried.
Silence.
Victor stared at his daughter with a blank expression on his gaze.
"Has she repaired her meridians?" he asked quietly.
Rosalind nodded. "Yes. Definitely. She was mid-session when I arrived. I caught her meditating, pulling mana into her body before she stopped."
Silence.
Then—
Victor Calloway threw his head back and laughed.
"Hahahaha!"
