chapters.title: Chapter 172 | Strange Family Tradition
paragraphs: "Hahahaha!"
Rosalind stared at her father in shock as his laughte rumbled through the entire study.
"This is excellent," Victor stood up as a hearty laughter bubbled in his chest."This is great news."
He walked out from behind the desk happily with his hands clasped behind his back.
"I knew she wouldn’t disappoint me," he said with pride.
He stopped at the window and looked out at the garden.
"To think she restored her meridians without relying on our family." He turned back to Rosalind, his eyes bright. "This is even better than I expected."
Rosalind’s face changed.

Her father had doted on her after Mira’s accident and she had received her fathers unconditional support for the past three years so she had expected her father to be furious that Mira had attacked his eldest daughter.
Instead, he was celebrating.
Her eyes flashed coldly as she immediately spoke.
"Father," she said carefully, "I asked her to come with me, told her about the Phoenix Flare Flower and the arrangement with Crowley."
"She said over her dead body."
Victor’s expression shifted slightly.
"She doesn’t want anything to do with the Calloway family. She said since she’s married to the Ashford, she is no longer a Calloway and belongs to someone else."
The words landed in the study like stones dropped into still water.
Victor’s face instantly ardened.
The pride faded and smile in his face faded as his face filed cold.
He remembered the contract.
The Death God Contract.
The ironclad, soul-binding agreement that the Calloway, Vance, Frost, and Ashford families had all signed. The contract that had been designed to trap the Ashfords but...
Recollecting this bad memory, Victor’s fist clenched as he slammed it against the deck!
"BANG!"
The desk cracked as spiderweb of fractures spread outward from the point of impact, splitting the polished wood surface.
Victor’s hair literally ignited into actual flames. Thin tongues of fire licked along the strands. The temperature in the room spiked. The edges of the nearest documents began to curl and brown.
His eyes blazed with the same fire, the Calloway family’s signature Crimson Flame talent, activating involuntarily under the pressure of his fury.
"Those Ashford snakes," he growled through clenched teeth.
"Actually managing to deceive us. Twice."
His burning gaze fixed on the far wall as though he could see through it, through the city, all the way to the Ashford family estate on the other side of Stargate City.
"First, crippling the most talented person our family has produced in a thousand years. And we let them convince us it was an accident."

"And then, deceiving us into marrying our daughters to a bastard, a damned nobody. Keeping it secret until the contract was signed and sealed with a Death God oath. Bullying all three of us just because they are stronger and possess more resources."
He slammed his fist on the desk again. The cracks widened as the desk groaned.
"This will not stand."
He took a step forward as his hair blazed brighter.
"There will come a day when we all come together and..."
He stopped as his eyes flicked to Rosalind. He has almsot let out their plan in front of his daughter.
Victor inhaled deeply and exhaled. The flames in his hair dimmed and then died.
He straightened his posture. Adjusted his cuffs. Picked up his fallen glasses and placed them back on his nose, ignoring the crack that now ran across one lens.

"The contract will still stand," he said flatly. "There is no way we can possibly break it. Not without triggering the Death God penalty. Even my death won’t break it. The curse would simply transfer to the next Calloway family head. And I will not condemn my successor to that fate."
He walked back to the desk, looked down at the cracked surface and smoothed a wrinkled document with his palm.
"But we cannot personally bring Mira to come back. The contract forbids it. Any direct action by the family to reclaim Mira would constitute a breach."
He paused as his eyes narrowed.
"However, there is no rule that says she can’t come in her own or a third party cannot coerce her."
He looked up at Rosalind.
"Set a meeting with Crowley Montclair."
Rosalind blinked. "Crowley?"
Victor’s lips curved into a thin, cold smile. "It’s high time we met and strategized."
He leaned against the edge of his cracked desk, folding his arms.

"Once the news of Mira’s recovery spreads, the Montclair family will be very interested. Crowley was engaged to her before the incident. The engagement was broken when she was crippled. But now that she’s healed...
He let the implication speak for itself.
"Doesn’t he love Mira?" Victor’s smile widened, but there was no warmth in it. "Let’s see what he’s willing to do now that she has recovered."
He turned and looked out the window again. The garden was peaceful. The maple trees swayed gently in the afternoon breeze. Somewhere in the distance, a child was laughing.
"Set the meeting, Rosalind."
Rosalind bowed her head.
"Yes, Father."
She tuned and left the study as the door closed behind her.
Victor Calloway stood alone in his cracked study, and smiled.
’Mira, you think you can escape us by hiding behind a bastard and a broken contract.’
’You are wrong.’
’You will come home, one way or the other and perform the family tradition.’
A faint sinister smile spread across his face making one think about the trauma Mira had faced in the hands of her father.
Dexter picked up the phone.
"Who is this?"
A faintly familiar came through the phone.
"Is this Dexter Ashford?"
Dexter frowned slightly. "Who is this?" he repeated.
The person on the other end cleared his throat.
"This is Cole. Cole Stanley. You might know me as Plasmatic Man."
Dexter’s frown deepened for a moment. The name Cole Stanley meant nothing to him. But Plasmatic Man...
Then it clicked.
The monster outbreak. He had fought alongside several of them in the chaos.
"Plasmatic Man," Dexter said. "I remember now. You’re the one who killed most of the monsters."

chapters.title: Chapter 173 | A Call & Thoughts Of Buying A House
paragraphs: Cole laughed quickly on the other end. "No, no, no, without your help, it would have been impossible for any of us to even get into position. If you hadn’t been there, I and the other heroes would have been dead. I wanted to call personally and say thank you."
Dexter smiled. "It’s no big deal. You’re a hero, I’m a hero, saving each other and protecting civilians is larr of the job."
Cole chuckled. "You’re quite modest. But whether it’s our duty or not, I still have to say thank you, sincerely."
"You’re welcome," Dexter said.
Cole paused for a bit and then spoke again.
"I’m sorry if this question is too personal but do you happen to have a Hunter party squad?"
Dexter blinked.
He didn’t have a squad yet and hadn’t asked the Hero Association to assemble one for him as he was too busy with his wives, his system and his cultivation.
He had no idea whether it would become stable enough to support him in the long term.

And while the bakery partnership with Tessa and Mr. Henry would provide one source of income, relying on a single revenue stream was risky. Especially when that revenue stream depended on his time, his energy, and his ability to cook meals that people wanted to buy.
Dungeon raiding was the other obvious option. Nexus cores, monster materials, rare drops. A single successful mid-rank dungeon run could yield more money than a week of food sales.
Combining the two together was the goal. Bakery sales for steady, reliable cash. Dungeon raiding for larger, periodic windfalls and cultivation resources.
With both, he could properly provide for his wives.

Maybe, eventually, enough to buy a piece of land somewhere far from the city. Far from the Ashfords, the Calloways, the Vances, the Frosts, thw Montclairs and everyone else who wanted to use his family as a pawn in their games.
A quiet place and safe place. Where he could properly take care of his wives.
"No," Dexter said. "I don’t have a squad yet."
He could almost hear Cole smiling through the phone.
"Perfect."
Dexter raised an eyebrow at the enthusiasm.

"How about a get-together tomorrow?" Cole said. "Me, you, and a few of the other heroes who fought alongside us that day. Just a chance to get to know each other. Figure out what we’re each good at and what we’re terrible at."
He paused.

"Then maybe, if everyone clicks, we head over to the Titan Training Center, run some tactical drills. Test our teamwork in a controlled environment. See if we’re compatible as a squad before we commit to anything serious."
Dexter pondered the offer.
Tomorrow.
He didn’t have a clear picture of his schedule for the next day. The bakery sales would need monitoring. The girls needed care and also, the window needed repairing.
Selene’s nighttime cultivation arrangement was still new.
And there was always the possibility that another unannounced visitor would show up at his gate.

But those were all variables he could manage. A few hours away from the house wasn’t unreasonable, especially with the Type-5 House Protection Talisman active and the girls’ cultivation progressing steadily.
"What time?" he asked.

"Any time your schedule is free," Cole said. "We know you’re married, and we know married life comes with its own set of responsibilities. Most of us aren’t married, so we don’t have the same constraints. But you do. So it’s entirely up to you. We’ll work around your availability."
Dexter was quiet for a moment.
"I’m not sure about my schedule tomorrow," he said. "Let me get back to you. I’ll text you with the details once I’ve sorted things out."
Cole chuckled. "That’s the best case scenario, actually. Take your time. We’ll be ready whenever you are."
"Thanks for reaching out," Dexter said.
"No, thank you," Cole replied. "For saving us. And for picking up the phone."
The call ended.
Dexter lowered the phone and stood there for a moment, deep in thought.
A squad.
It wasn’t something he had actively considered before. The idea of joining a team, of trusting other people with his safety in a dungeon environment, hadn’t crossed his mind.
But Cole was right. If he wanted to enter a dungeon in the future, he needed a squad for it.
And it would be best if it was people he knew, rather than been randomly assigned a squad by the Hero Association.
He pocketed his phone, walked around the corner of the building into a narrow alley where no one was watching, and flipped his hand.
The SUV materialized in front of him with a soft thump. He opened the door, climbed in, and started the engine.
The drive into the city took twenty minutes.
He found a hardware supply warehouse in the mid-district that carried everything he needed.
A new window frame.
Double-paned tempered glass panel, Interior drywall sheet, Insulation roll, exterior trim, caulking, and weatherproofing sealant.
Fasteners, brackets, and miscellaneous hardware. Everything totaled at about 2000 dollars.
He paid at the counter, loaded everything into his spatial storage in the parking lot, and climbed back into the SUV.
The drive home took him through the commercial district, past the towering glass buildings and large billboards that lined the main highway.
He wasn’t paying much attention to the large advertisements by the aid when the road.
However, one particular billboard caught his eye.
It had the image of a smiling hero in casual clothes who stood in front of a modern two-story house with a small garden and a white picket fence.
Beneath the image was a large stylized text
"HARVEST HOMES — A Comfortable House for You and Your Family"
"Because Heroes Deserve a Place to Come Home To"
Below that, in smaller print: "Flexible Payment Plans Available for Licensed Heroes. Visit any Harvest Homes branch for details."
Dexter only glanced at it. His eyes lingered for perhaps two seconds before returning to the road.
But as he read the texts, an idea started forming in his head.
Buying a house. A real house with four rooms and in a nice neighborhood too.
The idea began to grow, feeding on the accumulated stress and worry of the past three weeks.
Two monster outbreaks had occurred within walking distance of his bungalow. The first had been in his own neighborhood and the second had been at the market district, less than five minutes away.
Two outbreaks in a month. In the same general area was enough for anyone to flee immediately.
Either way, staying in that neighborhood was a risk.
A risk he didn’t need to take since he had a bit of money right now.
While he was already getting used to the neighborhood and he liked Tessa, Mr. Henry and Grandma Lucy, liking a neighborhood and being safe in a neighborhood were two very different things.
And to him, the safety of his wives came first.
’Surely, one million dollars should be enough to purchase a house right?...’

chapters.title: Chapter 174 | Strange Diary...
paragraphs: "Ding!"
Dexter’s phone rang and he caught a glimpse of the message.
It was credit apart and from the hero association.
[Bank Account: $1,200,556]
Dexter immediately smiled. "Perfect."
The payment for his official promotion and licensing had finally arrived.
"1.2 million should be enough to purchase a house, right?" he muttered, glancing at the billboard photo on his phone.
The idea continued to grow.
By the time he pulled up in front of his bungalow, it had evolved from a vague notion into a genuine plan and a goal he could look forward too.
’And maybe while I’m at it, I should also change my surname.’
Dexter arrived at the front of his bungalow. He parked the car and climbed out.
There were a few people walking around the neighborhood.
Dexter smiled and nodded at a few and they actually smiled and waved back at him which took him by surprise.
’When did they suddenly become nice?’

He shook his head and opened the gate, retrieving the construction materials from his spatial storage and stacking the window frame, glass panel, drywall, insulation, trim, and tool bag neatly against the exterior wall.
Then he walked to the front door, unlocked it, stepped inside, and closed it behind him.
"I’m home," he called out.
Mira was in her wheelchair by the boarded-up window with her eyes were closed, cultivating.
Lyra was on the couch with her legs were crossed beneath her in a meditation posture.
The Primordial Beast Egg rested in her lap with the AI glasses on her face.
Her eyes were closed which meant she was cultivating as well, but the moment Dexter’s voice reached her AI glasses, it vibrated and Lyra opened her eyes.
She frowned confusion at first, then turned her head to the door.
A faint smile touched her lips and she raised one hand from the egg and waved.
’Welcome back.’
Her cute voice rang out in his mind. Dexter smiled. "Thank you."
He looked at Mira but she hadn’t moved bro had she opened her eyes or acknowledged his existence in any way.
He smirked and considered saying something but he decided against it and walked to the front window and began removing the wooden planks he had nailed up the day before.
Sunlight poured through the empty window frame suddenly, slamming directly against Mira’s face, bathing her closed eyelids in warm, golden light.
Mira’s face scrunched up in a frown as she opened her eyes.
She squinted against the brightness, her crimson irises contracting to pinpoints.
Through the sun ray, she saw Dexter standing in front of the window with a pry bar in one hand and a wooden plank in the other.
He was looking down at her smiling.
’Since you’re pretending not here, how about now?’
Mira glared at him.
But dexter simply smiled as he pulled the last plank free and set it aside.
Mira’s Spectral Arms appeared behind her as one of them reached for the wheel of her chair.
Then with astonishing proficiency, she wheeled herself backward, away from the window, and away from Dexter’s insufferable grin.
"Hmph!"
She snorted and moved her self to the far edge of the living room, turning her back to him.
Dexter chuckled.
’Finally got a reaction out of her.’
He spent the next hour repairing the window.
Removing the damaged frame, cleaned the opening, installed the new frame with fresh fasteners, fitted the tempered glass panel into place, and sealed the edges with weatherproof caulking.
He patched the interior wall with new drywall, taped and mudded the seams, and applied a quick coat of paint that matched the surrounding wall.
When he was done, the window looked even better than before.
He was cleaning up his tools when a thought struck him.
’The beds and the weapons.’
All three girls were out of the bedroom.
Mira was in the dining room, Lyra was on the couch and Selene was in the backyard.
Right now, their bedroom was empty.
Which meant he could finally change the beds.
He had been meaning to do this for days but one of them were always in the room or it slipped his mind but now, he could change them.
He walked to the bedroom and pushed the door open.
The room wasn’t very large but it was enough to fit the three beds.
This was one of the reasons he wanted to change their place.
The three girls can’t possible live in one room forever. They would need their own personal space to do their own thing.
Lyra’s weapon was on her bed.
Mira’s weapon was on the stand beside her bed and Selene’s weapon was on the dresser.
Dexter flipped his hand and Three Type-6 weapons materialized on the bed in front of him.
He immediately swapped them, replacing each Type-3 weapon with its upgraded Type-6 counterpart in the exact same position.
The Type-6 versions looked similar to their predecessors at a glance.
Same general shape, basic design but the mana density radiating from them was orders of magnitude higher.
If any of the girls picked up their weapon and channeled even a thread of mana into it, they would immediately feel the difference.
’That would be for later.’
Now the beds.
He pulled the first mattress off the frame and leaned it against the wall. He retrieved the new mattress from his spatial storage.
He positioned the first new mattress on the frame, fitted it with fresh sheets and a new pillow, and moved to the second bed and repeated the exact same thing.
Then he moved to the third bed.
It sas Lyra’s. The sheets were wrinkled and slightly greasy from the chips she ate while cultivating. He gathered the corners of the fitted sheet and pulled it free from the mattress.
"Thump!"
Something fell.
It dropped from inside the folded sheet.
"Uhn?"
Dexter set the sheet aside and looked down.
What was on the floor was a book. The book was much thicker than a normal book with leather cover and no printed words.
’A diary?’
As it fell, it had open to a page near the middle.
Dexter picked it up and his eyes landed on the first few lines. His brows instantly furrowed and his eyes widened slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 175 | Strange Reaction...
paragraphs: Dexter raised an eyebrow.
He didn’t know Lyra had a diary.
He looked at the open page and unconsciously read the first few lines.
"My time is growing shorter and shorter. Can’t live as a cripple anymore, might as well let her in. It’s the same as death."
Dexter frowned.
The words were strange.
’Letting her in?’
What did that mean?
His curiosity was stirred, reaching its peak and he wanted to read more but his conscience pressed back just as hard.
It was someone else’s diary which contained detailed private thoughts most likely containing types of snacks she loved.
But reading them without her permission wouldn’t be nice and was a complete disregard of privacy. He slaps wouldn’t want someone prying into his thoughts either.
So he sighed and immediately closed the diary.
He lifted the edge of the new mattress, intending to slide the diary back underneath where it had fallen, when a chilling voice rang out behind him.
’What are you doing with my stuff?’
The voice was incredibly cold and icy. Dexter even felt his skin prickle with danger and his brows furrowed.
Dexter immediately turned around only to see Lyra standing in the doorway.
She was not wearing her AI glasses as her dark eyes locked onto Dexter like a predator looking at a prey.
Her expression was flat and indifferent, her eyes, cold and dearly.
Dexter’s was at first stunned by Lyra’s sudden change in behavior and he thought about various lies to tell.
But he ultimately decided to tell the truth.
"I swapped your bed for a better one," he said, holding up the diary. "I was changing the sheets and this fell out. I assume it’s yours."
Lyra’s face didn’t change.
Dexter frowned. Lyra at this moment looked extremely unfamiliar.
Lyra glanced at the diary in his hand, then at Dexter as she began walking slowly towards him.
"Tap." "Tap." "Tap."
Her feet barely making any noise on the ground as she stopped three feet away from him and tilted her head slightly, studying his face like a cat studying a mouse.
’Do you know the saying about the cat and curiosity?’ she asked.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed, something was wrong.
The voice sounded like Lyra, but it was different.
Dexter didn’t respond immediately. He stared at Lyra, searching her face for something.
His frown deepened.
"I assume this is your diary," he said carefully.
Lyra continued to look at his face.
’Hm. You look quite different from the first time.’
Dexter blinked. "What do you mean?"
Lyra’s eyes suddenly widened slightly as something similar to confusion flickered across her face before it vanished.
The with speed that surprised even Dexter, she snatched the diary from his hand.
’Don’t ever touch my stuff,’ she said with a smile and in a soft voice but that voice was even sharper and deadlier than Mira’s angriest voice.
Dexter remained silent, still feeling strange about Lyra’s sudden behavior.
But then again, he reasoned, if someone had touched his diary without permission, he would have been angry too.
It was an honest mistake on his part, but it was still a violation of her privacy. Her reaction, while unusually intense, was not unreasonable.
He nodded. "I won’t. I’m sorry. It was an honest mistake."
Lyra stared at him for a long, cold moment.
’Get out.’ she said.

Dexter’s frown deepened. The tone was harsher than anything Lyra had ever directed at him. Not even in the early days, when all three women had treated him with cold indifference, had Lyra used that tone.
He considered saying something but inhaled deeply and walked out of the room.
He stood in the hallway for a moment, processing what had just happened.
’She was angry. That’s fine. People get angry when their privacy is violated. I would be too.’
But the voice and the words with the way she looked at him.
"You look quite different from the first time."
What did that mean? Different from the first time how?
Dexter’s thoughts drifted to something the system had told him.
’Shadow Corruption.’

The system had warned that Lyra’s talent was beginning to corrupt her physical cells. If the corruption reached 100%, her body would collapse and transform into a permanent portal to the Shadow Realm.
He immediately opened his system interface and navigated to Lyra’s status panel.
[Name: Lyra Vance]
[Shadow Corruption Level: 2%]
Dexter exhaled slowly.
’So it’s not the corruption, the foodie Lyra is actually this scary when she’s angry.’
He shook his head and walked to the living room to continue repairing the window.
The rest of the morning passed in silence.
Dexter finished the window repair.
He massaged Mira while maintaining a mental focus so disciplined it would have impressed a monastery of celibate monks.
His face remained perfectly neutral throughout but Mira’s face and breathing did not which almost broke him.
At one point, Dexter even felt like the battle with the Four-Armed Goblins wasn’t even half as difficult as this.
After fleeing, he calmed himself down and made lunch which consisted of Celestial Spirit Bean porridge, seared vegetables and sliced Transcendent meat.
When he called out to them, Lyra actually came out last and when she ate, she only ate a single plate.
In the two weeks he had been cooking for these women, Lyra had never eaten less than two portions. Most days, she ate four. On particularly good days, she ate six.
And today, she ate one, leaving the remaining food on the table as she stood up, and walked back to the bedroom without a word.
Not just Dexter, Mira and Selene were both stunned to see Lyra leave without touching her food.
Mira glanced at Dexter and said expressionlessly. "What did you to her now?"
Dexter glared back at Mira. "Why do you think I did anything?"
Mira lips curled upwards. "Men."
She immediately turned her wheelchair to the living room and left.
Dexter smirked. ’Seems like she’s still mad about this morning.’
He ignored her and focused on Lyra.
If there was one thing in this world that could always cheer Lyra up, it was food.
The fact that she had turned her back on food meant she was not just annoyed, she was genuinely angry.
Dexter sat there, thinking for a long while.
He thought about going to her and apologizing again, since he would never intentionally violate her and the other girl’s trust.
But he thought even more about and maybe pushing her now, while she was in this state, would only make things worse.
’Let her simmer down for today.’
He would talk to her tomorrow. She might have calmed down by then. ’Moreover, I did nothing wrong either way.’
He collected the plates, washed the dishes, and spent the rest of the afternoon, practicing his punching and fighting techniques in the backyard.
[I promised Mass release since last week but one thing or the other kept popping up. I apologize for that. Just wanted to say that I haven’t forgotten and it will be possible this week at least."

Lyra continued to look at his face.
’Hm.
You look quite different from the first time.’
Dexter blinked.
"What do you mean?"
Lyra’s eyes suddenly widened slightly as something similar to confusion flickered across her face before it vanished.
The with speed that surprised even Dexter, she snatched the diary from his hand.
’Don’t ever touch my stuff,’ she said with a smile and in a soft voice but that voice was even sharper and deadlier than Mira’s angriest voice.
Dexter remained silent, still feeling strange about Lyra’s sudden behavior.
But then again, he reasoned, if someone had touched his diary without permission, he would have been angry too.
It was an honest mistake on his part, but it was still a violation of her privacy.
Her reaction, while unusually intense, was not unreasonable.
He nodded.
"I won’t.
I’m sorry.
It was an honest mistake."
Lyra stared at him for a long, cold moment.
’Get out.’ she said.
Dexter’s frown deepened.
The tone was harsher than anything Lyra had ever directed at him.
Not even in the early days, when all three women had treated him with cold indifference, had Lyra used that tone.
He considered saying something but inhaled deeply and walked out of the room.
He stood in the hallway for a moment, processing what had just happened.
’She was angry.
That’s fine.
People get angry when their privacy is violated.
I would be too.’
But the voice and the words with the way she looked at him.
"You look quite different from the first time."
What did that mean?
Different from the first time how?
Dexter’s thoughts drifted to something the system had told him.
’Shadow Corruption.’
The system had warned that Lyra’s talent was beginning to corrupt her physical cells.
If the corruption reached 100%, her body would collapse and transform into a permanent portal to the Shadow Realm.
He immediately opened his system interface and navigated to Lyra’s status panel.
[Name: Lyra Vance]
[Shadow Corruption Level: 2%]
Dexter exhaled slowly.
’So it’s not the corruption, the foodie Lyra is actually this scary when she’s angry.’
He shook his head and walked to the living room to continue repairing the window.
The rest of the morning passed in silence.
Dexter finished the window repair.
He massaged Mira while maintaining a mental focus so disciplined it would have impressed a monastery of celibate monks.
His face remained perfectly neutral throughout but Mira’s face and breathing did not which almost broke him.
At one point, Dexter even felt like the battle with the Four-Armed Goblins wasn’t even half as difficult as this.
After fleeing, he calmed himself down and made lunch which consisted of Celestial Spirit Bean porridge, seared vegetables and sliced Transcendent meat.
When he called out to them, Lyra actually came out last and when she ate, she only ate a single plate.
In the two weeks he had been cooking for these women, Lyra had never eaten less than two portions.
Most days, she ate four.
On particularly good days, she ate six.
And today, she ate one, leaving the remaining food on the table as she stood up, and walked back to the bedroom without a word.
Not just Dexter, Mira and Selene were both stunned to see Lyra leave without touching her food.
Mira glanced at Dexter and said expressionlessly.
"What did you to her now?"
Dexter glared back at Mira.
"Why do you think I did anything?"
Mira lips curled upwards.
"Men."
She immediately turned her wheelchair to the living room and left.
Dexter smirked. ’Seems like she’s still mad about this morning.’
He ignored her and focused on Lyra.
If there was one thing in this world that could always cheer Lyra up, it was food.
The fact that she had turned her back on food meant she was not just annoyed, she was genuinely angry.
Dexter sat there, thinking for a long while.
He thought about going to her and apologizing again, since he would never intentionally violate her and the other girl’s trust.
But he thought even more about and maybe pushing her now, while she was in this state, would only make things worse.
’Let her simmer down for today.’
He would talk to her tomorrow.
She might have calmed down by then. ’Moreover, I did nothing wrong either way.’
He collected the plates, washed the dishes, and spent the rest of the afternoon, practicing his punching and fighting techniques in the backyard.
[I promised Mass release since last week but one thing or the other kept popping up.
I apologize for that.
Just wanted to say that I haven’t forgotten and it will be possible this week at least."

chapters.title: Chapter 176 | Scheming Brat
paragraphs: "Knock!" "Knock!" "Knock!"
Dexter heard a knock at the gate.
His Enhanced Hearing picked up the heartbeat before the knock even landed and he immediately knew who it was.
He sighed, cleaned up his hands from washing the plates and then walked out of the door, to the gate.
Tessa stood on the other side, grinning from ear to ear as her green eyes sparkled.
"So?" Dexter asked, leaning against the gate frame. "How did the food business go?"
Tessa’s grin widened as she batted her eyelashes, and placed both hands behind her back.
"Guess."
Dexter rolled his eyes.
He was not in the mood for guessing games.
Lyra’s strange behavior was still gnawing at the back of his mind, spoiling imhjs mood slightly.
He rubbed the bridge of his nose.
"Just tell me."
Tessa pouted at his bluntness. The pout lasted approximately two seconds before the grin broke through again.
"We sold out," she said. "All twenty portions. In under eight hours."
Dexter stared at her.
"Eight hours?"
"Eight hours, every single container was gone. The shelf was empty by 3 to 4 in the afternoon."
Dexter was stunned.

Eight hours was not something he had expected. He had prepared for the possibility that the meals would take two or three days to sell and had braced himself for the likelihood that most people in this neighborhood would take one look at the price, hesitate, and walk away.
He had been wrong.
People in this neighborhood had been willing to spend money on a meal made by a stranger for 5000 dollars which was insane.
The heaviness that had settled over him since the incident with Lyra’s diary lifted as he felt a hint of satisfaction.
As a chef, as a Foodsmith, there was no greater validation.
"I didn’t have your contact information," Tessa continued, rocking on her heels. "Otherwise I would have called you. Definitely. We probably could have sold ten more portions if we’d had them."

"A few people came in specifically asking if there was more. One man bought two portions. A woman from Elm Street bought one, and came back twenty minutes later asking if she could buy another. And then there was this one older guy."
She paused dramatically.

"He wanted to personally know who made the food. I had to come up with some sort of excuse about the chef being a private person who didn’t want to be identified. It took some convincing to make him leave."
Dexter nodded slowly. The man had probably felt the effect of the Grade One meal.
"Thank you, Tessa," Dexter said. "Seriously. Thank you for handling everything."
"You’re welcome, Boss Chef."
Dexter considered the numbers.
"I should increase the batch size," he said. "From twenty to thirty. Maybe even forty if I can manage the prep time."

Tessa nodded vigorously. "I was going to say thirty minimum. Maybe even fifty if you have the time. Mr. Thompson, you know, the retired hero two streets over? He bought a portion and loved it and also, Mrs. Alvarez. They want to buy more, regularly."
She paused, her expression shifting to something slightly more earnest.
"And some of them are quite curious about you."
Dexter shrugged. "I’m quite busy. Maybe another time."
Tessa’s eyes lit up with a new idea.

"There’s a festival this weekend," she said. "Well, more of a picnic, really. The whole neighborhood participates. It happens at Roland Stone Garden, which is close by. You and your wives could come. Meet everyone. Get to know the people around here."
Dexter blinked as he thought about it but then, he shook his head.
"I’ll probably be too busy to attend. But I’ll keep it in mind."

Tessa pouted again. This time the pout was genuine. "It would be really good if you came, Dexter. The neighbors aren’t as bad as you think. They’re just... cautious. They don’t know you yet. Once they do..."
She trailed off, leaving the implication hanging.
Then her expression shifted back to business.
"Okay, give me your account information. Let me transfer the funds."
Dexter nodded and recited his account number. Tessa typed it into her phone, double-checked the digits, and hit send.
Dexter’s phone buzzed in his pocket. He pulled it out and opened the notification.
[Transfer received: 90,000 credits]
[From: Tessa Wren]
[Available balance: 1,590,000 credits]
Dexter stared at the number.
Ninety thousand credits. In a single day. From twenty portions of food that he had cooked in less than two hours using ordinary ingredients and deliberately suppressed techniques.
The warmth in his chest expanded.

But then his Foodsmith mind, ever analytical, kicked in. He ran the numbers. Twenty portions. The price on the sign had been set at six thousand credits per portion, which Tessa had apparently adjusted upward from the original five hundred when she saw the demand. Twenty portions at six thousand credits each was one hundred and twenty thousand.
Not ninety thousand.
There was a thirty thousand credit discrepancy.
Dexter looked up from his phone. He stared at Tessa with narrowed eyes.
"Where is the rest of the money?"
Tessa smiled. It was the smile of a woman who had been waiting for this exact question and had prepared her answer in advance.
"That’s my commission."
Dexter’s eyes narrowed further. "Your commission?"
"For selling the food. Twenty-five percent."
"Twenty-five percent?"
"Yep."

Tessa crossed her arms and leaned against the gate post with her green eyes shinnng bright in amusement. She looked like a cat that had just stolen a fish and was daring the owner to say something about it.

"I sold the food," she said, ticking off points on her fingers. "I dealt with the customers. I handled the payments. I answered all their questions about the meals and what they did and how they worked. I protected your identity when people started asking who the chef was. And I personally dealt with four separate people who begged me for extra portions that didn’t exist."
She lowered her hand and pointed at herself proudly.
"Don’t you think I’m worth twenty-five percent?"

chapters.title: Chapter 177 | Forgive What?
paragraphs: Dexter stared at her for several seconds.
The girl was at most 17 and had negotiated a twenty-five percent commission on his product with such confidence that she wasn’t even slightly apologetic about it.
He thought about Mr. Henry.
He had schemed against the father. The daughter had schemed right back.
"You really are a little schemer," he said.
Tessa grinned in satisfaction.
"Learned from the best."
Dexter’s mouth twitched. He wanted to be annoyed but he couldn’t bring himself to be.
Because she was right, she had done the work, handled the customers, managed the transactions and protected his privacy.
Twenty-five percent was bit much but also fair.
"Get out," he said.
Tessa covered her mouth and let out a tickling giggle.
"See you tomorrow, Boss Chef!"
She turned and skipped down the sidewalk, her curly red hair bouncing with each step as she waved once over her shoulder without looking back.
Dexter shook his head and he looked down at his phone again.
His total balance was now 1,290,556 dollars.
He slipped the phone back into his pocket and walked inside.
Dinner time arrived.
Dexter stood at the kitchen, stirring the food as the aroma filled the entire house.
He was plating the food when he felt a presence behind him.
He turned around.
Lyra was there standing at the kitchen door.
She was staring at the with drolling mouth as her fingers twitched.
Dexter blinked as he glanced at her carefully. Her exprsssion wasn’t as cold as it was that afternoon.
And the stranger seemed to have disappeared bringing back the cute Lyra.
She seemed to have forgiven him. Or at least forgotten. Or at mthe she decided that whatever anger she had been carrying was less important than food.
Dexter wasn’t sure which. So he didn’t say anything and just smiled at her.
He served the stew into four bowls, arranged them on the small dining table, and stepped back.
"Sit do—"
Lyra was in her seat before he could even pull the chair out.
She sat down, picked up her spoon, and began eating without a word.
Dexter stared at her for a moment then he went to get Mira, wheeling her to the dining table while she cultivated in silence.
Then he went to the backyard for Selene.
She was on the swing with her eyes closed in cultivation.
"Selene. Dinner."
She opened her eyes and gently stood up. Then she walked toward him without hesitation.
She paused as she passed him.
"Smells good," she said quietly.
Dexter smiled. "It’s the bean stew. You’d like it."
Selene smiled faintly as they both walked tk the dining room.
The four of them ate silently together at the small dining table. The silence wasn’t awkward and it seemed they were lost in their own world as they ate.
Well, except for Lyra who was devouring the food rapidly.
One bowl. Gone.
She looked at Dexter and her melodious voice rang in his head.
’M-more.’
Dexter blinked and then stood up as he refilled refilled her bowl.
Less than a minute, it was all gone.
She blinked her eyes pitifully at Dexter, making Dexter smile.
"Alright."
This happened repeatedly until six bowls were all devoured!
Dexter’s eyebrows rose steadily with each refill.

Six full bowls of food was more than she had ever eaten in a single sitting. And she wasn’t slowing down. She was slowing up. Each bowl seemed to make her eat faster, as though she was trying to make up off the afternoon.
Finally, after the sixth bowl, she set her spoon down and leaned back in her chair.
"Sigh."
Her hands moved to her stomach, pressing gently against her full belly as a satisfied exhale escaped her lips.
Then she looked at Dexter.
’Thank you.’
Dexter’s brow furrowed slightly as she stood up and walked to the living room couch.
’She was angry at me all day, ate only one portion at lunch and didn’t speak to me for hours. And now she’s acting like nothing happened.’
He checked her status through his system reflexively.
[Lyra Vance — Shadow Corruption Level: 2%]
Still two percent. Stable. No increase.
’At least the corruption isn’t getting worse.’
He finished his own food, collected the dishes, and began washing them.

He turn turned back and could see Lyra on the couch. She had the Primordial Beast Egg cradled in her lap and her eyes were closed while her other rested on her belly, patting it gently as she cultivated.
Dexter shook his head with a quiet smile.
He finished the dishes, dried his hands, and walked to the living room.
Lyra was still on the couch.
Dexter looked at her and spoke as he also projected his surface thought loudly.
"I assume you aren’t angry anymore," he said quietly.
Lyra’s eyes snapped open. She looked at him through her AI glasses, as her dark eyes blinking with what appeared to be genuine confusion.
’Why would I be angry?’
Her telepathic voice was innocent and slightly baffled as she stared at Dexter in puzzlement.
Dexter stared at her.
"This afternoon," he said. "With the diary matter."
Lyra blinked and her brows furrowed cutely.
"About this afternoon?" she repeated, her voice carrying nothing but confusion.
Dexter’s frown deepened.
It doesn’t seem like she was pretending.
’Did she genuinely forget?’
If Lyra didn’t want to remember, then it was better wasn’t it?
Moreover, he didn’t want her to be even more annoyed by bringing up the past.
"Forget it," he said, shaking his head. "It’s nothing."
Lyra stared at him for a moment longer. Then she shrugged, closed her eyes, and resumed cultivating.
After dinner, the girls drifted to their respective spaces.
Dexter went to his room and sat cross-legged on his bed, and exhaled slowly.
It had been a long day and a productive ine at that.
But even with all that, he still needed to cultivate and grow stronger so he could take care of himself and the girls.
But before he could begin, the system spoke.
[Ding!]

paragraphs: [10,000x Investment System Activated]
[Calculating daily investment returns...]
[Multiplier: 100x]
[Investment 1 — Protecting Mira]

[Action: Host shielded Mira Calloway from emotional and physical threat posed by hostile family visitor. Host absorbed Mira’s chronic pain via Ring of Shared Burdens and provided ongoing medical care through massage therapy and Grade-4 Enchanted Meals.]
[Return: Ultra Violet Protection Earring — Type 3Artifact]
A black stud earring that automatically protects the wearer against attacks from a Peak Ultra-Rank opponent. It can completely nullify three such attacks before its protective energy is exhausted.
[Investment 2 — Suppressing Selene’s Eternal Winter Ice]

[Action: Host activated Abyssal Flame to provide warmth for Selene Frost during shared cultivation session. Host endured three hours of immobile sitting to avoid disturbing Selene’s sleep. Host’s body heat suppressed the Internal Winter Ice throughout the night, allowing Selene her first pain-free rest in three years.]
[Return: Cold and Frost Resistance (Permanent) — 20%]
[Investment 3 — Caring for Mira]

[Action: Host performed 108 Body Massage Sutra on Mira Calloway using Shockwave Glove and Grade-4 Spiritual Massage Oil. Host channeled mana into damaged nerve pathways, stimulated dormant muscles, and provided sustained physical therapy over multiple sessions.]
[Return: Joy and Harmony Acupuncture Technique]

A peculiar acupuncture technique that stimulates specific acupoints throughout the body, triggering intense relaxation and pleasure. It has no healing effect and is purely designed to induce bodily comfort and pleasure.
[Investment 4 — Caring for His Wives]

[Action: Host provided sustained daily care for all three wives including cooking, cleaning, bathing assistance, medical treatment, emotional support, and household maintenance over an extended period without compensation or complaint.]
[Return: Lifespan Extension — One Additional Year]
[Investment 5 — Seeking a New Source of Income]

[Action: Host established business partnership with local bakery, prepared and sold 20 Grade-One Enchanted Meals to generate independent income for household support. Host deliberately suppressed own abilities to produce affordable meals suited to neighborhood economic conditions.]
[Return: Arcane Nutrition Insight — Passive Ability]

A passive knowledge ability that allows Dexter to identify the nutritional, restorative, and energy-boosting properties of any ingredient on sight. It also allows him to determine which ordinary, non-spiritual ingredients can be combined to create meals that provide minor but genuine benefits.
Effects include:
Improved stamina
Faster recovery from exhaustion
Better cultivation efficiency
Slightly improved concentration
Temporary resistance to fatigue
[Investment 6 — Repairing the Broken Window]

[Action: Host personally repaired damage to family home caused by hostile visitor. Host purchased materials, installed new window frame, fitted replacement glass, patched interior wall, and painted surrounding area to restore the living space for his wives.]
[Return: Type-3 Pure-Air Fragrance Artifact]

A small decorative artifact that releases a faint, pleasant fragrance throughout the house. It continuously filters dust and impurities from the air, removes unpleasant odors, reduces airborne pollutants, freshens the entire house, and maintains clean, breathable air for all occupants.
The artifact can operate continuously for one full year before needing to be replaced or recharged.
Reading the first notification, dexter flipped his hands and an simple black earring materialized in his palm.

Although it looked simple, it actually contained the power to nullify three full attacks of a Peak Ultra-Rank attack. That was the kind of defensive artifact that could save his life when placed in a desperate situation.
If he had this during the outbreak at the market district, he might have been more bold with his attacks.
The three girls already had their own defensive equipment. This one, he would keep for himself.
He immediately placed it in his ears. While he didn’t know how he looked, it should be quite alright right?
And maybe he would look even handsome. ’What would Mira, Lyra and Selene say?’
Before he knew it, his train of thought went to what his wives would think of it.
He laughed softly and shook his head to remove his thoughts from them. Then accepted his second reward.
20% permanent resistance to ice? It wasn’t necessary needed as he had a high ranking flames but if he came into contract with an ultra rank ice user, then maybe it would prove useful.
Since all attacks involving extreme cold, freezing temperatures, or ice-based energy will have their effectiveness reduced by twenty percent against him.
Dexter flexed his fingers but didn’t feel much of a change but he noticed even without his heavenly flame heating his blood, there wasn’t a shred of coldness in his body.
When it came to the Joy And Harmony Acupuncture Technique, Dexter ea stunned and read the notification twice.
’Pleasure.’
’Purely designed to induce bodily comfort and pleasure.’
’No healing effect.’
His face went through several expressions in rapid succession as he finally figured out what the system meant.
’First the contraceptive capsules. Now this.’
’What exactly does the system think I am doing with my wives?’
He pressed his palms against his face and groaned quietly into the darkness of his room.
’I am a Foodsmith. A husband who is trying his best to take care of three wives in peace. I am not running some kind of pleasure palace.’
He shoved the technique’s knowledge into the back of his mind.
Then his next return which was an additional year of lifespan.
Dexter lowered his hands from his face and blinked at the notification.
One year of life, just like that? He had thought he would receive a year of cultivation, not lifespan.
But every human being, no matter how powerful, was bound by the finite length of their life. One additional year meant one more year to live longer.
Although he didn’t think his lifespan was low but having additional life span wasn’t bad.
He accepted it without hesitation.
The next was the ability: Arcane Nutritional Insight.

Dexter’s eyes widened as the knowledge integrated into his mind. While he had a bit of this ability due to his high level foodsmith and his Heavenly Gastronomy Body, this ability would make him gain more insights into materials.
He could create an entire menu of affordable, beneficial meals tailored to different needs.
His mind was already racing through recipe combinations when the final notification appeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 179 | Joy And Harmony Acupuncture Technique
paragraphs: The last reward was the Pure-Air Fragrance.
Dexter accepted the reward and watched as a small object materialized on his palm.
It was a delicate ceramic lotus flower, no larger than a teacup, painted in soft shades of white and pale blue.
The petals were slightly open, revealing a tiny crystal set into the center that glowed faintly.

The moment it touched his skin, he felt a gentle, almost imperceptible wave of clean, fresh air radiated outward from the lotus as it released a subtle, clean freshness that reminded him of mountain air after a spring rain.
’This is actually really nice.’
He walked out of his room, holding the lotus and placed it behind the curtain.
The effect was immediate and noticeable.
The air in the bungalow, which had been carrying the lingering smells of cooking oil, paint and plaster dust, began to clear but by bit, like opening a window in a stuffy room.
Dexter stood in the hallway and breathed in.
He thought about his wives that loved their spots. it should help with the circulation of their breathing.
Dexter smiled as he returned happily to his room.
On his bed, he surfed through the internet dir random stuffs, reading various articles, dungeon outbreaks and even invitations to join a squad to enter a Dimensional Gate together.
His thumb paused on the billboard photo he had taken earlier that afternoon.
Dexter stared at the number for a moment then held the number and clicked the press call option.
The line rang three times before someone picked up.
"Harvest Homes, this is Jennifer speaking. How may I help you?"
"Good evening," Dexter said. "I saw your billboard advertisement on the main highway. I’m interested in learning about your available properties."

"Of course, sir. We have a wide range of options available. Residential homes, townhouses, estate properties, and undeveloped land parcels in various districts throughout Stargate City. I can email you our current catalog with pricing details and specifications, or..."
She paused.

"It would actually be preferable for you to visit our office in person. We can discuss your needs face to face, review floor plans, and I can walk you through the financing options available for others and also licensed heroes."
Dexter considered it as it would take him away from the girls.
But this was important and was about their future.
"Can I come tomorrow morning?" he asked. "Around ten?
"Ten o’clock works perfectly. May I have your name?"
"Dexter Ashford."
The line paused for a bit as a something clicked in Jennifer’s mind.
"Thank you, Mr. Ashford. I’ll have everything prepared for your visit. Do you need directions?"
"I’ll find it."
"Excellent. We’ll see you tomorrow at ten."
The call ended.
Dexter set the phone down and immediately thought of something else.
Plasmatic Man had called yesterday about meeting with a potential squad. Dexter had told him he would text back with his availability. He had forgotten about it until now.
He picked up the phone, saved Cole’s number, and typed a quick message.
[Available tomorrow at 12 PM. Let me know if that works for you.]
He didn’t wait for a response. He placed the phone face-down on the nightstand, closed his eyes, and began cultivating.
Tomorrow’s schedule was going to be busy.
He needed to make 50 portions of meals, also, ten o’clock at Harvest Homes, twelve o’clock with Cole and the others.
He had been cultivating for roughly an hour when he heard a familiar heartbeat.
His bedroom door opened slowly and the air in the room shifted as the temperature dropped by several degrees in seconds.
Dexter smiled.
’She’s early.’
Last night, Selene had come to his room around late midnight, but tonight, it was barely 11 and she was here.
He had half expected her to come even later tonight, embarrassed by the fact that she had fallen asleep on his shoulder that morning.
Instead, she had come earlier.
’She’s getting comfortable.’
Dexter kept his eyes closed and didn’t acknowledge her presence as he simply continued cultivating, giving her the space to settle in on her own terms.
Selene’s footsteps were soft as she walked to the bed but then, stopped.
Dexter opened his eye and smiled at her, gesturing with his arms pointing to the bed.
Then he closed his eye and erupted with his heavenly flames as he resumed cultivating.
Selene couldn’t see but with her talent, she ’saw’ his gesture and knew he trying his best not to make things uncomfortable.
She slowly sat down on the edge of the bed, raised her white, pale legs, crossed them beneath her, and settled into her meditation posture.
Themn she closed her eyes and then her cultivation began.

Mana flowed into the room from the surrounding air, drawn by the combined gravitational pull of their respective Star Nodes. The energy pooled around them like water filling a basin, warm and golden from Dexter’s side, cool and silver from Selene’s.
Thirty minutes passed.
Dexter suddenly opened his eyes and shifted his position.
He moved across the bed toward Selene as though he was simply adjusting his posture for comfort.
He only stopped when his knees were almost touching hers, their crossed legs forming a small diamond of space between them.
Selene didn’t need to open where eyes to see and her ears turned slightly pink as she felt the heat from his knees flowed directly to her lower body.
Dexter increased the heat radiating from his body, just enough so it won’t ignite the surrounding space.
They cultivated in silence.
Another thirty minutes passed and Dexter shifted again.
This time, he moved directly beside her.
Their shoulders touched and the sides of their knees pressed together.
With this position, the heat from his body flowed directly into hers through the points of contact.

Her shoulder, her arm and her knee. The warmth seeped through her thin sleeping clothes and into her skin, spreading through her damaged meridians and pushing back the Internal Winter Ice that lived beneath the surface.
Selene’s ears went from pink to red.
But she didn’t pull away.
Instead, she let out a slow, quiet breath. The kind of exhale that comes from a body finally letting go of tension it has been holding for so long that it forgot what relaxation felt like.
"Thank you," she murmured.
The words were barely audible but Dexter heard it.
Dexter didn’t respond and simply continued cultivating as he warmed her body.
They cultivated through the night.

chapters.title: Chapter 180 | You’re Insane...
paragraphs: Sometime past midnight, Selene’s head drifted sideways and rested directly on Dexter’s shoulder. Her silver-white hair spilled across his arm as her breathing slowed.
A few minutes later, her hands actually found his as her fingers closed around his arm, snuggling and cuddling his arm like a koala and Dexter was awake through all of it.
And then, unbidden, unwanted, and thoroughly unhelpful, his mind drifted to a particular system reward he had received earlier that evening.
’Joy and Harmony Acupuncture Technique.’
’Purely designed to induce bodily comfort and pleasure.’
Heat started to rise within his body.

Not the Abyssal Flame kind of heat. Not the mana-circulation kind of heat. A different kind entirely. One that had nothing to do with cultivation and everything to do with the fact that a beautiful woman was pressed against his side, her fingers wrapped around his arm, her hair brushing against his neck.
Dexter inhaled sharply through his nose.
’Don’t. Do not. Do not even think about it.’
He activated his breathing technique, forcing his mana circulation into a slower, deeper pattern to calm his mind and it helped slightly. .
’Just calm down. You’ve seen OnlyHeroes, done somethings, so you should be resistant to this.’
But his body was not listening to his mind with the same fidelity it usually demonstrated. The warmth continued to build as something within him started to rise.
’Just the thought is getting a rise out of you.’
He almost slapped himself.
’If she kissed you, what would you do?’
He rapidly thought about something else. Mira’s sister.
It helped.
For about ten minutes.
Then Selene shifted in her sleep, her head sliding from his shoulder to his chest, her body curling slightly toward his warmth. Her grip on his arm tightened.
"Sigh."
A quiet, content sound escaped her lips.
Dexter eyes trembled and he stared at the ceiling with the wide, unblinking eyes of a man enduring a trial of temptation.
He gritted his teeth as he glared at the air. It was this goddam system that placed useless thoughts in his mind.
First was the pill, then the glove and now the jog and harmony acupuncture technique.
’I am going to kill the system.’
He barely survived the night through stubbornness and willpower that rival’s that of John-wick.
"Ring! Ring! Ring!"
The alarm shattered the silence at 5:00 AM.
Dexter’s eyes snapped open.
Selene’s eyes snapped open.
For a brief, disorienting moment, neither of them moved.
Then Selene processed her situation.
Her head was on his chest, not on his shoulder but on his chest and her arm was wrapped around his waist as her body pressed against his side, curled into him like a vine clinging to a tree trunk.
Even her leg had somehow ended up draped across his knee.
She was, for all practical purposes, attached to him like a koala on a tree.
"W-what...?"
Selene’s face went from zero to crimson in half a second as she released him so fast it was as though his skin had been made of hot iron.

She scrambled backward on the bed, her hands slapping against the mattress, her silver hair flying in every direction. Her pale eyes were wide. Her lips were parted. Her entire face was the color of a ripe tomato.
She turned toward the door. Took two steps and then stopped.
Her hand gripped the door frame.
She stood there for a moment, her back to him, her shoulders tight, her ears burning.
"Thank you and I’m really sorry i did that, Dexter. It won’t happen again." she stuttered but sounded solemn.
Dexter was stunned and before she could leave he immediately spoke up.
"I don’t mind."
Selene who was planning to leave suddenly froze.
Dexter immediately relayed himself. "I truly don’t mind. As long as it makes you comfortable? I’d do anything to help you."
As he spoke those words, Selene’s body trembled. And she froze for a while before she muttered.
"Because it’s your responsibility, right?"
Dexter immediately nodded his head. "Yes.
Selene breathing paused and it seemed she didn’t receive the answer she wanted but Dexter voice continued.
"At the beginning, yes. I did it because it was my responsibility, but now, I’m doing it because of another reason entirely."
Hos words were sincere and although Selene couldn’t see, her Takent could see every inch of his face. Every expression he made and she knew he was been serious.
Selene turned her head slightly towards him and let out an extremely beautiful smile.
"You’re insane."
With that, she immediately left his room.
Dexter was stunned and he scratched his head. ’What does she mean by that? Is it a good thigh or a bad thing.’
He smiled and shook his head, exhaling as he stretched his arms above his head.
His spine popped, his neck cracked twice and his shoulders groaned. He hadn’t moved for about 5 hours.
Because a beautiful woman had been sleeping on him and he had been too stubborn and too respectful to disturb her.
He stood up, stretched again, then he looked at the clock.
He had a lot to do today.
He stood at the kitchen counter, sleeves rolled to his elbows, and began prepping. He used only ordinary ingredients like yesterday.
His Arcane Nutrition Insight passive ability made the process remarkably efficient.
’Carrots. High in beta-carotene. When combined with ginger, produces a mild stamina recovery effect lasting ninety minutes.’
’Grade One beast meat. Moderate protein density. Low mana content. When seared and paired with soy sauce, enhances physical recovery rate by six percent for two hours.’
’Onions. Trace sulfur compounds. When caramelized, improves absorption of accompanying nutrients by eight percent.’
He didn’t need to think about what would work and what wouldn’t. The knowledge simply existed, guiding his hands as he chopped, seasoned, and stirred with practiced efficiency.
He used the large ordinary pot, without heavenly flame. Just heat, oil, and technique deliberately dialed back to produce food that was good without being extraordinary.
By 6:30 AM, the first batch was done.

I did it because it was my responsibility, but now, I’m doing it because of another reason entirely."
Hos words were sincere and although Selene couldn’t see, her Takent could see every inch of his face.
Every expression he made and she knew he was been serious.
Selene turned her head slightly towards him and let out an extremely beautiful smile.
"You’re insane."
With that, she immediately left his room.
Dexter was stunned and he scratched his head. ’What does she mean by that?
Is it a good thigh or a bad thing.’
He smiled and shook his head, exhaling as he stretched his arms above his head.
His spine popped, his neck cracked twice and his shoulders groaned.
He hadn’t moved for about 5 hours.
Because a beautiful woman had been sleeping on him and he had been too stubborn and too respectful to disturb her.
He stood up, stretched again, then he looked at the clock.
He had a lot to do today.
He stood at the kitchen counter, sleeves rolled to his elbows, and began prepping.
He used only ordinary ingredients like yesterday.
His Arcane Nutrition Insight passive ability made the process remarkably efficient.
’Carrots.
High in beta-carotene.
When combined with ginger, produces a mild stamina recovery effect lasting ninety minutes.’
’Grade One beast meat.
Moderate protein density.
Low mana content.
When seared and paired with soy sauce, enhances physical recovery rate by six percent for two hours.’
’Onions.
Trace sulfur compounds.
When caramelized, improves absorption of accompanying nutrients by eight percent.’
He didn’t need to think about what would work and what wouldn’t.
The knowledge simply existed, guiding his hands as he chopped, seasoned, and stirred with practiced efficiency.
He used the large ordinary pot, without heavenly flame.
Just heat, oil, and technique deliberately dialed back to produce food that was good without being extraordinary.
By 6:30 AM, the first batch was done.

chapters.title: Chapter 181 | Kissing...
paragraphs: Dexter was halfway through the second batch when he felt a presence behind him.
He turned around and suddenly saw Lyra was standing at the kitchen door.
Her dark eyes were fixed on the gas cooker with thirst.
The food smelled amazing.
She looked at Dexter as she formed a pout of such devastating proportions that it could have ended wars.
Dexter scratched the back of his head.
"Sorry, Lyra. I haven’t made your food yet. I’m still cooking for the customers. Just give me about thirty minutes and I’ll be done."
Lyra’s pout deepened and her eyes grew wider as she looked so cute and pitiful.
Her shoulders dropped as she turned around saddened and began walking back to the living room.
Dexter watched her go and couldn’t help but sigh.
Suddenly, he flipped his hand and two bags of Sminley Chips materialized in his palm.
Then three Celestial Pastries also appeared beside it making everything smell like a bakery in heaven.
Lyra had already turned the corner when the smell traveled directly into her nose.
She immediately froze mid-step as her nose flared and she unconsciously inhaled deeply.
She suddenly turned her as her body rotated like a compass needle finding north and she was back in the kitchen doorway in less than two seconds.
Her eyes locked onto the chips and pastries in Dexter’s hand and the pout vanished as her lips curled up into an expectatant smile.
"Whoosh!"
She flash stepped across the kitchen with a speed that stunned even Dexter himself.
That speed actually rival Flame Burst step!
Her hands shot out and snatched the entire haul from Dexter’s palm like a pickpocket who had been doing this since birth.
She clutched the chips and pastries against her chest. Her arms wrapped around them protectively as her dark eyes looked up at him.
And she smiled.
It was, without exaggeration, the most brilliant smile Dexter had ever seen on Lyra’s face.
Then, before Dexter could react, she leaned forward.
She was almost his height so she didn’t need to tiptoe as she tilted her head to the side and suddenly, pressed her lips against his cheek.
A warm soft sensation touched against Dexter’s cheeks. If lasted for half a second as she then pulled back.
Her eyes widened.
The smile froze on her face as the realization of what she had just done crashed into her consciousness with the force of a freight train.
Her face instantly went red, climbing for her neck, consuming her cheeks, her ears, her forehead, and the back of her head.
She spun around, clutching her chips and pastries against her chest like a dragon guarding its hoard, and fled the kitchen.
Her bare feet slapped against the hallway floor. Her bedroom door slammed shut a moment later.
Dexter stood alone in the kitchen, a spatula in one hand, his other hand still extended in the air where the snacks had been.
He stared at the empty doorway.
His cheek tingled where her lips had touched.

The faint irritation he had been carrying since the diary incident, the lingering frustration from Lyra’s cold behavior the previous afternoon, the confusion about the voice that was almost hers but not quite.
All of it vanished.
Melted like snow in sunlight.

Something warm bloomed in his chest. Not the heat of his Flame Demon Bloodline. Not the mana warmth of his Abyssal Flame. Something quieter. Softer. Something that spread through his ribs like warm honey and settled there with a gentle, persistent glow.
The tips of his ears turned red.
His eyes blinked rapidly. Twice. Three times.
He inhaled sharply through his nose and held the breath for a long moment.
Then he exhaled slowly.
And smiled.
"These women," he muttered to himself, shaking his head as he turned back to the stove. "All of them. Every single one. They’re going to be the death of me.
He continued cooking.
By 7:15 AM, the fifty portions were done.

He had actually made fifty-five. Five extra, just in case. Each container was packed, sealed, and stacked neatly in his spatial storage. Fifty-five portions of Grade One Enchanted Meal. Comfort Chicken Rice with vegetables. Nothing fancy. Nothing that would attract heavenly tribulations. Just good, affordable food that would give ordinary people a genuine boost in their daily lives.
Then he turned his attention to the girls’ breakfast.
This was different. This was not for customers. This was for his wives.
He pulled out the good ingredients. Diamond Rice. Fresh vegetables. Premium chicken breast. A thin slice of Millennium Blood Ginseng. A single drop of Star Essence Serum.
His Arcane Nutrition Insight worked overtime, mapping combinations and calculating effects as he moved through the kitchen with the focused intensity of a man performing surgery.

The Type-II Spirit Cooking Pot came out. The heavenly flame ignited. His Great Grandmaster Foodsmith techniques activated fully, every movement precise and deliberate, every ingredient placed with the care of a master painter applying brushstrokes to canvas.
The kitchen filled with an aroma so rich and complex that even the walls seemed to lean closer.
[Ding! Congratulations! You have successfully created Celestial Dawn Nectar Bowl (Grade 5)]

’’[Effect: Permanently strengthens physical constitution. Accelerates meridian repair by 35%. Boosts mana regeneration for 6 hours. Induces deep cellular healing. Removes accumulated fatigue toxins.]’’
Grade Five.

Dexter stared at the notification. He hadn’t intentionally aimed for Grade Five. It had simply happened. The combination of premium ingredients, his upgraded cooking skills, and the Arcane Nutrition Insight had pushed the meal a grade higher than he thought would come out.
Also, there was no dark clouds gathered outside nor was there any heavenly thunder rumbling in the skies.
The meal’s energy was dense but was contained within the food rather than radiating outward.
The Grade Five threshold for atmospheric disturbance was higher than Grade Four, and this dish sat comfortably below it.

He plated four bowls. Each one glowed faintly with a warm, golden luminescence. Thin wisps of steam rose in lazy spirals, carrying a scent that was simultaneously savory, sweet, and deeply comforting.
He carried them to the dining table.

chapters.title: Chapter 182 | Taming The Dragon
paragraphs: After he was done with the meal, Dexter went to get Mira.
He walked to the bedroom and found her in her wheelchair with her eyes closed, cultivating.
"Mira. Bath time."
She opened one eye. Looked at him. Closed it.
"Give me a moment."
"Nop."
He ignored her glare as he wheeled her to the bathroom, carefully undressed her, and carried her to the shower.
He turned on the warm water, adjusted the temperature, and placed her on the shower bench.
Then he began bathing her, starting with her shoulders, using the same routine.

He usually kept his mind occupied with Cultivation techniques, recipe combinations, dungeon strategies and breathing patterns. Anything that could fill his thoughts and keep his mind detached from what he was currently doing.
Today, it didn’t work.
The mental firewall he had rebuilt overnight had been damaged by Selene’s touch and Lyra’s kiss that morning, and the residual cracks were letting things through.
He was washing Mira when he noticed her skin.

He had always noticed it, of course. You couldn’t bathe another human being daily without being aware of their physical form. But there was a difference between awareness and noticing things that made your heart pound and your breathing trembling.
Mira’s skin was pale, not pale like Selene’s skin but pale with tiny cute barely seen freckles on her skin.
As he touched her skin, he realized it was incredibly soft beneath his fingers as the soft sponge moved across her shoulders, softer than anything he had ever touched.
He noticed the way the warm water traced paths down her back. The way it followed the subtle curves of her spine, pooling briefly in the hollow above her hip before continuing downward.

He noticed her wet crimson hair as it darkened to the color of blood, clinging to her neck and shoulders. The color was so vivid and red that it didn’t look real. It looked like something painted by an artist who had been given access to colors that didn’t exist in nature.
He started to take notice of even the tiniest things.
The tiny mole just above her upper lip, no larger than the head of a pin. It made her beauty stand out to perfection.
The faint barely visible dusting of freckles across the bridge of her nose.
Her slender and graceful hands. The neat and unpolished nails, her long collarbones that had faint blue traces of veins beneath the surface.
Her full lips which was strangely red as it parted as she breathed. The lower lip was slightly fuller than the upper, giving her mouth a natural pout that she probably wasn’t aware of.
Everything about her was extraordinary.
And he couldn’t stop noticing.
’Dammit! What am I thinking? Think about literally anything other than the cute freckles on her nose, the mole above her lip and the way her hair looks when it’s wet.’
Shocker, it didn’t work.
The observations kept coming, unbidden, relentless, each one more detailed than the last.

Mira seemed entirely oblivious to his internal crisis. She passively closed her eyes, her expression holding its usual mask of calm indifference. If she noticed that his hands were moving faster than normal, or that his breathing was slightly more controlled than usual.
Dexter finished washing her as quickly as he could without being obvious about the haste.
He dried her, dressed her, pulled a fresh blouse over her head and began buttoning it.
His fingers fumbled and in his rush, he missed a button.
The second buttonhole went into the third button. The third into the fourth. The entire alignment was off by one, creating a subtle but noticeable asymmetry in the blouse’s fit.
Dexter didn’t notice.
He placed Mira in her wheelchair, wheeled her to the dining room, parked her at the table, and left.
Lyra and Selene were already there but Dexter did not put food on anyone’s plate.
He immediately left the dining room and walked directly to his bedroom, closed the door behind him, and stood in the center of the room with his hands pressed against his face.
’Calm...’
He activated his breathing technique and tried to calm himself. Then burning heat inside of him seemed to reduce slightly.
Then he walked to the bathroom, turned the cold water tap on full blast, and splashed his face about six times before the rising dragon was successfully tamed.
He looked at his reflection. ’Pervert,’
He sighed, dried his face, straightened his shirt, and walked back to the dining room.
The three girls were seated at the table. All three were looking at him with variations of the same expression.
Mira’s brow was furrowed. She had already noticed the missed button and her Spectral Arms were already correcting it.

Selene’s head was tilted slightly, her pale eyes aimed in his direction. Through her Echolocation, she had likely detected the elevated heart rate, the irregular breathing, and the hurried movements that were so unlike his usual calm demeanor.
Lyra blinked her eyes as she stared wide eyes at Dexter while eating her chips at the same time.
Dexter let out an awkward smile.
"Sorry about that, something urgent came up."
He didn’t explain further as he walked to the kitchen, ladled the Celestial Dawn Nectar Bowl into four serving bowls, and placed them on the table.
The moment the bowls touched the table, the aroma filled the room.
All three girls looked down at their bowls.
Mira’s Spectral Arms paused mid-button-correction. Her nostrils flared as her crimson eyes widened by a fraction.
Selene tilted her head further, her pale lips parting slightly as the scent reached her.
Lyra set down her chips.
For Lyra to voluntarily set down chips in the presence of food was, by itself, a miracle of biblical proportions.
Everyday that Dexter cooked for them, he always seems to stun them with his astonishing cooking skill.
Day by day, his skill kept on increasing rapidly as though he had no limit and right now, today’s food seemed to be even better than yesterday’s food.
Even in their homes, while they ate Arcane meals everyday, Dexter food beats everything they had tsted back at their family homes.
