chapters.title: Chapter 183 | You’re Important To me
paragraphs: ’Sorry I ran off because I couldn’t stop thinking about you girls?’
Nop, that sentence would never leave his mouth under any circumstances short of torture.

He was trying his best not to lie to his wives. He had learned, through bitter experience and the slow, painful process of building trust with three traumatized women, that secrets were the termites that ate through the foundation of any relationship.
But, some things were better left unsaid.
They ate in silence as the girls enjoyed their meal.
Mira kept glancing at him and she was subtle about it.
But Dexter noticed every single one and he said nothing.
He kept his attention on his food. He had gotten very good at pretending he didn’t notice things over the past few weeks.
Lyra was buried in her food. She wasn’t even trying to savor the taste. She was simply inhaling the food like a vacuum.
Selene closed her eyes as she ate quietly.
Halfway through the meal, Dexter remembered something.
"Oh," he said, setting down his spoon. "While I go deliver the meals to Tessa’s father’s bakery, I also have a few errands to run."
The girls glaced at him but continued eating.
"One involves getting a new place," Dexter continued. "And the other involves the monster outbreak I participated in recently."
"Whoosh!"
All three of them stopped eating immediately and simultaneously. As though someone had pressed a pause button on the entire room.
Lyra’s spoon froze mid-scoop. Selene’s hand stopped halfway to her mouth. Mira’s Spectral Arms went rigid.
Three heads immediately lifted as the pairs of eyes locked onto Dexter with the intensity of mothers hearing the word "hospital" in a phone call about their child.
Dexter quickly raised his hand and clarified.

"Don’t worry," he said, letting out a small, reassuring smile. "While it is regarding the monster outbreak, it has nothing to do with participating in another one. I just want to meet with the comrades I fought alongside. Discuss a few things with them. That’s all."
Lyra and Selene held his gaze for a moment longer. Then, slowly, they put their heads back down and resumed eating.
Mira did not.
She continued looking at him, her crimson eyes searching his face as though not entirely satisfied with the explanation but had decided not to press the issue.
Dexter met her gaze for a beat, then returned to his food.
Lyra finished first.
She stood up, carried her bowl to the sink and walked to the living room couch where the Primordial Beast Egg was there.
Selene finished second. She placed her spoon neatly beside her bowl, stood up, and drifted toward the backyard.
Then it was just Mira and Dexter.

Dexter had finished his own food several minutes ago. He was sitting at the table, waiting for Mira to finish so he could collect the plates and head out. His schedule was tight. Delivery to the bakery. Housing agent at ten. Squad meeting at twelve. Every minute he spent sitting here was a minute he didn’t have.
But he waited for his wives to finish eating first.
Mira’s Spectral Arms continued feeding her. The movements were becoming smoother each day, the mana limbs responding to her mental commands with increasing precision.
Then suddenly, the spoon stopped.
The Spectral Arm holding it lowered the utensil to the bowl as the spoon clattered softly against the ceramic.
Mira looked directly at Dexter.
Dexter blinked.
"Are you not going to continue eating?" he asked, raising an eyebrow.
Mira didn’t answer immediately as she held his gaze. Her crimson eyes studied his face as thd silence stretched.
Five seconds, ten seconds, fifteen.
Dexter began to feel slightly uncomfortable under the weight of her stare. He opened his mouth to say something but Mira spoke first.
"What is happening with you?"
Dexter blinked. "What do you mean?"
Mira raised an eyebrow as she gave him a look.
"You’ve been acting a bit weird with me. So tell me. What is happening with you?"
Her brows suddenly furrowed as she spoke. "Are you finally tired? Am I being too much of a burden?"
The last question landed in the quiet kitchen like a stone dropped into still water.
Dexter’s expression changed slightly and his gaze turned serious as he shook his head.
"I have never seen you as a burden," he coldly and seriously. "And I need you to stop calling yourself that.
Mira’s lips parted slightly. She hadn’t expected that tone.
"Any man who got married to you and called you a burden would be the stupidest person alive."
He held her gaze and his eyes were steady, his voice was firm.
"So stop calling yourself that."
He paused.
"You are important to me. You, Lyra, and Selene. You three are the most important people in my life right now. And that is not going to change."
The kitchen was very quiet.
Mira stared at him.
She had expected him to respond, had expected reassurance and had expected him to say something kind and move on. A quick "of course not" and a change of subject.
She had not expected this.
She had not expected him to look at her with that expression, speak with that conviction and say the words with the kind of absolute, unshakable certainty that left no room for doubt.
The words had stunned her.
She couldn’t say anything as her throat tightened and her crimson eyes, which could cut steel on a normal day, had gone slightly wide.
Her lips suddenly curled upward.
Then she immediately turned her head away, refusing to meet his gaze. Her ears had turned pink. Her Spectral Arms had retracted behind her back, disappearing completely.
Dexter chuckled softly.
He stood up, reached across the table, and picked up her bowl.
As he turned toward the kitchen.
But before he could take more than a few steps, he felt something grip his wrist.
Dexter smiled and looked down
But then, his entire body went rigid as his face changed drastically with wide-eyed shock. His jaw tightened, his eyes widened and his pupils contracted.
The grip on his wrist was warm, small, soft and strong.
Dexter looked down and his body trembled.

Selene closed her eyes as she ate quietly.
Halfway through the meal, Dexter remembered something.
"Oh," he said, setting down his spoon.
"While I go deliver the meals to Tessa’s father’s bakery, I also have a few errands to run."
The girls glaced at him but continued eating.
"One involves getting a new place," Dexter continued.
"And the other involves the monster outbreak I participated in recently."
"Whoosh!"
All three of them stopped eating immediately and simultaneously.
As though someone had pressed a pause button on the entire room.
Lyra’s spoon froze mid-scoop.
Selene’s hand stopped halfway to her mouth.
Mira’s Spectral Arms went rigid.
Three heads immediately lifted as the pairs of eyes locked onto Dexter with the intensity of mothers hearing the word "hospital" in a phone call about their child.
Dexter quickly raised his hand and clarified.
"Don’t worry," he said, letting out a small, reassuring smile.
"While it is regarding the monster outbreak, it has nothing to do with participating in another one.
I just want to meet with the comrades I fought alongside.
Discuss a few things with them.
That’s all."
Lyra and Selene held his gaze for a moment longer.
Then, slowly, they put their heads back down and resumed eating.
Mira did not.
She continued looking at him, her crimson eyes searching his face as though not entirely satisfied with the explanation but had decided not to press the issue.
Dexter met her gaze for a beat, then returned to his food.
Lyra finished first.
She stood up, carried her bowl to the sink and walked to the living room couch where the Primordial Beast Egg was there.
Selene finished second.
She placed her spoon neatly beside her bowl, stood up, and drifted toward the backyard.
Then it was just Mira and Dexter.
Dexter had finished his own food several minutes ago.
He was sitting at the table, waiting for Mira to finish so he could collect the plates and head out.
His schedule was tight.
Delivery to the bakery.
Housing agent at ten.
Squad meeting at twelve.
Every minute he spent sitting here was a minute he didn’t have.
But he waited for his wives to finish eating first.
Mira’s Spectral Arms continued feeding her.
The movements were becoming smoother each day, the mana limbs responding to her mental commands with increasing precision.
Then suddenly, the spoon stopped.
The Spectral Arm holding it lowered the utensil to the bowl as the spoon clattered softly against the ceramic.
Mira looked directly at Dexter.
Dexter blinked.
"Are you not going to continue eating?" he asked, raising an eyebrow.
Mira didn’t answer immediately as she held his gaze.
Her crimson eyes studied his face as thd silence stretched.
Five seconds, ten seconds, fifteen.
Dexter began to feel slightly uncomfortable under the weight of her stare.
He opened his mouth to say something but Mira spoke first.
"What is happening with you?"
Dexter blinked.
"What do you mean?"
Mira raised an eyebrow as she gave him a look.
"You’ve been acting a bit weird with me.
So tell me.
What is happening with you?"
Her brows suddenly furrowed as she spoke.
"Are you finally tired?
Am I being too much of a burden?"
The last question landed in the quiet kitchen like a stone dropped into still water.
Dexter’s expression changed slightly and his gaze turned serious as he shook his head.
"I have never seen you as a burden," he coldly and seriously.
"And I need you to stop calling yourself that.
Mira’s lips parted slightly.
She hadn’t expected that tone.
"Any man who got married to you and called you a burden would be the stupidest person alive."
He held her gaze and his eyes were steady, his voice was firm.
"So stop calling yourself that."
He paused.
"You are important to me.
You, Lyra, and Selene.
You three are the most important people in my life right now.
And that is not going to change."
The kitchen was very quiet.
Mira stared at him.
She had expected him to respond, had expected reassurance and had expected him to say something kind and move on.
A quick "of course not" and a change of subject.
She had not expected this.
She had not expected him to look at her with that expression, speak with that conviction and say the words with the kind of absolute, unshakable certainty that left no room for doubt.
The words had stunned her.
She couldn’t say anything as her throat tightened and her crimson eyes, which could cut steel on a normal day, had gone slightly wide.
Her lips suddenly curled upward.
Then she immediately turned her head away, refusing to meet his gaze.
Her ears had turned pink.
Her Spectral Arms had retracted behind her back, disappearing completely.
Dexter chuckled softly.
He stood up, reached across the table, and picked up her bowl.
As he turned toward the kitchen.
But before he could take more than a few steps, he felt something grip his wrist.
Dexter smiled and looked down
But then, his entire body went rigid as his face changed drastically with wide-eyed shock.
His jaw tightened, his eyes widened and his pupils contracted.
The grip on his wrist was warm, small, soft and strong.
Dexter looked down and his body trembled.

chapters.title: Chapter 184 | Are You Sure?
paragraphs: Stargate City — Main Hero Association Headquarters
Stargate City.
The heart of the world’s hero industry.
At the center of the city stood the Main Hero Association Headquarters, a massive structure that dwarfed nearly every branch headquarters scattered across the various regions.
This was not a branch.
It was the central headquarters of the Hero Association, the place where major decisions were made and where countless departments worked around the clock to keep the organization running.
Inside one of the administrative departments, the atmosphere was busy.

Dozens of people in suits sat at their desks, typing on computers, writing reports, submitting forms, and conducting the thousands of small, unglamorous tasks that kept the Hero Association functioning. The sound of keyboards clicking filled the room like mechanical rain. Occasional murmurs. The rustle of paper. The soft ping of arriving emails.
In one corner of the office, a young woman sat at her desk.
She was not typing.
While every other person around her was engaged in the steady, productive rhythm of morning work, she was staring at a document.
The document lay flat on her desk. A single sheet of official Hero Association letterhead, filled out in neat handwriting and signed at the bottom in blue ink.
Her eyes were fixed on the title printed at the top.
REQUEST FOR TRANSFER
Below the title, in the same neat handwriting:
Requesting transfer from Main Hero Association Headquarters to Branch Office, Lower District.
She stared at the words.
She had been staring at them for fifteen minutes.
She was twenty-three years old, slim, dark-haired and pretty, in the kind of way that drew attention without trying to.

She wore a standard Hero Association administrative uniform. A fitted grey blazer over a white blouse and a pencil skirt. Her employee badge hung around her neck, the photograph showing a younger version of herself with a slightly forced smile.

She had worked at the Main Headquarters for eight months. She had fought for the position. Made calls. Pulled favors. Endured three rounds of interviews and a background check before finally being offered a junior administrative role in the Personnel Division.

It was not a glamorous job. It involved processing hero registration forms, filing mission reports, and maintaining the personnel database. But it was a position at the Main Headquarters. The center of everything. The place where careers were built and futures were shaped.
Her name was Jasmine Constance.
And now she was leaving.
She picked up the letter. Stood up. Her chair rolled backward slightly.
She took a breath. Held the letter against her chest. And walked toward the department manager’s office at the far end of the floor.
She had taken three steps when a figure stepped directly into her path.
Darren.

He was tall. Well-built. Clean-shaven. The kind of man who looked like he belonged on a recruitment poster rather than behind a desk. He wore his blazer with the casual confidence of someone who knew he looked good in it. His dark hair was styled with expensive product. His cologne was subtle but present.
He was also, as Jasmine had learned over the past four months, persistent to the point of obstruction.
His brow furrowed as he looked down at her.
"Jasmine. Are you sure you want to do this?"
His voice was low. Intended to be private. But in an open-plan office where every worker within ten meters had enhanced hearing or simply well-trained ears, low voices didn’t stay private for long.
Jasmine stopped. She looked at him.
"Yes," she said. "I’ve made my choice."

Darren’s frown deepened. He glanced around the office, noting the subtly tilted heads and the suddenly very interested typists who were absolutely, definitely, one hundred percent focused on their screens and not on this conversation.

"You struggled to get here," Darren said, his voice dropping further. "You made calls. You pulled strings. You were lucky to get a position at the Main Headquarters. And now you want to transfer to a branch office? In the lower district?"
"Yes."
"Just yes?"
"Just yes."
Darren’s jaw tightened. He reached out and grabbed her wrist.

The grip was not aggressive. It was the grip of a man who was accustomed to getting his way and was genuinely confused when things didn’t go according to his plan. It was also a grip that Jasmine did not appreciate.
"What about me?" he said.
Jasmine looked down at his hand on her wrist. Then up at his face.
"What about you?"
Darren’s eyes flashed. "What about what we have?"
Jasmine stared at him.
Then she shook her head slowly.

"You have quite the imagination," she said. Her voice was flat and tired. The kind of tired that came from having the same conversation multiple times. "There is nothing between us. There has never been anything between us."
She held his gaze.
"Please get your hand off me. Unless you want to embarrass yourself in front of the entire office."
Darren’s face went red.

He looked left. He looked right. The nearby typists had suddenly become very interested in their screens, their typing speeds increasing dramatically as they pretended to be deeply absorbed in quarterly personnel reports.
But their ears were perked. Every single one of them was listening.
Darren released her wrist.
He opened his mouth to say something. Then closed it. Then opened it again. Then closed it again.
Jasmine didn’t wait for whatever was going to come out of his mouth.
She turned and walked away.

Her heels clicked against the grey carpet with a steady, unhurried rhythm. She passed rows of cubicles where her colleagues suddenly developed intense fascination with their monitors. She walked the length of the office floor without looking back.
She reached the department manager’s door, knocked once, and entered.
The door closed behind her.
Darren stood alone in the middle of the office floor, his hand still hovering in the air where her wrist had been, his face the color of a ripe tomato.
Nobody looked at him.
Everyone was typing.

chapters.title: Chapter 185 | I Owe You More Than I can Repay
paragraphs: Back at the bungalow.
Mira stared at her own hand.
Her right hand, her actual, physical, flesh-and-blood right hand that had been paralyzed for three years.
The one that no doctor, no healer, no geneticist had been able to restore was wrapped around Dexter’s wrist.
She hadn’t meant to do it. She had reached out instinctively, intending to grab him with her Spectral Arm as she had done dozens of times before. But something different had happened.
Her Spectral Arm had materialized above, hovering in the air as intended.
But her real arm had moved too.
Her real, physical arm had reached out from the her lap, fingers had extended and her hand had closed around Dexter’s wrist
A tear fell from her left eye and dripped off her jaw onto the fabric of her blouse.
She didn’t wipe it away. She couldn’t. Her left arm was still paralyzed.
But her right arm.
Her right arm was holding her husband’s wrist.
She flexed her fingers. Slowly. Deliberately.
They moved.

Her index finger curled inward. Then her middle finger. Then her ring finger. Then her pinky. Each one responding to her mental command with a lag of perhaps half a second, the movements trembling slightly from three years of muscular atrophy.
But they moved.
They moved.
"Dexter," she whispered. Her voice cracked on his name. "I can..."
She couldn’t finish.
Dexter set the bowl down on the counter. Slowly. Carefully. As though any sudden movement might shatter whatever miracle was happening in front of him.
He knelt in front of her wheelchair.
He looked up at her. His eyes were bright. His expression was gentle. His voice, when he spoke, carried a quiet certainty that he didn’t fully feel but knew she needed to hear.
"You did it."
Mira looked at him. Her crimson eyes, usually so sharp and guarded, were wide and glistening. Tears streamed down her face in silent rivers.
She shook her head. "I don’t... I can’t..."
"Yes," Dexter said firmly. "You did."
Mira’s trembling right hand released his wrist. She raised it slowly, inch by inch, the muscles straining visibly beneath her pale skin. She held it in front of her face.
Her own hand was actually moving at her command.
It looked as though it was an illusion, but they were hers.
She suddenly looked at Dexter.
"Thank you."
The words were barely audible. Spoken through tears, through a throat tightened by emotion, through lips that trembled with the weight of three years of despair finally cracking open.
It was the most emotional thank you she had ever spoken in her life.
Dexter shook his head. "There’s no need to thank me. I didn’t do much apart from the massages and taking care of you. This was all you. Your body, your will, your strength."
Mira shook her head firmly. The tears continued to fall, but her expression had hardened.
"No," she said. Her voice was stronger now. Still cracking, but anchored by conviction. "I don’t know what you did. I don’t know how you did it. But I know one thing for certain."
She looked directly into his eyes.
"This was because of you."
Dexter opened his mouth to protest.
"Don’t," Mira said, cutting him off. "Don’t deny it. Don’t minimize it. Don’t stand there and pretend you had nothing to do with this."
Her right hand reached out again. This time, it touched his face. Her fingers, trembling and weak, brushed against his cheek. The touch was feather-light. Barely there. But it was real.

"I thought my life was over," she whispered. "I thought everything was gone. My talent. My future. My worth. Everything that made me Mira Calloway. I thought death was better than being paralyzed. I thought... I thought I was nothing."
Her voice broke. She swallowed hard. Continued.
"But you changed that. You tried your best and even though I would rather die than admit it, you gradually changed my thoughts and tried your best to heal me.’
She pulled her hand back. Held it in front of her face again, staring at it as though it were the most precious thing in the world.
"My family couldn’t do this," she said. "The Calloway family. With all their wealth. All their resources. All their connections. They couldn’t do what you did."
She looked at him.
"I owe you," she said. "I owe you more than I can ever repay. And I don’t say things I don’t mean."
Dexter stared at her. He had expected an emotional reaction. He had not expected this.
"Whatever request you want," Mira continued. "No matter how despicable. No matter how evil. No matter how villainous. I will honor it. Just give me the command, and I will do as you say."
Dexter’s eyes widened. "Mira, there is no need...
Mira raised her right hand.
The movement was deliberate. Not the instinctive grab from before. A conscious, willed motion of a hand she had only just regained control of.
She raised it high.
"This promise," she said. Her voice was steady. Clear. Carrying the weight of absolute conviction. "I swear by the Death God in the night. I swear with my soul."
The words left her lips in a cadence that was not conversational. It was ritualistic. Ancient. Each syllable weighted with power that predated modern cultivation systems.
Dexter’s face changed.
The air in the kitchen shifted. The temperature dropped. Not from cold, but from presence.
Something chilling that existed between the living and the dead had been summoned by the invocation of a power older than the Hero Association itself.
A shadow emerged from the ground.

It rose directly behind Mira’s wheelchair. A phantom shape, roughly humanoid, composed of darkness so dense it seemed to absorb the light around it. It had no features. No face. No expression. It simply existed, towering behind the wheelchair like a silent witness.
Mira bit her right hand.
Her teeth broke the skin of her thumb. A drop of blood, dark red and vivid, welled up from the wound.
She extended her hand downward.
The phantom image descended. It reached toward the falling drop of blood with an almost reverent slowness. Its shadowy hand caught the blood midair, cradling it as though it were a gem.
Then it sank back into the ground.
The shadow vanished. The temperature normalized. The oppressive presence disappeared as suddenly as it had arrived.
The entire event had lasted perhaps three seconds.
Dexter stared at the floor where the phantom had disappeared.
’She just swore a Death God oath. She bound her soul to this promise.’
That meant she was dead serious!
A Death God oath was the most binding commitment a person could make. Breaking it would tear the swearer’s soul from their body. The same principle that governed the marriage contract.
Mira had just put her soul on the line for a promise to him.
Dexter looked at her solemnly.
"Okay," he said quietly. He didn’t argue, nor did he protest. You didn’t argue with someone who had just sworn a Death God oath. You accept and honor it, making sure it was never abused.
Mira nodded her head as the contract was signed.

She looked at Dexter with a smile.
"By the end of this year, I should be able to move my second arm and maybe even walk."
Dexter smiled. "Hopefully even before that."
Mira glanced at him. The smugness returned to her expression, but it was lighter now. Playful rather than defensive.
"Don’t push it," she said. But she was still smiling. Still staring at her hand.
Dexter left her in the dining room, still mesmerized by her own hand.
He went to the kitchen, dealt with the dishes as he thought about Mira.

The 108 Body Massage Sutra, the Glove, the Grade-4 Spiritual Massage Oil, the diamond rice, the Star-Shaped Leaf tea, the Grand Cosmos Scripture, and various other things he had given herc it’s no wonder she could finally move in just a month.
It hadn’t been wasted at all. The only thing left was the bloodline. It hadn’t surfaced yet but Dexter had a feeling it needed some sort of trigger.
He shook his head. ’Will find a way to trigger the bloodline for them’

"Yes."
"Now?"

"I want to see the outside world with you."
Dexter was stunned.

Mira wanted to go outside. Mira, who hadn’t left the house since the day she arrived. Mira, who sat by the window every day and stared at nothing. Mira, who had spent a couple weeks treating the outside world as though it didn’t exist.
She wanted to go out, to see the city.
Dexter stared at her suspiciously.
"I hope this is not you completing a request of mine. Because I didn’t ask for this."
Mira glared at him. "Do you think I am that devious?"

Dexter’s expression didn’t change. He continued to look at her with the flat, unblinking skepticism of a man who had been on the receiving end of Mira’s manipulations enough times to recognize the pattern.
Mira snorted. "Okay. I might be that devious. But not this time. This is me wanting to go outside."
Dexter exhaled a breath of relief.

Dexter smirked.
"Don’t worry," he said. "You’ll find out later."
Mira glared at him. Her face flushed. Her ears turned pink.
"Pervert," she muttered.

If he took Mira out today, he was showing favoritism.

Taking one wife out while leaving the other two at home. Lyra and Selene would notice. They would feel excluded. They might not say anything, because neither of them was the type to complain openly, but the silence would be worse.

Dexter was conflicted.
Mira noticed.
Her brow furrowed and the excitement in her eyes began to dim.

She thought he was embarrassed.
She thought he didn’t want to be seen in public with a cripple. A woman in a wheelchair who couldn’t walk. A broken wife who would draw stares and whispers and pity from strangers on the street.
She thought he was ashamed of her.
Dexter’s chest tightened.
"No," he said quickly. "You don’t understand. That’s not it at all."
Mira looked at him. The doubt in her crimson eyes was painful to see.

He paused, rubbing the back of his neck.

"But what I’m doing today involves delivering meals to the bakery, meeting with the heroes I fought alongside during the outbreak, and visiting a housing company. I’ll be moving between locations. I won’t have the time to properly look after the three of you while I’m running around. And I can’t just leave you somewhere while I handle business."
Mira’s eyes changed as the doubt and slight guarded hurt faded as she understood. Her eyes finally brightening.
She was about to speak when Dexter held up a hand.

chapters.title: Chapter 187 | The Promise
paragraphs: "How about this instead," he said. "There’s a festival this weekend. Two days from now. Tessa mentioned it. The entire neighborhood is participating. It’s a picnic, held at Roland Stone Garden, which is close by."
He looked at her.
"How about all three of you attend the festival with me? What do you think?"
Mira blinked.
"A festival," she repeated.
Dexter nodded.
Mira’s brow furrowed slightly. A festival meant crowds. Noise, and lots of people.
She didn’t know if she was ready for that.
Dexter saw the hesitation on her face and smiled gently. "It’s fine if you don’t want to go."
Mira shook her head slowly. "No. At some point I would have to go out. One way or another. It might as well be during the festival."
She paused as her eyes drifted to space.
"Since everyone is attending, no one would be focused on us. It wouldn’t be bad to see the neighbors either."
Dexter smiled. "Okay. I’ll tell Selene and Lyra."
He wheeled her to the living room and positioned her by the window. She was still staring at her right hand.
He turned toward the couch.
Lyra was there, but something was different.
She was not holding the Primordial Beast Egg.
Dexter raised an eyebrow. In the weeks since he had brought the egg home, Lyra had practically fused with it.
She carried it everywhere. On the couch. In the kitchen. To the bathroom. She cultivated with it, slept with it.
Seeing her without it was slightly odd.
’Maybe they are taking turns?’
Dexter smiled to Lyra and spoke.
"Lyra. Would you like to attend a festival in two days? It’s a neighborhood gathering. A picnic. Not far from here. The entire neighborhood will be there."
Lyra’s eyes remained closed for a moment. Then they opened.
She blinked.
Then her voice appeared in his mind.
"Will there be food?"
Dexter chuckled.
"Yes. There will be food."
Lyra’s face lit up like a sunrise.
"Yes. I would love to go."
Dexter shook his head with a quiet smile.
He walked to the backyard.
Selene was on the swing, eyes closed, cultivating.
The Primordial Beast Egg rested in her lap.
The swing moved gently in the breeze, giving her the appearance of a ghost drifting in the wind. A pale, silver-haired spirit suspended between earth and sky.
He walked directly beside her and waited.

He knew better than to speak. Selene’s Echolocation talent detected his presence through the vibrations of his footsteps and the displacement of air around his body. She knew he was there. She would acknowledge him when she was ready.
Five seconds passed.
Selene’s eyes opened.
She looked at him. And smiled.
Dexter smiled back.
And then, without warning, the memory of last night hit him.
Her head on his chest. Her arm around his torso. Her leg draped across his knee. The warmth of her body pressed against his side.
The quiet, content sound she had made in her sleep.
Heat rose within him.

Not Abyssal Flame heat. Not mana circulation heat. The other kind. The kind that had nearly destroyed his composure that morning in the bathroom and was now threatening to do it again in the backyard.
He inhaled deeply through his nose, held it and immediately exhaled slowly through his mouth.

’Calm down, Calm down, Calm down. She is a person, not an object. She might be your wife but they might not see you as their husband. Moreover, you are still a very busy man with responsibilities but here you are thinking about crazy things... what the hell did I take?’
The rising heat subsided but not by much. However, it was manageable.
He spoke.
"Selene. Would you like to go out for a festival in two days? It’s a picnic, not far from here. The entire neighborhood will be participating."
Selene blinked her pale, sightless eyes.
Then she slowly nodded.
Dexter was stunned. He had expected resistance and hesitation.
Of the three women, Selene had been the most withdrawn and then most guarded. The most reluctant to engage with the world beyond the walls of the bungalow.
But she had said yes.
Without argument or hesitation not did she even think much about it.
She had simply nodded.
Then she smiled.
"Good luck," she said.
Dexter blinked and he understood. She was wishing him well for his errands. The bakery delivery, the housing agent and the squad meeting.
"Thank you," he said. "And bye."
"Bye."
He turned and walked back inside.
He reached the front door and opened it. Before stepping out, he turned back toward the living room.
"Bye, everyone. I’m leaving."
Lyra’s voice echoed in his mind. "Bye."
Mira didn’t respond verbally. She was still staring at her right hand, flexing her fingers with the absorbed concentration of a scientist studying a new species.
Dexter leaned back inside.
"Mira. Don’t open the door for anyone."
A laugh rang out from the living room.
An actual laugh from Mira sounded out.
He was quite stunned by this as it sounded genuine as though she found his joke funny.
Dexter paused, then he realized why she was laughing.

For three weeks, he had been telling Mira not to open the door for anyone. It had been a running gag between them, born from the fact that Mira was paralyzed from the neck down and physically incapable of opening any door.
It was a playful tease. A small, joke to annoy Mira whenever he was leaving the house.
And it had always worked. But now, she could actually move her right arm!
Which meant that she could open a door!
The joke that had been harmless for three weeks had suddenly become real, and the irony of it had struck Mira with enough force to make her chuckle unexpectedly.
Dexter shook his head at his own expense.
"Right," he muttered. "Note to self. Update the jokes."
He stepped outside, closed the door behind him, and walked to the SUV parked in front of the house.

chapters.title: Chapter 188 | The Appointment
paragraphs: The drive to the bakery took five minutes.
Dexter parked behind a small sedan in the lot beside the bakery, killed the engine, and checked the time on his phone.
Not late but not particularly early either. The bakery opened at seven, and by eight to nine, the morning rush was in full swing.
He climbed out of the SUV, retrieved two large bags from the back seat, and walked inside. Each bag contained twenty-five sealed containers of Grade One Arcane Meals.
When he entered, he saw that the bakery was crowded.
Every table was occupied and then line at the counter almost stretched to the door.
Parents in work clothes waited with tired expressions while children tugged at their sleeves and pointed at the pastry display.
Two teenage girls in school uniforms were sharing a croissant and giggling over something on one of their phones.
The smell in the bakery was incredible. Fresh bread, roasted coffee, butter and sugar, it was really nice.

Tessa appeared to possess some kind of sixth sense for Dexter as the moment he stepped through the door, her head popped up from behind the counter as her green eyes found him immediately across the crowded room.
She waved, turned to the staff member beside her, said something brief, and then wove through the customers toward him.
"Good morning," she said, arriving at his side with a bright smile. She looked him up and down. "You clean up quite good."
Dexter was slightly startled by the comment.
He immediately chose to ignore her.
"Where should I drop these?" he asked, lifting the two bags slightly.
Tessa’s eyes widened at the size of the bags. "Come. Back here."

She led him through the narrow hallway behind the counter, into the small storage room at the back of the bakery. Steel shelves lined the walls, filled with ingredient containers, baking supplies, and spare equipment.

"Place them here," Tessa said, pointing to an empty section of shelf. "I’ll display about ten out front. When those sell out, I’ll restock from back here. If everything goes like yesterday, we won’t need to restock more than twice."

Dexter set the bags down and began stacking the containers neatly on the shelves. White boxes with tight-sealing lids, each one containing a portion of Comfort Chicken Rice. The smell of seasoned chicken and ginger seeped through the seals, mingling with the bakery’s existing aroma of bread and butter.
Tessa watched him stack them with a particular gleam again in her eyes.
"These will probably sell out before 5 PM today," she said.
Dexter straightened up and looked at her. "I hope so."
Then he saw the gleam.
His eyes narrowed.
"You’re not increasing your commission again, are you? Because I can’t go higher than the twenty-five percent you already stole from me."
Tessa smirked. "Stolen? I worked hard for that twenty-five percent. I sold the food. I handled the customers. I answered questions. I—"
"Fine! Fine! You did everything. You worked hard for it."
Dexter rolled his eyes.
"Alright. I’m leaving. Have a good one."
"Bye, Boss Chef!"
Tessa waved him off with a cheerful grin and dollar signs in her eyes.
Dexter climbed back into the SUV and pulled up the address for Harvest Homes on his phone.
The navigation system calculated a thirty-minute drive from the bakery to the mid-district. He merged onto the main highway and settled in for the drive.
The city scrolled past his windows. Billboards advertised everything from. Hero gear to Dungeon insurance to Mana supplements to even Guild recruitment drives.
Twenty-eight minutes later, Dexter pulled into the parking garage beneath the Harvest Homes building.
He stepped out of the SUV, looked up, stopped, and was really stunned.
The building was really extraordinary.
It wasn’t very tall but was something else entirely. The Harvest Homes building was a work of art.
The structure more than 70 floors, but its height was not what made it remarkable, it was the design.
It looked like someone had brought a massive mountain cliff into the city.
Water fell from the top of the buiding, rushing straight to the ground. Living plants grew from integrated balconies on every floor, cascading downward in rivers of green.
It was difficult to describe.
Dexter stared at the building for a long moment.
He had seen impressive architecture before. The Ashford estate had been grandiose, the Hero Association headquarters was imposing and the Grand Meridian hotel had been luxurious.
But this was different.

He shook his head. In an age of heroes, where people possessed abilities that could mold stone, shape metal, and grow plants at will, extraordinary construction was simply the natural result of extraordinary talents applied to ordinary problems.
He walked through the archway and into the lobby.
The interior matched the exterior. It was really a thing of beauty.
A reception desk sat in the center of the lobby. Several receptionists were stationed behind it.
Dexter walked to the nearest available desk.
The receptionist was a beautiful young woman with blonde buzz-cut hair and sharp, angular features.
If not for two rather bumps on her chest, pushing against her fitted blazer, Dexter might have assumed she was a very handsome young man.
She looked up as he approached and smiled.
"Good morning. Welcome to Harvest Homes. How may I help you?"
"Good morning. I’m Dexter Ashford. I have a ten o’clock appointment with Jennifer."
The receptionist’s fingers moved across her keyboard, then studied her screen for a moment, as she smiled.
"Ah, yes. Dexter Ashford, ten o’clock with Jennifer. We’ve been expecting you." She gestured toward the elevator on the far wall.
"Please head to the twenty-fourth floor. You’ll be met by someone there."
Dexter thanked her and walked toward the elevators.
A soft chime sounded and the door in front of him slid open silently, revealing a couple was already inside.
The man wore a tailored grey suit and the woman wore a designer dress and heels that added several inches to her height.

When those sell out, I’ll restock from back here.
If everything goes like yesterday, we won’t need to restock more than twice."
Dexter set the bags down and began stacking the containers neatly on the shelves.
White boxes with tight-sealing lids, each one containing a portion of Comfort Chicken Rice.
The smell of seasoned chicken and ginger seeped through the seals, mingling with the bakery’s existing aroma of bread and butter.
Tessa watched him stack them with a particular gleam again in her eyes.
"These will probably sell out before 5 PM today," she said.
Dexter straightened up and looked at her.
"I hope so."
Then he saw the gleam.
His eyes narrowed.
"You’re not increasing your commission again, are you?
Because I can’t go higher than the twenty-five percent you already stole from me."
Tessa smirked.
"Stolen?
I worked hard for that twenty-five percent.
I sold the food.
I handled the customers.
I answered questions.
"Fine!
Fine!
You did everything.
You worked hard for it."
Dexter rolled his eyes.
"Alright.
I’m leaving.
Have a good one."
"Bye, Boss Chef!"
Tessa waved him off with a cheerful grin and dollar signs in her eyes.
Dexter climbed back into the SUV and pulled up the address for Harvest Homes on his phone.
The navigation system calculated a thirty-minute drive from the bakery to the mid-district.
He merged onto the main highway and settled in for the drive.
The city scrolled past his windows.
Billboards advertised everything from.
Hero gear to Dungeon insurance to Mana supplements to even Guild recruitment drives.
Twenty-eight minutes later, Dexter pulled into the parking garage beneath the Harvest Homes building.
He stepped out of the SUV, looked up, stopped, and was really stunned.
The building was really extraordinary.
It wasn’t very tall but was something else entirely.
The Harvest Homes building was a work of art.
The structure more than 70 floors, but its height was not what made it remarkable, it was the design.
It looked like someone had brought a massive mountain cliff into the city.
Water fell from the top of the buiding, rushing straight to the ground.
Living plants grew from integrated balconies on every floor, cascading downward in rivers of green.
It was difficult to describe.
Dexter stared at the building for a long moment.
He had seen impressive architecture before.
The Ashford estate had been grandiose, the Hero Association headquarters was imposing and the Grand Meridian hotel had been luxurious.
But this was different.
He shook his head.

In an age of heroes, where people possessed abilities that could mold stone, shape metal, and grow plants at will, extraordinary construction was simply the natural result of extraordinary talents applied to ordinary problems.
He walked through the archway and into the lobby.
The interior matched the exterior.
It was really a thing of beauty.
A reception desk sat in the center of the lobby.
Several receptionists were stationed behind it.
Dexter walked to the nearest available desk.
The receptionist was a beautiful young woman with blonde buzz-cut hair and sharp, angular features.
If not for two rather bumps on her chest, pushing against her fitted blazer, Dexter might have assumed she was a very handsome young man.
She looked up as he approached and smiled.
"Good morning.
Welcome to Harvest Homes.
How may I help you?"
"Good morning.
I’m Dexter Ashford.
I have a ten o’clock appointment with Jennifer."
The receptionist’s fingers moved across her keyboard, then studied her screen for a moment, as she smiled.
"Ah, yes.
Dexter Ashford, ten o’clock with Jennifer.
We’ve been expecting you." She gestured toward the elevator on the far wall.
"Please head to the twenty-fourth floor.
You’ll be met by someone there."
Dexter thanked her and walked toward the elevators.
A soft chime sounded and the door in front of him slid open silently, revealing a couple was already inside.
The man wore a tailored grey suit and the woman wore a designer dress and heels that added several inches to her height.

chapters.title: Chapter 189 | Choosing A Home
paragraphs: They were standing close together, the woman’s hand resting on the man’s arm.
As the door began to close, the man noticed Dexter approaching. He reached out and pressed the open button. The door reversed, sliding back open.
Dexter stepped inside. "Thank you."
The man nodded and smiled politely.
The woman glanced at Dexter. Her eyes moved from his face to his clothes to his shoes.
Then her brow furrowed slightly as she looked at her boyfriend then she let out a soft snort.
Dexter remained expressionless.
He pressed the button for the 24th floor.
The elevator began to rise and it felt like floating upward on a cloud of air, the floor numbers ticking past on the display panel beside the door in soft, glowing digits.
At the 20th floor, the elevator stopped and the doors opened as the couple stepped out.
As they exited, the man glanced back at Dexter. His expression carried a trace of apology.
The woman didn’t look back as the doors closed and the elevator continued upward.
Dexter stood alone as he chuckled. "Women..."
"Ding!"
The doors opened and Dexter stepped out into the hallway.
He had expected Jennifer to meet him, the woman he had spoken to on the phone but was instead met with a middle-aged man.
The middle-aged man came striding toward him from the far end of the corridor.
The man was... uhm... Fat.
Not fat, exactly, but heavy.
But his stomach was in the bigger side, stretching his dark blue suit very wide.
His face was round and ruddy, with thick lips and small eyes that crinkled into a smile when he saw Dexter.
"Dexter Ashford!" his voice booming through the hallway.
He immediately crossed the distance in a flash and grabbed Dexter’s hand before Dexter could offer it and shook his hands enthusiastically!
"Welcome, welcome! You’re very much welcome! Come, come, come. Let’s go to my office."
Dexter frowned slightly. He glanced past the man, looking for Jennifer but the hallway was currently empty.
"I was supposed to meet Jennifer," Dexter forcefully removed his hand and spoke..

The man waved a dismissive hand. "Yes, yes. Jennifer is one of our junior staff. She handles the initial phone inquiries and is very good at what she does. But for property consultations of this nature, the company felt it best that someone with more experience handle your case personally."
He smiled broadly. "And that someone is me. Marcus Webb, Senior Property Consultant."
He extended his hand again. Dexter didn’t shake it and simply glanced at him.
’He’s looking quite sketchy...’
"Please, here, come with me to my office."
Dexter filed the observation away and followed Marcus down the corridor.
The office was at the far end and marcus opened the door with a flourish and gestured Dexter inside.
The office was tidy. A large iron desk dominated the center of the room and its surface was clean except for a tablet, a stylus, and a small potted plant.
But it was the wall behind the desk that caught Dexter’s attention.
Weapons.
Three swords hung on the wall, mounted on individual display shelf.
Type One, Type Two, Type Three weapons!
Dexter’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Relic weapons and three of them at the moment.
Displayed openly on an office wall like hunting trophies.
Marcus noticed him looking and smiled proudly. "Collectibles. A hobby of mine. The Type Three was a gift from a client who was very happy with the property I found him."

Dexter said nothing. Real estate agents in this city earned well. That was no secret. The most successful ones dealt with properties worth tens of millions of credits. A Type Three relic on the wall was the equivalent of a luxury car gift to someone people.
Marcus sat behind his desk with a grunt and gestured toward the leather chair opposite. "Please, sit, sit."
Dexter sat.
Marcus leaned forward, his small eyes bright with enthusiasm. "Now. I understand you are searching for a property. A home. Somewhere to live."
Dexter nodded. "Yes. I’m looking for a simple house. At least four bedrooms. In a decent neighborhood."
Marcus clapped his hands together. "Perfect. That is exactly the kind of request I love to hear."
He tapped his tablet and a holographic display materialized above the desk, projecting a three-dimensional map of Stargate City.
The city was rendered in miniature, with districts color-coded by zoning type and property value.
Small icons marked available properties, each one pulsing gently.

"Now," Marcus said, manipulating the display with practiced gestures. "As you may know, the rate of gate openings and monster outbreaks has increased across the city in recent months. This has driven up demand for residential properties in stable districts. Various families have been investing heavily in new developments, particularly in the outer rings where land is cheaper and security formations can be installed from scratch."
He zoomed the map outward, showing the ring of new developments along the city’s perimeter.
"Several new estates have been completed in the last month."
The holographic display shifted, showing a series of newly developed neighborhoods, houses, townhouses, small estates.
Each one rendered in three-dimensional detail with specifications, pricing, and availability floating beside them.
Dexter studied the display.
Marcus swiped through several options. A townhouse in the western district. A duplex near the commercial ring. A mid-size family home in the northern sector.
Dexter’s eyes moved across the properties without interest. None of them felt right.
Then Marcus swiped to the next property, and Dexter’s hand shot out.
"Wait."
Marcus paused as he swiped back.
Dexter looked at the image.
It was a two-story house with white exterior and dark roof.

It also has its front porch covered with a wooden railing wnd a small garden in the front with a path leading from the gate to the door. Behind the house, a backyard with enough space for a garden, a patio, and maybe a training area.
It was in a standard suburban neighborhood that looked and felt quite to Dexter.
But the most important detail was the location!

The house was at the eastern edge of Stargate City, at the far edge and the boundary where the city’s developed territory met the wilderness buffer zone that separated urban civilization from the untamed regions beyond.
It was far from the central district and far from the political heart of the city where the Nine Families schemed and maneuvered.
Far from the Ashfords, the Calloways, the Vances and far from the Frosts.
Moreover, it was isolated and completely anonymous.
Dexter felt something settle in his chest like he’d seen what scarily he wanted.
"This one," he said. "This is perfect."
Marcus beamed. "Excellent eye! Excellent eye indeed." He tapped the property icon, and a detailed specification sheet expanded beside the house.
Property: Harvest Crest Residence, Plot 47
Type: Two-Story Single Family Home
Bedrooms: 5
Bathrooms: 3
Floor Area: 320 square meters
Lot Area: 450 square meters
Features: Integrated defense formation (Tier 2), climate-controlled interior, mana-infused foundation, private backyard, covered garage, storage basement
Year Built: Current Year (3 weeks prior)
Status: Unoccupied
Neighborhood Status: Newly developed. Low population density. 12 of 30 plots occupied.
"The entire estate was completed just three weeks ago," Marcus smiled
Dexter nodded slowly and interrupted him. "How much?"
Marcus’s smile widened. "This particular property is priced at nine million credits."
Dexter’s expression didn’t change.
But inside his mind, he chuckled bitterly.
Nine million credits.

chapters.title: Chapter 190 | Purchase
paragraphs: "How much?"
Marcus’s smile widened. "This particular property is priced at nine million Dollars."
Dexter’s expression didn’t change.
But inside his mind, he chuckled bitterly.
Nine million Dollars.
His bank account held 1.2 million.
He had walked into this building thinking his 1.2 million might be enough to purchase a decent home outright but he eas dead wrong.
If was even less than twenty percent of the asking price and wasn’t even close.
He kept his face neutral as he spoke.
"Alright, I’ll come back later when I have the funds."
He placed both hands on the armrests, preparing to stand.
Marcus’s smile faltered for a second before he quickly spoke and raised his hands.
"No, no, no. Wait, please sit. There’s no need to leave just yet."
Dexter paused as he glanced at Marcus for a while before he lowered himself back into the chair.
"We have options," Marcus continued, his smile returning. "For clients who have not yet gathered the full purchase price, we offer flexible installment plans."
He tapped the tablet and a new display appeared, showing three payment plan options.
"We have a three-month plan, a six-month plan, and a twelve-month plan. Each one allows you to move into the property immediately upon payment of the first installment."
Dexter blinked. "Move in immediately?"

"Immediately," Marcus confirmed. "The first payment secures the property. You receive the keys and the provisional deed. The property is yours to live in, to use, to make your home. Subsequent payments are made monthly until the full amount is settled, at which point the final deed is transferred to your name."
Dexter listened attentively. "What are the terms?"
Marcus leaned forward. "Let’s take the twelve-month plan, for example. The total purchase price under the twelve-month plan is twelve million Dollars."
He tapped the display.
"Monthly payment: one million Dollars per month for twelve months."
Dexter frowned. "One million per month."
"Yes.
"That’s twelve million total. Three million more than the asking price! Dexter was quite stunned at the greed of this company.
Marcus spread his hands. "That’s the interest and it’s a standard rate too. Every property developer in the city charges the same rate and some even charge more."
Dexter frowned as he sat back in his chair.
One million per month while he currently had 1.2 million. That would cover the first payment and leave him with roughly 220,000 Dollars.
But he needed to make one million Dollars every month for twelve months which places burden on him by quite a lot.
The bakery business was generating approximately 90,000 dollars per day in gross sales.
After Tessa’s 25 percent commission, his net was about 67,500 Dollars per day. If he sold fifty portions daily, that was roughly 2 million dollars per month.
But that was just the gross price. He needed to subtract ingredient costs, which ran about 20,000 dollars per day for fifty portions.
That left roughly 1.4 million net per month from the bakery alone.
Add dungeon raiding income, and the math worked.
But it was tight. But then, the house was truly perfect.
Five bedrooms. One for each wife. One for himself and a real house in a real neighborhood where no one knew their names.
He thought more about it.
"Okay," Dexter said. "I’ll take the twelve-month plan."
Marcus’s face lit up like a sunrise. "Excellent decision! Very good decision! I promise you, you will not regret this."
He practically lunged for his desk drawer, pulling out a stack of documents with the speed of a man who had closed this particular deal a hundred times and had the paperwork memorized.
"Sign here. And here. And here. And one more here."

He placed four documents in front of Dexter, each one marked with a highlighted signature line. Dexter read each one carefully, his eyes scanning the legal language for hidden clauses, unfavorable terms, or the kind of small print that the Ashford family had used to trap three families into marrying their daughters to a bastard.

The documents were clean. Standard purchase agreement. Installment terms. Property transfer schedule. Default clause that returned the property to Harvest Homes if payments were missed for three consecutive months.
He signed all four.
Marcus produced an account number. "Please transfer the first payment to this account. Once the transfer is confirmed, the process begins."
Dexter pulled out his phone, opened his banking app, and initiated the transfer. One million Dollars.
[Transfer sent: 1,000,000 Dollars]
The confirmation appeared on Marcus’s tablet within seconds. The man’s smile became almost blindingly bright.
"Wonderful! Wonderful! The transfer is confirmed." He reached into his drawer again and pulled out a leather folder. Inside was a document embossed with the Harvest Homes seal.

"This is your provisional housing deed," Marcus said, presenting it with both hands as though it were a royal decree. "It confirms your ownership of the property pending completion of all installment payments. Once the final payment is made, this will be replaced with the permanent deed."
He then placed a small envelope on the desk.
"And these are your keys."
Dexter took the envelope. Inside were two keys and a small electronic fob.
A thought struck him.
The system had given him the actual deed to his current bungalow, revealing that the Ashford family’s original documents had been fake. He was the true, legal owner of the bungalow.
Which meant he could sell it.
The bungalow, despite its run-down condition, sat on a plot of land in a developed neighborhood.
Even in poor condition, the land alone was worth something, enough to pad his remaining balance.
He would look into it later.
Marcus stood up, his round belly shifting as he rose. He extended his hand.
"Let me be the first to congratulate you, Mr. Ashford. You are now the proud owner of a Harvest Crest residence."
Dexter stood and shook his hand. "Thank you."

Marcus grabbed a tablet and pulled up a map. "The property is located in Edge District 3, about forty minutes from the city center. I can have someone accompany you to the property for a walkthrough if you’d like."
Dexter shook his head. "No need. I’ll go alone."
Marcus blinked. "Alone? Are you sure? I could send an agent to show you around the neighborhood, introduce you to the local amenities, explain the defense formation system..."
"No," Dexter said firmly. "I’ll go alone."
There was something about Marcus that Dexter didn’t quite trust. It wasn’t anything specific. The man was professional. The documents were clean. The transaction had been straightforward.
But he still felt something was wrong.
Dexter pocketed the keys, placed the deed in his spatial storage, and headed for the door.

"Alone?
Are you sure?
I could send an agent to show you around the neighborhood, introduce you to the local amenities, explain the defense formation system..."
"No," Dexter said firmly.
"I’ll go alone."
There was something about Marcus that Dexter didn’t quite trust.
It wasn’t anything specific.
The man was professional.
The documents were clean.
The transaction had been straightforward.
But he still felt something was wrong.
Dexter pocketed the keys, placed the deed in his spatial storage, and headed for the door.

chapters.title: Chapter 191 | The House
paragraphs: "Thank you for your assistance, Marcus."
"My pleasure! Absolutely my pleasure! And if you have any questions, don’t hesitate to call."
Dexter nodded once and stepped into the hallway.
The elevator ride down was smooth and silent. He stepped out into the lobby, walked through the marble archway, and emerged into the morning sunlight.
He stood on the plaza for a moment, looking up at the extraordinary building with its cascading plants and prismatic glass.
He had a house now.
He pulled out his phone and checked the time.
Plasmatic Man’s meeting was at twelve. He had two hours.
Two hours to drive to his new house, see it for the first time, and decide if it was truly as perfect as the holographic image had suggested.
Dexter walked to his SUV, climbed in, and entered the address into the navigation system.
Destination: Harvest Crest Residence, Plot 47, Edge District 3.
Estimated drive time: 38 minutes.
He started the engine and pulled out of the parking garage.
He needed to see the house first, Needed to verify that the holographic images and the enthusiastic sales pitch matched reality.
The drive took 42 minutes.
He drove through the city and then the city ended.
Instead, the urban landscape simply... ran out. The last row of houses faced an open expanse of cleared land, beyond which the wilderness buffer zone began.
There were trees, grasses and distant silhouette of mountains on the horizon.
Dexter turned into the development.
He drove slowly, studying the neighborhood through the windshield.
Marcus had described it as a newly built estate, and the description was accurate.
The houses were fresh with the streets smooth, newly paved asphalt without a single crack or pothole and also standing street lamp.
Of the thirty plots in the development, perhaps twelve showed signs of occupancy with cars in driveways.
Furniture visible through windows and even a child’s bicycle foils be seen leaning against a fence. The rest were unoccupied as of yet.
The entire place was silence not too silent but was a comfortable kind of sileve.
Dexter found Plot 47 at the end of a cul-de-sac.
He parked on the street and got out.
The house looked exactly as it had in the holographic display with white exterior, dark roof and front porch with a steel railing. A small garden space in the front too.
He walked to the front gate and pushed it.
He could feel it was a grade one steel and could withstand significant force.
Wild monsters could break through it eventually, but it would hold long enough for the neighborhood’s defense formation to activate and for residents to take shelter.
He walked up the path to the front door and used his new key to open it.
Dexter stepped inside.
The house was just as he expected, clean and fresh.
The living room was spacious, larger than the entire ground floor of the bungalow.

There was room for multiple sofas, a coffee table, a television unit, and still enough open space for someone to move around comfortably, or for a wheelchair to navigate without bumping into anything.
He walked through the living room into the dining area and it was large enough for a table that could seat six or even eight, if you pushed it.
The kitchen was twice the size of his kitchen at the bungalow, it was enormous, running along two full walls with an island in the center.
The stove was a commercial-grade unit with six burners and a built-in oven and the sink was deep and wide and looked quite flashy.
Cabinet space lined every wall, floor to ceiling and enough storage to hold ingredients, equipment, and supplies for a small-scale Foodsmith operation.
There was even a separate pantry room off to the side. A dedicated space for dry goods, spices, and bulk ingredients.
Dexter ran his hand along the counter with slight smile on his face.
’This kitchen could feed an army.’
He moved on to the bedroom and it was large also, large enough for a queen bed, a wardrobe, and a desk.
This would be perfect for Mira as it was ground floor access and didn’t need stairs to navigate and was also close to the bathroom, which was right next door.
The bathroom was fully equipped with walk-in shower, deep bathtub and dual sinks.
Everything looked brand new, which meant it was ever used.
He went upstairs.

Three bedrooms. Each one larger than the bedrooms at the bungalow. Each one with its own window, its own closet space, and access to a second bathroom that was identical in design to the one downstairs.

Dexter stood in the largest of the upstairs bedrooms and looked out the window. The backyard stretched out below him with enough space for a garden, a patio and maybe a small training area, if he sectioned off a corner and installed some equipment.
Beyond the backyard, the iron fence marked the property boundary.
It was quiet, private and I solated.
Dexter nodded slowly.
The girls would like this.
Mira would have her ground-floor bedroom, giving her independence and dignity without the humiliation of being carried up stairs.

Selene would have a quiet room where she could cultivate in peace, far from the noise and chaos of the old neighborhood. Lyra would have space for her egg, her chips, and whatever else she wanted to accumulate.
And he would have a kitchen that could actually handle the volume of cooking he needed to do for both the household and the bakery business.
He smiled.
’This is quite perfect!’
He locked up, returned to the SUV, and checked his phone.
A message from Cole Stanley.
[Hey Dexter. We’re meeting at Janice’s Cuisine, 24 Thourist Plaza, Central District. Booth 24. We’ll be there by noon. See you there!]
Dexter raised an eyebrow. The restaurant was quite popular, he didn’t expect them to go to ont if the most expensive restaurants in the city.
He entered the address into the GPS, the Central District which was twenty-five minutes from his current location.
He started the engine and was about to move when a large man stood in front of his car.
"Who are you and what are you doing coming out from my building?"

chapters.title: Chapter 192 | What Are You Doing In My Home?
paragraphs: Dexter opened the car door, sat down and then started the engine.
However, a figure suddenly appeared in front of the vehicle.
Dexter’s foot paused over the accelerator.
A muscular man stood directly in his path and his face was set in an aggressive scowl as he glared at Dexter through the glass.
"Who are you?" the man demanded with a loud voice. "What were you doing inside my building?"
Dexter was stunned.
He turned off the engine, opened the door, and stepped out.
"Your building?"
The man’s scowl deepened.
He moved from the front of the SUV to the passenger side, closing the distance between himself and Dexter like he Wa about to fight.
"So you’re one of those people," the man sneered. "One of those people who break into houses and squat there for free once they see it’s empty."
He pulled out his phone.
"I’m calling the cops on you right now."
Dexter’s stomach dropped.
But it wasn’t from fear but sinking else entirely as realization began to hit him.
’No.’
He raised both hands calmly. "Hold on. There’s a misunderstanding."

He turned back to the SUV, reached into the center console where he had placed the documents, and pulled out the leather folder Marcus had given him and then opened it as he held it out toward the man.
"Look. I have documents. From Harvest Homes. I signed a purchase agreement. I have a deed. I have keys."
The man looked at the documents. His eyes scanned the Harvest Homes letterhead and a few things.
Slowly, his scowl faltered as he frowned in confusion, shich caused him to Lowe his phone and cut off the call he was making.

"Harvest Homes doesn’t deal with properties in this neighborhood," the man said slowly. "This estate is managed by Crestline Properties. They’re the exclusive sales agent for this development. Harvest Homes has no authority to sell anything here."
Dexter’s face changed and the feeling in the pit of his stomach grew even more.
"What about the key?" Dexter said, his voice tight. "The key opened the door. The key you gave me opened the door."
He was talking to himself now as much as to the man.
’The key worked and the door opened which meant that the property exists and the sale was real. Right?’
But deep down, he knew he had been scammed.
One million dollars, transferred less than an hour ago.
The man was looking at Dexter with an expression that had shifted from suspicion to pity.
He had clearly seen the name. Dexter Ashford and knew who he was, the one the news had been talking about. The one married to three crippled women.

"Look," the man said, his voice softer now. "I don’t know why you have my key. I just bought this house last month. I’m still moving in. Can I have the key back? I feel uncomfortable with someone else having a key to my home."
Dexter stared at the man. His mind was racing rapidly.
’Harvest Homes is a real company. A registered business. They can’t just disappear. Their office is in the mid-district. Their building exists. Their employees exist. Marcus Webb exists.’
’Even if the sale was fake, the scammer is still there. Still reachable. Still findable.’

"And as for Harvest Homes," the man continued, his voice hardening, "I’ll be reporting them to the appropriate authorities. If they have keys to my house, they might have keys to other people’s houses in this neighborhood too. This won’t stand."
Dexter nodded numbly.
"Let me make a call," he said.
He pulled out his phone. Found Marcus’s number in the documents and pressed dial.
The phone rang and then the call connected.
"Hello, yes, you’re speaking to Marcus."
The familiar, cheerful voice. The same warm tone the man had used while shaking Dexter’s hand and sliding documents across his desk.
"Marcus," Dexter said. "This is Dexter. Dexter Ashford. The man you just sold a house to in Edge District 3.
A pause on the line.

"I’m having a problem," Dexter continued, keeping his voice level. "There’s another man standing in front of me right now. He claims to be the owner of the house. He says he bought it last month from a different agency."
Silence on the line.
Then Marcus laughed.
It was not the professional, warm laugh Dexter had heard in the office. This was different. It was cold and sinister. The laugh of a man who had been waiting for this moment and found it amusing.

"Oh!" Marcus said, his voice bright with genuine delight. "You actually met the owner! That’s quite fortunate. I was thinking of stringing you along for two or three months. Collecting a few more payments. Maybe two or three million more before you realized."
Dexter’s blood went cold.
"What do you mean by that?"
Marcus’s tone shifted. The warmth vanished entirely. What replaced it was the casual, unconcerned voice of a man who had done this before and knew there would be no consequences.
"What can I say? It has nothing to do with me. It has everything to do with your family."
He paused.
"Courtesy of the Ashford family."
The words landed like a hammer blow.

"No home agency in their right mind would ever sell you a home," Marcus continued, his voice carrying the smug confidence of someone who knew they were untouchable. "Everybody knows the Ashford family controls this city. And they’ve spoken. If you need a home, we can simply take your money and sell you a fake one."
Dexter’s grip on the phone tightened. His knuckles went white.
"Aren’t you scared of the authorities?" Dexter asked. His voice was quiet. Controlled. But something beneath it was beginning to fracture.
Marcus laughed again. Longer this time. More genuine.

"The authorities? Are you truly that ignorant? The Ashford family controls over half the authorities in this city. The only thing they don’t control is the Hero Association. And the Hero Association will never involve itself in personal matters. Especially family feuds."
His voice dropped, becoming almost conversational.
"So there is nothing you can do."

chapters.title: Chapter 193 | Choose One...
paragraphs: "There’s nothing you can do!"
There was a beat of silence before he spoke again.
"If that is all, I’m pretty sure the Ashford family will be very impressed with what I’ve done. I’ll gain a few favors from them. So I’ve got to say..."
He paused.
"Thank you very much for this."
He suddenly chuckled which grew into a mocking laughter as he need the call.
"Ding!" "Ding!" "Ding!"
Dexter stood in the street, phone pressed against his ear, listening to the dead tone of a disconnected call.
The man, the real owner, stood a few meters away. He had heard everything. His face changed sligrhtk as he looked at Dexter with uncomfortable pity.
He looked at Dexter the way people look at stray dogs in the rain.
Dexter lowered the phone.
He looked at the key in his hand expressionlessly.
One million Dollars.
His hard-earned money, money he had earned through sweat and labor and the systematic suppression of his own abilities. Money that was supposed to buy his family a home was now gone and stolen.
By a man who had done it on the Ashford family’s orders.
Dexter’s face was scarily blank.
He turned to the man and held out the key.
"I’m sorry for the inconvenience," he said in a mechanical tone.
The man took the key but didn’t say anything.
Dexter ignored the man and climbed into the SUV, started the engine and pulled away from the curb.
The Harvest Homes building looked the same as it had two hours ago. The cascading plants. The prismatic glass. The marble archway. The water features with their lazy koi.
Dexter didn’t see any of it.
He parked the SUV in the garage, killed the engine, and walked toward the building.
He entered the lobby.
The blonde receptionist looked up as he passed.
"Sir! Sir, who would you like to meet?"
Dexter ignored her.
He walked straight past the reception desk, past the waiting area, past the art displays and the living walls, and pressed the elevator call button.
"Sir, you can’t just go up without an appointment!"
The elevator doors opened. Dexter stepped inside. Pressed 24. The doors closed.
The elevator rose.
The doors opened.
Two men stood in the hallway.

They were large. Both taller than Dexter by several inches. Both wider. Both carrying the unmistakable physical density of peak Superhuman Realm cultivators. They wore dark suits that had been tailored to accommodate bodies built like refrigerators.
Their arms were folded across their chests. Their expressions were professionally neutral.

Marcus had called ahead. Of course he had. He knew Dexter would come back. One million Dollars was not a small sum, especially not to a man who had nothing. Marcus had expected this. Had prepared for it.
The first bodyguard spoke in a very deep tone.
"Mr. Dexter. Please turn around and leave. You have no business here. Go home before you embarrass yourself."
Dexter looked at them.
Then he smiled.

It was not a warm smile. It was not a friendly smile. It was the smile of a man who had spent the last hour compressing an overwhelming amount of rage into a space approximately the size of a fist, and was now feeling the quiet, focused clarity that came on the other side of that compression.
"Okay," Dexter said.
Then he activated Flame Burst Step.
The air ignited beneath his feet. A concussive bang echoed through the hallway as his speed multiplied fivefold. The world blurred as the marble floor cracked beneath the force of his launch.
He appeared in front of the first bodyguard before the man’s brain had finished processing the word "okay."
His open palm struck the bodyguard’s chest.
"BOOM!"

The impact was devastating. A shockwave exploded outward from the point of contact, shattering the overhead light fixtures and sending cracks spider-webbing across the marble floor. The bodyguard’s feet left the ground entirely. His massive frame became a projectile, hurtling backward through the hallway until he collided with the wall.
CRACK!

A human-shaped dent appeared in the reinforced concrete. The bodyguard slid downward, groaning, his suit torn, his chest caved inward by a palm strike that carried the full force of a Tenth Stage Superhuman with an Ancient Grade Flame Demon Bloodline.
The second bodyguard reacted faster.
His eyes widened and his body shifted into a combat stance as he threw a punch aimed directly at Dexter’s jaw, his fist cutting through the air with the insane speed and poer.
However, Dexter didn’t dodge and simply smirked coldly as he punched back.
Fist met fist.
"BOOM!"
The shockwave was enormous as the entire hallway walls shuddered, the ceiling panels rattled and a decorative vase on a nearby table shattered.
Even the air itself seemed to compress and rebound, sending a visible ripple of force radiating outward in all directions.
Neither combatant moved a single inch. The bodyguard’s eyes went wide, clearly stunned.

He was a peak Superhuman and had trained for years, fought monsters, criminals, and villains. He had never, in his entire career, met someone at a lower cultivation realm who could match his raw physical strength.
But this man had just stopped his full-power punch with an equal punch of his own eithout even changing expression.
The bodyguard was strong but Dexter’s body wasn’t made of foam either. One might even say he was stronger than him.
Before the bodyguard could recover from his shock, Dexter activated Flame Burst Step again.
He vanished.
The bodyguard roared as he activated his Talent.
His entire body turned silver, his muscles densified and his bones reinforced as he became a living statue of refined metal.
Dexter reappeared behind him. His fist drove into the bodyguard’s back.
"BANG!"
It was like punching a steel wall. The silver technique absorbed the kinetic energy, dispersing it across the bodyguard’s entire frame. The man barely staggered.
But Dexter wasn’t finished.
He smirked.
Blue lightning exploded from his knuckles.
The Thunder Manipulation talent, extracted from the dead assassin on the highway, activated at maximum output.

Crackling arcs of electricity poured from Dexter’s hand into the bodyguard’s body, bypassing the metallic defense entirely. Electricity didn’t care about physical hardness. It cared about conductivity. And the bodyguard’s silver-coated body was essentially one giant conductor.
The bodyguard screamed.

His entire body seized, his muscles locked as the silver talent covering his entire body flickered as his skin turned brown and then silver and eventually, it died as the electrical current overwhelmed his nervous system.
His eyes instantly rolled back and his jaw clenched unconsciously so hard that blood appeared at the corner of his lips as he collapsed to the ground.
"Thud!"
His bidy twitched involuntarily as residual electricity arced across his skin.
Dexter didn’t care and simply stepped over him.
He walked to Marcus’s office door, grabbed the handle and turned it.
