His hard-earned money, money he had earned through sweat and labor and the systematic suppression of his own abilities.
Money that was supposed to buy his family a home was now gone and stolen.
By a man who had done it on the Ashford family’s orders.
Dexter’s face was scarily blank.
He turned to the man and held out the key.
"I’m sorry for the inconvenience," he said in a mechanical tone.
The man took the key but didn’t say anything.
Dexter ignored the man and climbed into the SUV, started the engine and pulled away from the curb.
The Harvest Homes building looked the same as it had two hours ago.
The cascading plants.
The prismatic glass.
The marble archway.
The water features with their lazy koi.
Dexter didn’t see any of it.
He parked the SUV in the garage, killed the engine, and walked toward the building.
He entered the lobby.
The blonde receptionist looked up as he passed.
"Sir!
Sir, who would you like to meet?"
Dexter ignored her.
He walked straight past the reception desk, past the waiting area, past the art displays and the living walls, and pressed the elevator call button.
"Sir, you can’t just go up without an appointment!"
The elevator doors opened.
Dexter stepped inside.
Pressed 24.
The doors closed.
The elevator rose.
The doors opened.
Two men stood in the hallway.
They were large.
Both taller than Dexter by several inches.
Both wider.
Both carrying the unmistakable physical density of peak Superhuman Realm cultivators.
They wore dark suits that had been tailored to accommodate bodies built like refrigerators.
Their arms were folded across their chests.
Their expressions were professionally neutral.
Marcus had called ahead.
Of course he had.
He knew Dexter would come back.
One million Dollars was not a small sum, especially not to a man who had nothing.
Marcus had expected this.
Had prepared for it.
The first bodyguard spoke in a very deep tone.
"Mr.
Dexter.
Please turn around and leave.
You have no business here.
Go home before you embarrass yourself."
Dexter looked at them.
Then he smiled.
It was not a warm smile.
It was not a friendly smile.

It was the smile of a man who had spent the last hour compressing an overwhelming amount of rage into a space approximately the size of a fist, and was now feeling the quiet, focused clarity that came on the other side of that compression.
"Okay," Dexter said.
Then he activated Flame Burst Step.
The air ignited beneath his feet.
A concussive bang echoed through the hallway as his speed multiplied fivefold.
The world blurred as the marble floor cracked beneath the force of his launch.
He appeared in front of the first bodyguard before the man’s brain had finished processing the word "okay."
His open palm struck the bodyguard’s chest.
"BOOM!"
The impact was devastating.
A shockwave exploded outward from the point of contact, shattering the overhead light fixtures and sending cracks spider-webbing across the marble floor.
The bodyguard’s feet left the ground entirely.
His massive frame became a projectile, hurtling backward through the hallway until he collided with the wall.
CRACK!
A human-shaped dent appeared in the reinforced concrete.
The bodyguard slid downward, groaning, his suit torn, his chest caved inward by a palm strike that carried the full force of a Tenth Stage Superhuman with an Ancient Grade Flame Demon Bloodline.
The second bodyguard reacted faster.
His eyes widened and his body shifted into a combat stance as he threw a punch aimed directly at Dexter’s jaw, his fist cutting through the air with the insane speed and poer.
However, Dexter didn’t dodge and simply smirked coldly as he punched back.
Fist met fist.
"BOOM!"
The shockwave was enormous as the entire hallway walls shuddered, the ceiling panels rattled and a decorative vase on a nearby table shattered.
Even the air itself seemed to compress and rebound, sending a visible ripple of force radiating outward in all directions.
Neither combatant moved a single inch.
The bodyguard’s eyes went wide, clearly stunned.
He was a peak Superhuman and had trained for years, fought monsters, criminals, and villains.
He had never, in his entire career, met someone at a lower cultivation realm who could match his raw physical strength.
But this man had just stopped his full-power punch with an equal punch of his own eithout even changing expression.
The bodyguard was strong but Dexter’s body wasn’t made of foam either.
One might even say he was stronger than him.
Before the bodyguard could recover from his shock, Dexter activated Flame Burst Step again.
He vanished.
The bodyguard roared as he activated his Talent.
His entire body turned silver, his muscles densified and his bones reinforced as he became a living statue of refined metal.
Dexter reappeared behind him.
His fist drove into the bodyguard’s back.
"BANG!"
It was like punching a steel wall.
The silver technique absorbed the kinetic energy, dispersing it across the bodyguard’s entire frame.
The man barely staggered.
But Dexter wasn’t finished.
He smirked.
Blue lightning exploded from his knuckles.
The Thunder Manipulation talent, extracted from the dead assassin on the highway, activated at maximum output.
Crackling arcs of electricity poured from Dexter’s hand into the bodyguard’s body, bypassing the metallic defense entirely.
Electricity didn’t care about physical hardness.
It cared about conductivity.
And the bodyguard’s silver-coated body was essentially one giant conductor.
The bodyguard screamed.

His entire body seized, his muscles locked as the silver talent covering his entire body flickered as his skin turned brown and then silver and eventually, it died as the electrical current overwhelmed his nervous system.
His eyes instantly rolled back and his jaw clenched unconsciously so hard that blood appeared at the corner of his lips as he collapsed to the ground.
"Thud!"
His bidy twitched involuntarily as residual electricity arced across his skin.
Dexter didn’t care and simply stepped over him.
He walked to Marcus’s office door, grabbed the handle and turned it.

chapters.title: Chapter 194 | Anger (1)
paragraphs: The door swung open and Marcus could be seen seated in his seat, right behind the desk.
There were lots of documents on his desk as he wrote something down with a self-satisfied smile on his round, ruddy face.
As the door opened, Marcus didn’t bother to look up.
"Is it done?" he asked casually, his pen still moving. "Have you chased the bastard away?"
There was a bit of silence and then a voice spoke.
"Yes. It is done."
Marcus still didn’t look up as he chuckled and continued writing.
"Good. If that is all, just keep guarding. The bastard might come back again."
There was another silence throughout out the entire room.
Just when Marcus was feeling something was wrong, a fist came down on the iron desk..
"CRACK!"
The metal and glass desk instablt shattered as though made of wood as the entire surface exploded into pieces, splitting apart Instantly.
A massive shockwave of pure physical force ripped through the air as documents were sent flying.
Marcus’s was stunned and he raised his head. At that exact moment, his heart skipped a beat as the Marcus’s his face vanished like an illusion.
Dexter stood on the other side of what used to be a desk. His fist was still pressed into the wreckage and his eyes were cold.
Marcus’s face went pale and the ruddy complexion drained to a sickly grey in approximately one second. His mouth opened. No sound came out.
Dexter reached across the wreckage of the desk, grabbed Marcus by the throat, and lifted him out of his chair.
Marcus weighed over a hundred kilograms. Dexter lifted him with one hand as though he were a bag of feathers.
The man’s feet dangled in the air. His hands clawed at Dexter’s grip. His face turned from grey to red to purple as the pressure on his throat cut off blood flow and air simultaneously.
Dexter held him there. At eye level. Close enough that Marcus could see every detail of Dexter’s face. Close enough to see that there was no bluff in his eyes. No negotiation. No room for talk.
Dexter smiled.
"Either you give me my money," he said, his voice light, almost pleasant, "or you die. Choose one."

Marcus’s eyes bulged. Sweat poured down his forehead, running into his eyes and mixing with the tears that had begun to leak from the corners. His lips moved, producing choked, wheezing sounds that couldn’t quite form words.
"Wait," he managed, the word barely audible through his crushed throat. "Wait, wait, wait. I’ll send you your money. I’ll send it right now. Don’t do anything rash. Don’t do anything rash."
He gasped, his face contorting with desperate urgency.

"But the money is with the company. It’s not with me. I’m just a messenger. I’m just a messenger for the higher-ups. I had nothing to do with the decision. I’m just a messenger. I just did what I was told."
Dexter’s smile didn’t waver.

"Didn’t you say you wanted to curry favor with the Ashford family?" he asked, tilting his head slightly. "You wanted to impress them. Gain a few favors. And you’ve got Type One, Type Two, and Type Three relic weapons hanging on your wall."
He glanced at the three swords on their display plaques, still rattling from the shockwave that had destroyed the desk.
"So I’m sure you can afford one million credits. Transfer my money. Right now. This instant."
Marcus’s face turned even paler. The blue tint receded slightly as Dexter loosened his grip just enough to allow speech, but the terror in the man’s eyes only deepened.
He gritted his teeth. A flash of defiance, born from desperation rather than courage, crossed his features.
"You have no idea who you’re dealing with," he hissed.
Dexter smiled wider.
"You also have no idea who you’re dealing with."
His grip tightened.

Marcus’s face went from blue to a mottled red. Then green. Then a horrifying combination of both as the pressure on his throat increased. His eyes began to bulge. The veins on his forehead stood out like cables as his kicking became weaker, frantic and pathetic.
Dexter stared into his eyes.
And Marcus saw something there.
It was killing intent.
Pure, cold, absolute killing intent.
Marcus saw it, and he understood that the next five seconds would determine whether he lived or died.
"Pl-ease!" "Waaaait!"
He began to plead. Frantic, garbled sounds spilled from his lips.
But Dexter wasn’t listening anymore.
His eyes had flashed violet and then crimson as killkmgbjnegent began to rise.
Demonic essence surged through his DNA, flooding his muscles, his bones, his nervous system with power that was not entirely human.
The Asura Physique also stirred, wanting souls.
The two combined want enough to fully influence Dexter but it was enough for them to give him an idea which grew rapidly.
’Kill him.’
’Kill him and forget about the money. He insulted you, he stole from you and he deserves death. Take it.’
Dexter’s violet eyes narrowed and his grip on Marcus’s throat shifted, no longer a restraining hold but was tightening.
Marcus eyes went wide with terror and he opened his mouth to scream but he could not.
Dexter’s other hand began to rise, crimson flames flickering around his knuckles.
"You can only blame me for what is about tot happen."
Dexter grinned as he tightened his hand and was ready for the kill when his Enhanced Hearing Talent suddenly heard something behind him.
The thing was fast to an almost impossible level as it closed in on him with speed that rivaled sound.

Dexter’s eyes snapped back to their natural color for a fraction of a second and his conscious mind, the part that was still Dexter Ashford and not the Flame Demon ascending through his bloodline, processed the information speed.
But as Dexter’s brain processed all this, he didn’t dodge in the slightest.
It wasn’t that he didn’t have time to dodge, it was that he chose especially at that moment not to dodge!

chapters.title: Chapter 195 | Anger (2)
paragraphs: Dexter didn’t dodge. Instead, he left his back vulnerable as the attack swooshed towards him.
At that moment, the black stud earring suddenly exploded outward from Dexter’s body, expanding to cover both him and Marcus in a transparent, dome-shaped barrier.
At that split second, a silver arc of sword energy collided with the barrier with a cataclysmic force.
"DING!"
A massive shockwave exploded out in an astonishing burst.
The entire office shook violently as glass shattered and every window in the room exploded!
Even the walls cracked and the ceiling panels also shattered to smithereens!
"Crack!"
The barrier had mutiple cracks on it but it actually didn’t explode.
Dexter slowly turned around.

Marcus still dangled from his left hand, choking and gasping and crying, barely able to speak but Dexter barely noticed as his entire attention was focused on the figure standing in the doorway of the office.
The person was a middle-aged who looked his fifties it maybe even older.
It was difficult to tell because his face carried the particular agelessness of a high-level her.
His hair was pure white, cropped short and swept back from a forehead. There was also a matching white beard covered his jaw which was trimmed neatly.
The man wore an expensive blue suit that proved he had money but the most astonishing part was that in his left hand was a long silver sword.
The man’s brow was furrowed slightly as his eyes stared at Dexter.
Dexter’s face turned serious as his gaze landed on him.
’Ultra Realm.’

He immediately knew the cultivation level of the man. The attack he had launched had been reduced to Peak Superhuman levels, thinking it was enough to deal with Dexter which was why he used the strength of a peak realm Super Human.
However, he had been very wrong. Nit only had Dexter survived, he had survived with indifference!
Dexter turned around and stared at the man with an expressionless gaze and then suddenly smirked.
"You truly want him to die, don’t you?"
The middle-aged man didn’t say anything as he moved his gaze from Dexter to Marcus, ehi was still dangling and choking from Dexter’s grip.
After a while, he suddenly spoke.
"You do know, i possess the power to make you stay here forever if I wish."
His said in a casual tone as thought he wasn’t bothered that his employee was on the verge of death.
"Even if I give you the one million back or even 100 million, I can make sure you never leave this building."
Dexter blinked at the man’s voice but then suddenly, he chuckled drily.
"You can try,
Then he tilted his head, his violet-tinged eyes meeting the old man’s dark gaze.
"But what do you think killing an Ashford son would do to your company? Most especially you..."
Dexter’s grin widened as he said this.
Dexter Ashford was, by legal definition, the firstborn son of the Ashford family. Disowned or not, cast out or not.
He still bore the Ashford name.
Killing him would would definitely benefit the Ashford family but the Ashford family would definitely not let it down especially not in public.
The company would definitely die and so would he, like literally!
If it became known that a real estate company had murdered an Ashford son, even a disowned one, the political fallout would be significant.
The delicate web of business relationships that Harvest Homes depended on would be damaged.
The old man stared at Dexter for a long time.
Silence filled the ruined office.
"What do you want?" the old man asked.
Dexter chuckled.
"I want my two million credits back." He paused. "With interest."
He raised Marcus slightly, adjusting his grip.
Marcus’s eyes went wide. He tried to speak to explain that it wasn’t two million credits personally. But Dexter’s grip tightened, crushing the words back down his throat before they could form.
The old man glanced at Marcus. Then at Dexter.
Then he chuckled.
"Even if I give you the two million," the old man said, "do you think you would leave here intact?"
He paused, letting the question settle.
"Although I might not be able to kill you, the Ashford family won’t blame me if I cripple you. Disownment works both ways, boy. They discarded you. That means you have no protection."
His dark eyes narrowed.
"Crippled and useless wives, crippled husband. Isn’t that fitting?"
He smiled. It was not a kind smile.
"A few people were quite jealous that you managed to snag three beauties. However, they are crippled and they are stupid. And now you will be crippled and useless along with them."
He tilted his head.
"I know what the headlines will say tomorrow.
Dexter was silent.
His face turned blank and expressionless.
’Useless.’
’Crippled.’
’Stupid.’
’My wives.’
"Bang!"
Something broke inside him.
Something even Dexter didn’t understand.
The old man had insulted him. That was fine. Dexter had been insulted his entire life, a bastard and even a slave with an f rank talent.
He had heard every variation, every iteration, every creative combination of contempt that the human vocabulary could produce and he was alredy quite used to it.
But the old man had not stopped at insulting him, he had insulted his wives.
Mira who had sworn a Death God oath to honor any request Dexter made, Selene who had fallen asleep on his chest because she needed heat and Lyra who had kissed his cheek because he gave her chips.
’Useless.’
’Crippled.’
’Mute.’
’Blind.’
The words echoed in his mind, bouncing off the walls of his consciousness, growing louder and louder as time passed.
Dexter’s eyes changed drastically.
One moment they were their natural dark brown. The next moment, they were violet.
A strange pressure began to radiate from his body as the temperature in the office rose rapidly
Even the air shimmered as the dust motes suspended in the air began to glow faintly by the heat that was pouring from Dexter’s skin.
The old man’s expression changed.
"What are you..."
Dexter’s lips curled into a cold smile.
"Flame Demon Transformation!"

chapters.title: Chapter 196 | Enough!
paragraphs: "Flame Demon Transformation."
"BOOM!!!"
An enormous pillar of crimson flame erupted from Dexter’s body.
The flames surged upward, punching through the ceiling of the office, up into the office above.
Then the flames collapsed inward.
They wrapped around Dexter’s body, compressing, molding themselves to his form.
His hair lifted, floating upward as though suspended in zero gravity as they literally lit up with white, gold and violet flames.
The flames compressed in Dexter’s body as it formed demonic tattoos on his skin!
The visual manifestation of a bloodline that was older and more powerful than anything the old man had ever encountered.
His eyes burned with violent flames as the entire office trembled and shook from the raw power and sheer heat that Dexter was radiating T that moment.
The old man’s expression changed as he became serious.
He hadn’t expected this trouble maker who everyone knew has been useless to possess this sort of strength.
"So you’ve been hiding your strength," he murmured.
Dexter didn’t answer but released his grip on Marcus.
The man dropped to the floor like a sack of wet sand.
"K-off!" "Koff!!"
He gasped, coughed, and tried to crawl away on his hands and knees.
Dexter didn’t look at him.
His burning gaze remained fixed on the old man.
Dexter lifted his leg up and stepped forward but as his feet landed on the ground—
"BOOM!"
The floor beneath his foot exploded. A spiderweb of fractures spread outward from the point of impact, reaching the walls in every direction.
The old man’s pupils contracted.
’That physical strength...’
Dexter smiled wider. The violet flames in his eyes flickered.
"You said something interesting earlier," Dexter voice was thick and different. It sounded as though two of him was talking at the same time and not just one.
He took another step.
"BOOM!"
"You said crippling me would be fitting."
Another step.
"BOOM!
"You also said my wives are useless."
The demonic patterns on his skin pulsed with light, darkening and spreading as the bloodline’s influence deepened.
"You called them crippled."
The old man’s expression hardened. He raised his sword, the blade humming with gathered mana.
"Don’t think that transformation is enough to..."
"WHOOSH!"
Dexter vanished.
The air where he had been standing exploded outward in a shockwave of displaced atmosphere and superheated air.
The old man’s eyes widened.
’Fast!’
He swung his sword on pure instinct. A full-speed horizontal slash that drew a silver arc through the air with the speed of a lightning bolt.
"CLANG!!!"
Dexter’s fist collided with the edge of the blade.
As the shockwave tore through the office. What remained of the furniture was destroyed as the office cracked even more.
The old man’s arm trembled and he actually slid three meters backward as his feet carved trenches on the ground before he finally stopped.
His arm was trembled as the. The impact traveled from his sword to his entire body.
But Dexter hadn’t moved a single inche backward.
The old man’s expression changed.
’Impossible.’
’He’s not at the Ultra Realm. His cultivation is Superhuman. Tenth Stage at most. But his physical strength...’
’His physical strength is matching mine.’
’No. Exceeding mine.’
Dexter slowly raised his head. His violet eyes locked onto the old man’s dark gaze.
"One thing you said was correct."

The heat around him intensified and the temperature in the room climbed past the point where ordinary materials could survive. The carpet smoldered. The remaining furniture began to char and even the air itself seemed to ignite.
"My wives are crippled."
The old man’s lip curled. He opened his mouth to speak.
Dexter’s voice cut through the air like a blade.
"But they are still my wives."
The violet light in his eyes flared.
"And anyone who dares insult them..."
His fist slowly clenched. The flames around it compressed, densified, concentrated into a point of light so intense it was painful to look at.
"...will pay the price.
"BOOM!!!"
Dexter vanished again.
A crater appeared in the ground, surrounded by a ring of superheated debris that was already melting from the residual thermal energy.
The old man reacted on pure instinct. He raised his sword, channeled every ounce of his Ultra-Rank mana into the blade, and braced.
"BANG!!!"
Dexter’s fist smashed against the blade.
A massive shockwave exploded through the entire room.
The collision unleashed a shockwave not like a wave but a solid, visible wall of compressed air and mana. This sphere-shaped wall expanded outward, simultaneously hitting every surface in the office.

Windows shattered throughout this office and every other one on the floor. The hallway walls cracked and ceiling panels across the entire twenty-fourth floor disintegrated. Everything not bolted down - desks chairs computers filing cabinets - became projectiles.
The old man’s was blasted backwards as he slammed against the office wall!
His sword arm screamed with pain and the blade in his hand developed a visible fracture line.
He was barely able to land on his feet as he stared at Dexter with wide eyes.
Shock.
He looked at the man standing in front of him and he realized something.
The Ashford family was wrong. There was no way a useless person could climb realms to battle!
They were clearly lying to everyone again!
He had barely thoug he this when another fist flashed through the air.
He immediately tried to block it but he was too late.
"Bang!"
The fist struck the side of his mouth and he was sent flying with a black mark on his face.
He collided again with the wall, creating a dent in the wall as gravity let him down.
The old man touched his lips and saw blood on his palm.
His face changed as he looked down at his trembling sword arm.
Then he looked up at Dexter as his gaze turned cold.
"Enough," he said.
As he said this, his body exploded instantly exploded with energy as he activated his own talent.
His body began to change as he also transformed.
The custom-fitted suit that had cost more than most people’s monthly rent ripped like tissue paper as his body expanded.
The white dress shirt beneath it followed. Then the undershirt. Then the skin itself seemed to shift, stretching, thickening, densifying.

chapters.title: Chapter 197 | Attack!
paragraphs: The middle aged man’s body expanded outward in every direction simultaneously.

His shoulders broadened until they were wider than the doorway behind him. His chest deepened until it was deeper than Dexter’s entire torso. His arms thickened, the muscles swelling to proportions that no human skeleton should have been able to support, each one larger than Dexter’s waist.
Four meters.
The old man had been slightly under two meters tall. Now he was four. His head nearly touched the cracked ceiling of the ruined office.
His face had changed too. The aristocratic features, the neat white beard, all of it was gone
His jaw had extended, his brow had thickened and his teeth, visible behind lips that no longer closed properly, had become pronounced.
He looked down at Dexter.
Licked his lips.
His dark eyes burned with a violent, predatory hunger.
He chuckled.
"Do you think you’re the only one hiding your strength?"
Dexter’s violet eyes narrowed.

The transformed man’s power had exploded upward. Stage Two Ultra Realm had been his baseline. The transformation had pushed him past Stage Three. Past Stage Three’s peak. All the way to Stage Four Ultra Realm.

Stage Four Ultra Realm meant an additional two hundred attribute points across every stat compared to a Stage Two. Strength. Agility. Physique. Mana. All of them had surged far beyond anything Dexter’s Tenth Stage Superhuman cultivation could match through raw numbers alone.
Dexter’s gaze turned serious.
But he didn’t care.
He activated Flame Burst Step.
The air ignited.m as he vanished. A crater appeared in the floor where he had been standing, the marble vaporized by the force of his launch.
He materialized directly beside the transformed man.
He punched out once more.
Amplified by Scorching Fury, powered by every ounce of physical strength his Ancient Flame Demon Bloodline and Extreme Slaughtering Demon Body could produce.
The man reacted as he also punched out with his massive trunk-sized fist that moved with a speed that should have been impossible for something that large.
"BOOM!"
Their fists collided.
The shockwave was unlike anything the building had experienced so far. It didn’t just shatter windows or crack walls. It tore through the office like a bomb detonating.
The floor between them disintegrated. The ceiling above them collapsed inward, raining concrete and rebar. The entire corner of the twenty-fourth floor opened to the sky.
The transformed man turned his head slowly toward the point of impact to Dexter.
His massive lips curled.
"As expected," he rumbled. "You’re quite weak now, aren’t you?"
Dexter said nothing but his arm trembled slightly.
But Dexter didn’t retreat.
He flipped his right hand.
The Void Star Saber materialized in his grip. The blade was dark.
The transformed man’s eyes tracked the weapon.
Then he vanished.
Dexter’s Enhanced Hearing screamed.
’Above!’
He swung upward. A desperate, full-power vertical slash that channeled every passive effect the Void Star Saber possessed.
DING!
The collision was sharp. Piercing. The sound of two relic-grade weapons meeting at maximum speed. A point of light appeared at the contact point, so bright it burned afterimages into the retina.

The transformed man had appeared directly above Dexter. Descending. His massive body casting a shadow that blocked the sunlight streaming through the destroyed ceiling. His sword, the same silver blade he had been carrying before the transformation but now enlarged to match his four-meter frame, was aimed straight down. A killing strike. Intended to split Dexter from crown to groin.
The Void Star Saber caught it.

The force of the impact drove Dexter downward. His feet punched through the marble floor. Then through the concrete beneath. He sank to his ankles, his knees absorbing the impact, his entire body compressing under the weight of a four-meter Ultra-Rank combatant bearing down from above.

The ground beneath him exploded. Cracked. Shattered. A crater formed, spreading outward, the floor giving way under the combined pressure of two fighters who had long since exceeded the structural capacity of the building.
Dexter didn’t care.
He countered.
His blade twisted, deflecting the massive sword to the side. He stepped forward, out of the crater, and slashed. A horizontal cut aimed at the transformed man’s midsection.
DING!
The man’s sword came down, blocking.
Dexter reversed the blade and slashed again.
DING!
It was once again blocked m.
Another slash!
DING!

Dexter pressed forward. His blade became a blur. Slash after slash after slash, each one flowing into the next without pause, without hesitation, without the briefest fraction of a second’s recovery between strikes.
The Void Star Saber’s Star Velocity passive increased his attack speed by thirty percent.
The Void Edge doubled his attack power. Armor Break ignored twenty percent of the man’s physical defense.
DING! DING! DING! DING! DING!
The collisions came so fast they merged into a continuous scream of metal against metal.
Sparks flew in every direction as white-hot fragments of displaced mana ignited the air, creating brief, violent flares of light that strobed across the ruined office like lightning.
The transformed man matched his every strik, deflecting each of Dexter’s strikes with accuracy.
The office was being destroyed around them.

The room was being dismantled. The walls were gone. The ceiling was gone. The floor was a landscape of craters and cracks. What had once been a corner office on the twenty-fourth floor of a luxury building was now an open-air platform, exposed to the sky and the wind and the distant sounds of the city below.
Marcus had been crawling toward the corner when the first shockwave hit.

He was no longer crawling on the ground but was flattened, pressed down against the floor by the combined atmospheric pressure of two fighters exchanging blows at a rate that turned the air itself into a weapon.
Marcus pressed his face against the floor, covered his head with his hands, and prayed to every deity he had ever heard of.
He was not a fighter and was just a businessman. He had never even been in a real fight in his life.

chapters.title: Chapter 198 | Ultimate Attacks
paragraphs: "BANG!"
Shockwave exploded out as the two fighters separated, each launching backward to opposite ends of what remained of the office.
Dexter’s feet dug trenches in the cracked marble as he slid to a stop near the destroyed doorway.
The transformed middle-aged man landed on the far side, his massive four-meter frame cracking the floor beneath his weight
The office was mostly gone. The walls destroyed, revealing the entire office to the outside world.
The ground had several holes in them too
The middle aged man’s expression was grim as he stared down at Dexter.
"I must admit," His voice rumbling like distant thunder. "You are quite strong."

"But I’ve been fighting way before your mother was even born," the man continued. His dark eyes narrowed. His grip on his enlarged silver sword shifted, the blade angling upward. "Now, let me show you the power of a true Ultra Realm expert."
The moment he raised his sword the air immediately changed drastically.
The turbulent mana surging like a violent river from their battle suddenly inverted and began to spiral toward the raised blade like vacuum.
In that split second, darkness descended like nightfall.
The darkness swallowed every single light in ten surrounding as everything seem to vanish.
Dexter’s eyes narrowed as he watched the strange darkness consume the office.
"Crimson Moon Slash."
As his voice landed, the darkness pulsed as something illuminated directly behind him!
The light surged and formed a crescent moon directly behind the man.
The crescent moon was large, about three meters tall as it cascaded crimson blood like rays of light to the enter office.
Suddenly, the man smirked as he slashed directly at Dexter.
In that split second, the crimson moon obeyed.
It suddenly moved as it slashed down at Dexter, spinning rapidly as it flew.
"Whoosh!
The air screamed in its wake as a massive pressure surged directly at Dexter.
Dexter’s face turned grim.
The power behind this attack was on a completely different level from anything the man had demonstrated before.
Dexter raised his saber.
"Don’t think you’re the only one with a technique," he muttered through gritted teeth.
He activated the first form of the Thunder God Saber Art.
God Slayer Flash.
Thunder crackled around Dexter’s body. Blue-white arcs of electricity exploded from his skin, dancing along his arms, his shoulders, his neck.
His hair lifted, standing on end, each strand crackling with electrical charge.
But that wasn’t all.
Dexter simultaneously activated his bloodline skill. Flame Slash.
Violet flames erupted from his blade, merging with the blue lightning.
Fire and lightning. Two of the most volatile, incompatible elemental forces in existence, brought together on the edge of a single weapon.
Previously, this combination wouldn’t have been possible. Thunder and flame repelled each other and attempting to merge them would have resulted in a violent reaction.
Before his flame evolved to become an heavenly flame!

The Void Star Saber erupted with a blinding cascade of crimson and blue. Fire and lightning wrapped around each other in a double helix of destructive energy, climbing the blade in spiraling tendrils that reached upward and outward, painting the darkness with streaks of violent color.
Dexter took a single step forward as he slashed out.
The two attacks collided and everywhere went silent for a moment.
"KA-BOOOOOOOOM!!!"

What happened was an event. A moment where the fabric of reality bent, warped, and briefly tore. The collision point between the crimson moon and the flame-thunder slash became a singularity of compressed energy so dense that the air around it turned to plasma.
Then it released.
BOOOOOOM!!!

A mushroom cloud of mixed energy exploded upward. Crimson and blue and white and black, all swirling together in a towering column that punched through the remains of the ceiling, through the floors above, through the roof of the building, and into the sky. The column rose hundreds of meters, visible from across the city like a beacon.
The shockwave that followed was total.
The next, every molecule of air in a fifty-meter radius was moving outward at supersonic speed.
The remaining walls of the office disintegrated. The concrete and steel and glass reduced to powder in an instant, the particles carried outward by the shockwave like sand in a hurricane.
The floor beneath them gave way entirely, replaced by a jagged hole that extended downward through multiple floors.
Marcus was hit.
The shockwave caught him as he lay flattened against the floor, already barely conscious, already broken from the earlier impacts.

The wall of compressed air struck his body with the force of a freight train. His mouth opened. Blood erupted from his lips in a thick, dark spray. His chest compressed. His ribs cracked. His internal organs shifted violently against each other.
He was a Superhuman Realm cultivator. His body was enhanced. Toughened. Reinforced by years of cultivation. An ordinary human would have been vaporized.
Marcus was merely almost killed.

Blood poured from his ears. His nose. His mouth. His eyes rolled upward, showing white. His body went limp, his mind shutting down to escape the pain. He lost consciousness immediately, his broken body slumping against the debris-covered floor like a discarded puppet.
Dexter was blasted backward.

The shockwave caught him and threw him like a leaf in a hurricane as he tumbled through the air, spinning, crashing through the remains of the office doorway, through the hallway wall, and into the corridor beyond.
He stood there and with The Void Star Saber still gripped in his right hand, its blade dimmed, the flame-thunder combination exhausted. His Flame Demon Possession had faded during the collision.
But he was alive.
The transformed man was instead blasted out of the building.

His massive four-meter frame was launched through the exterior wall, which no longer existed to stop him, and into the open air beyond. He tumbled through the sky, his enormous body rotating end over end, trailing debris and dust.
He fell twenty-four floors.
Glass, concrete fragments, steel rebar, office furniture, and pulverized drywall rained down around him, a cascade of debris that peppered the street below like hail.
He hit the ground.
CRACK!

Fire and lightning wrapped around each other in a double helix of destructive energy, climbing the blade in spiraling tendrils that reached upward and outward, painting the darkness with streaks of violent color.
Dexter took a single step forward as he slashed out.
The two attacks collided and everywhere went silent for a moment.
"KA-BOOOOOOOOM!!!"
What happened was an event.
A moment where the fabric of reality bent, warped, and briefly tore.
The collision point between the crimson moon and the flame-thunder slash became a singularity of compressed energy so dense that the air around it turned to plasma.
Then it released.
BOOOOOOM!!!
A mushroom cloud of mixed energy exploded upward.

Crimson and blue and white and black, all swirling together in a towering column that punched through the remains of the ceiling, through the floors above, through the roof of the building, and into the sky.
The column rose hundreds of meters, visible from across the city like a beacon.
The shockwave that followed was total.
The next, every molecule of air in a fifty-meter radius was moving outward at supersonic speed.
The remaining walls of the office disintegrated.
The concrete and steel and glass reduced to powder in an instant, the particles carried outward by the shockwave like sand in a hurricane.
The floor beneath them gave way entirely, replaced by a jagged hole that extended downward through multiple floors.
Marcus was hit.
The shockwave caught him as he lay flattened against the floor, already barely conscious, already broken from the earlier impacts.
The wall of compressed air struck his body with the force of a freight train.
His mouth opened.
Blood erupted from his lips in a thick, dark spray.
His chest compressed.
His ribs cracked.
His internal organs shifted violently against each other.
He was a Superhuman Realm cultivator.
His body was enhanced.
Toughened.
Reinforced by years of cultivation.
An ordinary human would have been vaporized.
Marcus was merely almost killed.
Blood poured from his ears.
His nose.
His mouth.
His eyes rolled upward, showing white.
His body went limp, his mind shutting down to escape the pain.
He lost consciousness immediately, his broken body slumping against the debris-covered floor like a discarded puppet.
Dexter was blasted backward.

The shockwave caught him and threw him like a leaf in a hurricane as he tumbled through the air, spinning, crashing through the remains of the office doorway, through the hallway wall, and into the corridor beyond.
He stood there and with The Void Star Saber still gripped in his right hand, its blade dimmed, the flame-thunder combination exhausted.
His Flame Demon Possession had faded during the collision.
But he was alive.
The transformed man was instead blasted out of the building.
His massive four-meter frame was launched through the exterior wall, which no longer existed to stop him, and into the open air beyond.
He tumbled through the sky, his enormous body rotating end over end, trailing debris and dust.
He fell twenty-four floors.
Glass, concrete fragments, steel rebar, office furniture, and pulverized drywall rained down around him, a cascade of debris that peppered the street below like hail.
He hit the ground.
CRACK!

chapters.title: Chapter 199 | The Meeting
paragraphs: The asphalt cratered beneath his impact. A shockwave rippled outward from the landing point, shattering the windows of parked cars and sending pedestrians staggering.
The man’s massive frame was driven into the street surface, his body creating a crater roughly two meters deep and five meters across.
He lay there. In the crater. In his four-meter form. His silver sword buried in the rubble beside him.
Then he moved.

He pushed himself up. His massive arms trembled. His transformed body, which had seemed so invincible moments ago, was battered. Bruised. Cracked in places where the shockwave had exceeded even his enhanced durability.
He stood and then Looked up.
At the twenty-fourth floor of the ruined building.
At Dexter.
Who was standing at the edge of the destroyed floor, looking down at him.
People were gathering.

Dozens of them. Pedestrians who had felt the shockwave, heard the explosions, seen the pillar of light, and come running. They stood at the edge of the crater, their phones raised, recording everything. Some were screaming. Some were crying. Most were simply staring with the wide-eyed, uncomprehending shock of ordinary people who had just witnessed something far beyond their understanding.

The transformed man’s massive form was impossible to miss. A four-meter tall, impossibly muscled, white-haired figure standing in a crater in the middle of the street. People immediately recognized him as they saw the power he was Radiating.
And he was looking up at a young man standing in the ruins of the twenty-fourth floor.
Dexter stared down at the old man.
His violet eyes had faded back to their natural brown.
Dexter wanted to go down there, tocontinue the fight. Wanted to finish what the old man had started. Wanted to make him bleed. To make him pay for every word.
But now was not the time.
The street was full of people, cameras were recording and the Hero Association would be responding within minutes.

The police were probably already on their way. Fighting an Ultra Realm expert in front of a crowd of civilians, in the middle of the central district, during broad daylight, would attract exactly the kind of attention he could not afford.
Not today.
Dexter turned away from the edge.
He walked back into the ruins of the office. His eyes scanned the debris. The desk was gone. The bookshelves were gone. The decorative items were shattered beyond recovery.
But Marcus was still there.
The man lay unconscious in a corner of what remained of the office. Blood had pooled beneath him and his breathing was shallow.
Dexter felt no sympathy for him in the slightest.
He walked over to Marcus’s unconscious body and knelt beside it and started to remove the man’s watch. A luxury timepiece. Mana-powered. Probably worth 100,000 dollars.
He removed the gold ring on Marcus’s right hand which seemed to Worth at least a hundred thousand.
He removed the bracelet on Marcus’s left wrist and was about to move when he noticed something in Marcus’s mouth.
A gold tooth.
Dexter reached down, pried Marcus’s jaw open with his thumb, and yanked.
The tooth came free with a faint resistance and a wet sound.
He held it up.
"Gold! Nice!"
Dexter pocketed it anyway.

Then he stood up and walked to the far wall, where the three sword plaques had fallen. The display mounts were broken, but the swords themselves were intact. Type One. Type Two. Type Three. Three relic weapons, undamaged by the battle.
He collected all three.
Seller’s remorse, Marcus?
He placed everything into his spatial storage.
He looked around the ruined office one last time. Scanned for anything else of value. Found nothing that had survived the destruction.
He nodded to himself. Satisfied.
Then he turned and walked out.
The elevator was still functional. Miraculously.
Dexter rode it down to the lobby. The doors opened. He stepped out.

The lobby was full of people. Receptionists behind the desk, security guards near the entrance, visitors who had been evacuated from the upper floors, all of them crowded into the ground floor space, staring upward through the skylights at the smoke and debris rising from the twenty-fourth floor.
Several bodyguards stood near the elevator bank. They were armed. Armored. Their postures were aggressive. Their faces were set with the determination of men who had been ordered to stop someone.
They saw Dexter step out of the elevator.
None of them moved.

They had seen what happened. Or heard about it. The security feeds, the frantic radio communications, the bodyguards who had been stationed on the twenty-fourth floor and had been found unconscious in the hallway. The four-meter transformation of their boss. The pillar of light that had blown through the roof.
And they had seen the old man. Their employer. Their leader. An Ultra Realm expert. Lying in a crater in the middle of the street.
Looking up at a young man who was now walking calmly through the lobby.

None of them were Ultra Realm. Most were Peak Superhuman at best. And they had just witnessed their Ultra Realm boss get thrown out of a building by the casually dressed young man now walking toward them.
They stepped aside.
Dexter walked through the lobby without looking at any of them. His pace was unhurried and his expression was neutral.
He pushed through the glass doors and stepped out into the sunlight.
The pillar of energy had dissipated, leaving only a thin trail of smoke rising from the damaged building.
A crowd had gathered behind police barricades that had been erected as Emergency vehicles were arriving.
And in the center of the crater, the transformed man had reverted to his human form. He was surrounded by emergency responders who were wisely keeping their distance.
He was staring at Dexter.
Their eyes met across the chaos of the street.
The old man’s expression was unreadable.
He was reassessing.
Dexter held his gaze for one second.
Then he turned away, walked to his SUV, opened the door, climbed in, and started the engine.
He pulled out of the parking garage. Merged onto the main road and then instantly drove out.
He was driving when his phone rang.
Dexter glanced at the screen. Cole.
’Damn! I almost forgot.’
He answered.
"Hey, Dexter. I don’t mean to disturb, but I just wanted to make sure you haven’t forgotten about the meeting we set up."
Dexter checked the time on his dashboard display.
He was thirty minutes late.
"I apologize. I got held up by something but I’m on my way."

chapters.title: Chapter 200 | You Don’t Have To Carry It Alone
paragraphs: Three years before the present.
The rooftop of the old Ashford servants’ quarters was a flat, tar-papered surface cluttered with ventilation ducts, rusted water tanks, and exposed pipes.
Nobody came up here and the door to the roof was supposed to be locked, but the lock had been broken for years, and nobody had bothered to fix it because nobody cared enough except for Dexter.
He had found this place when he was 12 and it had always been hiding spot.
The one place he could sit and not be seen by the servants and the family members who looked down on him.
He had also always celebrated his birthday here, alone since no one had remembered his birthday.
If wasn’t that he had expected them to anyways.

If he was remembered, he got extra chores instead, had to scrub floors until his knees arched, washed laundry and plates and even eaten leftovers in the corner of the servants’ hall, alone, while the other servants chatted and laughed around him.
He was used to it.
But this particular sunset was quite nice.
The sky above Stargate City was in shades of amber and rose and deep, burning gold. The towers of the central district caught the light and threw it back in blinding flashes.
Dexter sat on the concrete wall, his legs dangling over the edge.
He also wore a faded grey t-shirt that was slightly too large for his body. At this particular day, he was 16. But right now, he didn’t feel 16, but quite tired.
The rooftop door creaked and immediately, Dexter’s head turned.
A girl stepped through.
She was a slim, dark haired beautiful girl who looked 18 to 17.
Her hair was pulled back in a simple ponytail, and she wore a plain white blouse tucked in her dark skirt and carried a small cloth bundle in both hands,
That young woman was Jasmine Constance, the only person in the entire Ashford estate who had ever looked at Dexter and actually smart enough ot lucky enough tot have lived.
Others have died but Jasmine’s hero talent had rendered her invisible, so she couldn’t be seen with Dexter.
It wasn’t that there wasn’t people that cared for Dexter, it was that they hadn’t lived long enough.. they had all died mysteriously!
Dexter suspected it was his father and most likely Step mother Seraphina.

He had met Jasmine a year ago. Dexter had been carrying a stack of clean linens through the east corridor when he had rounded a corner and collided with Jasmine, who had been carrying a stack of documents in the opposite direction.

They had both knelt on the floor, gathering the scattered mess, apologizing simultaneously, and in the process of disentangling their respective stacks, Jasmine had looked up at him and said, "You have really nice eyes."
The comment had so thoroughly short-circuited his brain that he had simply stared at her, stunned for ten full seconds before stammering "thank you" and fleeing down the corridor.

After that, they had kept running into each other. In the corridors. In the kitchen, in the garden. Each encounter was brief, giving each other a smile, greetings, comment about the weather or the food or the latest news from the Hero Association. Small moments that accumulated like snowflakes until they formed something solid between them.
Jasmine found the rooftop three weeks ago. Dexter hadn’t shown it to her. She had followed him.
She hadn’t asked why he hid not asked why he was alon, she had simply sat down beside him on the wall, dangled her legs over the edge, and watched the sunset in comfortable silence.
They had been coming here together ever since.
Jasmine walked the rooftop. She reached the wall, climbed up beside him, and sat.
She didn’t say anything immediately.
She just sat there, shoulder to shoulder with him as they both watched the sunset.
Then she held out the cloth bundle.
"Happy birthday," she said.
Dexter stared at the bundle.
Then at her.
"How did you know?"
Jasmine shrugged with a smile on her lips."That’s for me to know."
She wiggled the bundle slightly. "Open it."
Dexter took the bundle from her hands and he unfolded the cloth carefully.
Inside was a sweater, a clearly secondhand cloth that was worn but clean. The color was warm blue and the stitching was slightly uneven in places, suggesting it had been repaired by hand.
But it was warm, thick and soft against his fingers.
It was the nicest piece of clothing Dexter had ever owned.
His throat tightened.
"You didn’t have to," he said quietly.
"I know," Jasmine replied. "That’s the point."
She bumped her shoulder against his. "Try it on. I want to see if it fits."

Dexter pulled the sweater over his head. The fabric settled onto his shoulders with a soft, warm weight that immediately began to insulate his body heat. It fit. Not perfectly. The sleeves were slightly long, covering his hands to the first knuckle. But the shoulders were right, and the torso was snug without being tight.

He looked down at himself. At the blue fabric covering his arms and chest. At something that was his. Something that had been given to him not because it was owed, not because it was required, but because someone had wanted to.
"It’s perfect," he said.
His voice cracked on the second word.
He looked away quickly, blinking hard, his jaw clenched against the pressure building behind his eyes.
Jasmine didn’t comment on the crack in his voice. She didn’t look at his face. She simply sat beside him, her shoulder pressed against his, and watched the sunset as though nothing had happened.
After a moment, she spoke.
"Do you know what I thought the first time I saw you?"
Dexter shook his head. His eyes were still fixed on the horizon, his jaw still tight.
"I thought, ’That boy looks like he’s carrying the weight of the entire world on his shoulders,’" Jasmine said. "And then I thought, ’He’s carrying it alone.’"
She paused.
"You don’t have to carry it alone, Dexter."
The sunset painted her profile in shades of gold and rose.
